          Vertical, Relentless, Effective: The Tottenham Transformation Under Martin Ho
        
      
                          
                      Sep 23, 2026
          
                      Maya Shah / Author, Jakob Abrahamson / Design
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
Martin Ho has overseen a remarkable turnaround at Tottenham. From an 11th-place finish two seasons ago to one of the WSL's most exciting and progressive teams, and just one of four unbeaten sides this season after three games. How close are Spurs to closing the gap on the division's elite?

Tottenham Hotspur's 7-0 victory over Crystal Palace may have been the performance that turned heads in the Women's Super League this weekend, but the foundations for such a display have been building for some time.

Just over a year ago, Spurs were coming off an 11th-place finish and searching for a new direction. While there had been flashes of progress in earlier seasons, including fifth- and sixth place finishes in 2021-22 and 2023-24 respectively, their slide towards the bottom end of the table in 2024-25 underlined the gap that still existed to the league's leading clubs.
Since Martin Ho's arrival in July 2025, however, that trajectory has changed dramatically.

Tottenham collected a club-record 36 WSL points in Ho's first season in charge, winning 11 matches and returning to fifth place. Indeed, that points tally was the most ever by an English manager in their debut season in the competition.
Since taking the reins, Ho has overseen 13 WSL victories in just 25 matches, with only Manchester City (21), Chelsea (17) and Arsenal (16) winning more games in that period.
And their start to the 2026-27 campaign suggests that progress has continued.
Spurs are one of only four unbeaten teams remaining in the division, and sit second in the table after three matches, just behind Man City.

Tottenham are currently enjoying a six-match unbeaten run in the competition, equalling the longest in the club's WSL history, and the first since such a six-game streak between October-November 2023. The challenge now is sustaining that momentum.
They face the third-toughest fixture run in the division over their next five WSL games according to the Opta Power Rankings, coming up against London City Lionesses, Chelsea and Arsenal.
That makes their start even more intriguing.

Spurs won four of their opening five WSL games last season, before winning just seven of their remaining 17. This time around, Ho will be hoping his side can bridge that gap to the league’s elite, and, crucially, sustain their strong start across the entirety of the campaign.
The meetings with the ‘big four' will provide a significant test, but there is growing evidence that Spurs are closer to that level than they have been before.
Ho's emphasis on brave, front-foot football combined with defensive discipline is already evident in Tottenham's early-season performances, none more so than their 7-0 victory over Crystal Palace.

While the visitors were helped by Palace being reduced to 10 players after just seven minutes, scoring seven goals at WSL level is no simple task. After all, this was a Palace side that had drawn 0-0 against Arsenal at Emirates Stadium just a week earlier despite facing 30 shots.
The manner of Tottenham's dominance was particularly striking. Spurs registered 42 shots, the third-highest total in WSL history, and the most ever recorded by an away side in the competition.

They also amassed 82 touches in the opposition box, the most by Tottenham in a WSL match and the joint fourth-highest total ever recorded in the league. No team had reached that figure since Chelsea managed 82 against Leicester City in December 2024.
On top of that, the game was goalless at the break, with all seven goals coming in a ruthless second half.

There were standout individual performances.Olivia Holdt became just the second Tottenham player to score a WSL hat-trick, after Martha Thomas against Aston Villa in October 2023, while Amanda Nildén‘s late goal perfectly captured the collective nature of Spurs' attacking play.
Nildén's 86th-minute strike came at the end of a 37-second move involving nine different Tottenham players, the most players involved in a single WSL goal this season.

          UEFA Women's Champions League Predictions 2026-27: The Opta Supercomputer Projections
        
      
                          
                      Sep 22, 2026
          
                      Yash Thakur / Author, Jakob Abrahamson / Design
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
Who will win the UEFA Women's Champions League in 2026-27? Will Barcelona retain their crown? Here, we detail how the Opta supercomputer sees this season playing out.
The UEFA Women’s Champions League is back with its 18-team league-phase format for the 2026-27 season, and Matchday 1 kicks off on Tuesday.

Each team will play six games in the league phase, with the top four teams at the end securing direct qualification to the quarter-finals, while the teams ranked 5th to 12th will compete in a knockout play-off to book their place in the last eight.

Barcelona were crowned champions for the fourth time in their history after thrashing OL Lyonnes 4-0 in the final last season. Ewa Pajor and Salma Paralluelo both scored twice in the second half to secure the title.

In a summer of major moves, two-time Ballon d’Or winner Alexia Putellas departed Barcelona for the WSL, while Salma Paralluelo made the switch to Lyon. Arsenal and Lyon have both strengthened their already potent attacks, Real Madrid continue to build around an exciting young core, and Chelsea, Bayern Munich and Manchester City will all be firmly in the hunt for silverware this season.
So, which side has got the Opta supercomputer's backing for European glory?

Barcelona come into another season as the favourites to win the competition and equal their men’s team’s tally of five European titles. The Spanish champions have featured in all the UWCL finals this decade, being crowned champions four times.

Despite losing some long serving members of the squad this summer, Pere Romeu’s side came out winners in 41.2% of the supercomputer's simulations. The Blaugranas are the side to beat in Europe and have lost just three out of 38 games in the UWCL since the start of 2023, with all three losses coming against English sides (1-0 vs Arsenal on 24 May 2025, 2-0 vs Man City on 10 October 2024 and 1-0 vs Chelsea on 20 April 2024).

After losing out to eventual champions Barcelona in the semi-finals of the last edition, Bayern Munich are the second most likely side to win the competition this season with Opta’s supercomputer. José Barcala’s winning machine reached the final in 34.8% of the simulations and were crowned champions in 17.3% of them.

In fact, Bayern’s only two losses in all competitions last season came at the hands of Barcelona (7-1 in October and 4-2 in May). Although Georgia Stanway switched the Bavarians for Arsenal this summer, Barcala should feel confident in their attack of Klara Bühl, Pernille Harder, Edna Imade and others.
Bayern and Barça are set to face each other again in the final match of the league phase this season. Bayern will hope to do better this time.
According to the supercomputer, all English teams and OL Lyonnes are expected to secure a place in the quarter-finals of the UWCL this year, alongside the title contenders of course.

Sonia Bompastor’s Chelsea (94.0%) have been given the second highest chance of reaching the last eight of the competition, behind Barcelona. This is largely down to their favourable draw as the Blues have the lowest average fixture difficulty rating of all teams in the league phase this year.

Surprisingly, the Opta supercomputer is not too bullish on the prospects of eight-time champions and last year’s runners-up OL Lyonnes, or the 2024-25 champions Arsenal. Those two teams came out on top in only 8.7% and 7.0% of the simulations, respectively.Jonatan Giráldez's side reached the final in 20.6% of simulations, behind Barcelona, Bayern Munich, Chelsea and Man City. Despite adding more attacking firepower to the side with the signings of Caroline Weir and Paralluelo, Lyon lack balance in the midfield following Lindsey Heaps’ departure this summer to Denver Summit FC.
The side struggled to maintain the intensity and compactness throughout the 90 minutes in last season’s final against Barcelona and could yet fall short in that regard this season.

Renee Slegers’ Arsenal have had their own issues in front of goal, unable to maximise their goalscoring opportunities, a glimpse of what has continuously haunted the Gunners when it comes to the fine margins.

Their recent goalless draw against Crystal Palace was another in a long list of games where they failed to convert their chances. According to the Opta supercomputer, Arsenal reached the final on just 17.8% of the simulations.

English champions Manchester City reached the semi-final stage in 50.1% of the simulations on their return to the competition. Andree Jeglertz’s side haven’t featured in the final four since the 2017-18 season, when they were beaten by the eventual champions Lyon thanks to a goal by Lucy Bronze.

Spearheaded by Khadija Shaw, City will hope to add a European star to their domestic triumphs, building on their momentum. The side has talented players across all positions but potentially lacks the depth needed to compete three times a week.

Outside the top six, Real Madrid have the highest probability of making the quarter-finals of the UWCL this season (49.6%). Las Blancas have lost their leading goalscorer and assist provider in the club’s history, Caroline Weir, but have brought in the prodigious talent of Felicia Schroder to lead the attack alongside Linda Caicedo.

113zwiiotwzbp1qrrhyk053ne3.title: De Bruyne: I did not try to leave Napoli
113zwiiotwzbp1qrrhyk053ne3.subtitle: Kevin De Bruyne previously seemed to suggest he could leave Napoli, but the Belgian has insisted he did not try to do so this summer.
paragraphs: Kevin De Bruyne has claimed he did not attempt to push through an exit from Napoli in the summer transfer window.
De Bruyne previously suggested he was unhappy at Napoli, and there was speculation linking him with a move away from the Serie A club.
The Manchester City great did not see eye to eye with coach Antonio Conte, who has since been replaced by Massimiliano Allegri.
De Bruyne, however, has now insisted he was not interested in leaving Napoli.
He told reporters: "No, I haven't really spoken to anyone about it.
"I just enjoyed my holidays and went straight back to Naples."
Napoli have made their worst start to a Serie A season in a decade, having taken seven points from their opening five matches.
De Bruyne, though, is not overly concerned.
He said: "We've had a rough start to the season, we've played a lot of strong teams already.
"We even had the chance to win it in the final minute against Inter, but we still lost. Those details are the difference between our seven points and the 10 or 11 we might've deserved.
"We're not doing so well in terms of points, but I think we're doing fine."
Injury restricted De Bruyne to 21 games last term. He scored five goals, assisted four more and created 40 chances.
De Bruyne has made six appearances this season, scoring once and providing one assist.

11saz8tdl2qod1a8ck4tw8mtj9.title: Koge relishing Women's Champions League adventure after Arsenal edge out minnows
11saz8tdl2qod1a8ck4tw8mtj9.subtitle: Arsenal had 19 shots but hit the target just twice as they edged out minnows Koge in their opening Women's Champions League games.
paragraphs: Nadia Nadim says minnows Koge are simply relishing their Women's Champions League adventure following a narrow defeat to Arsenal.
The Gunners, European champions in 2025, clinched a 1-0 win over the Danish team, who are featuring in just their second Champions League campaign.
Mariona Caldentey's last-gasp penalty claimed the points for Arsenal, who were wasteful in front of goal.
Arsenal had 19 shots, but got just two of them on target, while they also hit the woodwork.
While Koge suffered late heartbreak, Nadim, who led the visitors' line, was thrilled with her team-mates.
"So proud of the team and the way we conducted ourselves, especially in the first half," she told ESPN on Disney+.

"We have a young team, a lot of them have no experience playing at this level, good for them to experience what it's like at this level. Good learning, disappointed they got the goal and penalty in the last minute. That's a part of the game, could've done better, but it's our first Champions League game and there's a lot of games left.
"We wanted to be compact and keep the ball, we had people who were comfortable with the ball. We changed in the last 30 minutes, and it didn't do us well because we couldn't get out of the pressure.
"Credit to Arsenal, great team, they find each other well. It's okay, happy for the young players to experience this.
"I enjoy the game. Physically, it's tough because you're so low, it becomes hard to be dangerous, takes a toll to try and get in the box the whole time.
"I love football, I love this game. It's nice to be back here. I always love the Champions League. Now we're a new team, let's see where this adventure will take us."
English sides are now unbeaten in their last 11 Champions League games against clubs from Denmark (W8 D3), since Arsenal’s 1-5 defeat to Fortuna Hjorring in the 2002-03 semi-final.
This win did see Arsenal snap a run of losing their opening Champions League fixtures in each of the past two seasons.
"We left it late," said Arsenal defender Steph Catley.
"It's tough at the moment and in the Champions League there are no easy games. They defended great, we didn't score early and it didn't come until the end.

"In the Champions League, you never think it's an easy day. I was expecting a tough game and it became really difficult but credit to the girls, they did everything and Mariona was very calm in that moment.

"It's hard to put your finger on it [what is going wrong], it is a bit of a slog and the goals are not coming as freely as they have in the past. It's not a lack of trying, we're doing everything we can to put the ball into the back of the net.

"We have great history in this competition and it's important we are in it every year and challenging to win. We have a real belief that we can go on and win it. It's a long season and we're working really hard so to get the wins early on is very important."
Elsewhere on Tuesday, Real Madrid and Paris Saint-Germain drew 1-1.
Felicia Schroder opened the scoring for Madrid after just two minutes, but Sakina Karchaoui equalised from the penalty spot in the second half.

12fytptholf7i1erdgqmlacsmi.title: Australia friendlies the beginning of 'new generation' for Brazil, says Ancelotti
12fytptholf7i1erdgqmlacsmi.subtitle: Brazil face Australia in their first matches since exiting the World Cup, with Carlo Ancelotti making a string of changes to his squad.
paragraphs: Carlo Ancelotti says Brazil's friendlies during this international break should serve as the beginning for a "new generation", following their disappointing World Cup campaign.
Brazil were dumped out of the last 16 at this summer's World Cup by Norway, which was the earliest they had been eliminated from FIFA's flagship tournament since 1990.
Ancelotti has responded by making a raft of changes to his 26-man squad to face Australia (twice) and India, with Casemiro and Fabinho among the big names to miss out.
In fact, only Gabriel Magalhaes, Marquinhos, Bruno Guimaraes, Danilo Santos, Vinicius Junior, Raphinha, Endrick and Rayan remain from Brazil's World Cup contingent.
Ancelotti's selection is partly built around players who are also eligible for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics, hoping he can use them as the spine of his squad for the 2030 World Cup.
The Brazil boss is expecting a tough test in Brazil's two friendlies against Australia, and he hopes they mark the start of the new era for the Selecao.
"It's difficult to say it's a friendly. For Brazil, it will never be a friendly game," Ancelotti said. "It will be an important game.
"A new season, we have a goal to find new players, to find a new generation of players for the World Cup and the Copa America. And we start the game tomorrow.
"I know that soccer in Australia is not the biggest sport. But they did really well [at the World Cup], and Tony [Popovic, Australia's coach] did a fantastic job.
"He organised a fantastic team, really compact, strong defensively, with a fantastic counter-attack. They won a fantastic game against Turkiye, then lost on penalties against Egypt.
"I think that in modern football, there are no easy games. You have to prepare well for the game; you have to respect the rival and do your best."
Australia come into the game fresh from reaching the World Cup knockout stages for the third time in their history, having lost on penalties to Egypt in the round of 32.
Tony Popovic is preparing Australia for the Asian Cup next January, at which point his contract is set to conclude.
It will be the first time that Ancelotti has managed a match in Australia, and he is looking forward to reuniting with Popovic, with whom he has a friendship with off the pitch.
"We are good friends," Ancelotti said of his relationship with Popovic. "Sometimes we have the possibility to meet to talk about football.
"We spent time together when I was in Milan; we spent time together in Brisbane. It's a pleasure to talk about football with him. He's doing a fantastic job here.
"A really passionate manager. I hope the best for him. I think the World Cup he had was a really good World Cup. The team showed strong quality, a compact team.
"We've had a fantastic reception, not only from the Brazilian community, but from all the people.
"The national team of Brazil is really respected everywhere in the world. [It's] my first time in Australia, so I'm trying my best to enjoy this beautiful country."

Carlo Ancelotti says Brazil's friendlies during this international break should serve as the beginning for a "new generation", following their disappointing World Cup campaign. 

Brazil were dumped out of the last 16 at this summer's World Cup by Norway, which was the earliest they had been eliminated from FIFA's flagship tournament since 1990. 

Ancelotti has responded by making a raft of changes to his 26-man squad to face Australia (twice) and India, with Casemiro and Fabinho among the big names to miss out. 

In fact, only Gabriel Magalhaes, Marquinhos, Bruno Guimaraes, Danilo Santos, Vinicius Junior, Raphinha, Endrick and Rayan remain from Brazil's World Cup contingent. 

Ancelotti's selection is partly built around players who are also eligible for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics, hoping he can use them as the spine of his squad for the 2030 World Cup.

The Brazil boss is expecting a tough test in Brazil's two friendlies against Australia, and he hopes they mark the start of the new era for the Selecao.

"It's difficult to say it's a friendly. For Brazil, it will never be a friendly game," Ancelotti said. "It will be an important game.

"A new season, we have a goal to find new players, to find a new generation of players for the World Cup and the Copa America. And we start the game tomorrow.

"I know that soccer in Australia is not the biggest sport. But they did really well [at the World Cup], and Tony [Popovic, Australia's coach] did a fantastic job.

"He organised a fantastic team, really compact, strong defensively, with a fantastic counter-attack. They won a fantastic game against Turkiye, then lost on penalties against Egypt.

"I think that in modern football, there are no easy games. You have to prepare well for the game; you have to respect the rival and do your best."

Australia come into the game fresh from reaching the World Cup knockout stages for the third time in their history, having lost on penalties to Egypt in the round of 32.

Tony Popovic is preparing Australia for the Asian Cup next January, at which point his contract is set to conclude. 

It will be the first time that Ancelotti has managed a match in Australia, and he is looking forward to reuniting with Popovic, with whom he has a friendship with off the pitch. 

"We are good friends," Ancelotti said of his relationship with Popovic. "Sometimes we have the possibility to meet to talk about football.

"We spent time together when I was in Milan; we spent time together in Brisbane. It's a pleasure to talk about football with him. He's doing a fantastic job here.

"A really passionate manager. I hope the best for him. I think the World Cup he had was a really good World Cup. The team showed strong quality, a compact team.

"We've had a fantastic reception, not only from the Brazilian community, but from all the people.

"The national team of Brazil is really respected everywhere in the world. [It's] my first time in Australia, so I'm trying my best to enjoy this beautiful country."

12wp6fcugs0qg1dmw9ecnwclom.title: Chelsea's Estevao to 'seize every opportunity' after falling behind Palmer, Rogers and Joao Pedro
12wp6fcugs0qg1dmw9ecnwclom.subtitle: Cole Palmer, Morgan Rogers and Joao Pedro have shone as a front three for Chelsea this season, with Estevao playing a backup role.
paragraphs: Estevao is determined to "seize every opportunity" he gets at Chelsea, having found himself behind Cole Palmer, Morgan Rogers and Joao Pedro in Xabi Alonso's pecking order.
The Brazilian arrived at Stamford Bridge from Palmeiras in 2025 and appeared 36 times across all competitions for the Blues in his debut season at Stamford Bridge.

Across those outings, 20 of which were starts, he scored eight goals and laid on three assists, while ranking second for dribbles attempted (133) and third for dribbles completed (58) among all players in Chelsea's squad, despite his relative lack of gametime.

The 19-year-old would have been hoping to kick on at the start of 2026-27, following Xabi Alonso's appointment as head coach, but he is yet to provide a goal involvement in six outings and has only started twice.
While Pedro Neto has found a new role at wing-back in Alonso's 3-4-3 system, the attacking trio of Palmer, Rogers and Joao Pedro have been highly impressive.
Of the Blues' 10 Premier League goals this season, only one – Romeo Lavia's opening goal in a 4-3 win over Brighton – has not involved at least one of that trio as the scorer or the assister.
Estevao understands the form of Chelsea's other attackers has limited his opportunities, but he hopes to make a big impression when he gets a chance.
"I think every coach has their own way of playing. Of course, we work every day, I give my best every day, and that's what I do," Estevao said at a press conference while on international duty.
"We have quality players at Chelsea, so what I do is focus on what I can control. I try to give my best in training. When I get an opportunity, I try to give my best, day after day.
"I try to seize every opportunity I have, control everything I can, and I leave it in God's hands, and I trust myself a lot, too."
Estevao has only played 148 minutes in all competitions for Chelsea this term, compared to 578 for Palmer and 552 for Rogers, with those figures making them the Blues' two most-used players.
Joao Pedro has played 377 minutes, having missed last Friday's 3-0 defeat to Brentford due to a knee issue.
That injury caused the striker to withdraw from Brazil's squad, but Estevao will hope to rack up some minutes when the Selecao face Australia (twice) and India in friendlies.

14qi2wh9aop4w1iaia6yqd00d6.title: Portugal 1-0 Wales: Joao Felix goal enough to give Jesus winning start
14qi2wh9aop4w1iaia6yqd00d6.subtitle: Portugal's first match under Jorge Jesus saw them beat Wales in the Nations League, but they were made to work for Thursday's victory.
paragraphs: Jorge Jesus got his Portugal tenure up and running with a win as the defending Nations League champions began their 2026-27 campaign with a 1-0 victory against Wales.
Joao Felix struck the decisive blow in the first half at Estadio Jose Alvalade, though Wales had more than enough chances to at least claim a point away from home.
Portugal started brightly as Cristiano Ronaldo's first sight of goal saw him drag a shot wide, before Vitinha and Joao Felix had their efforts blocked by Wales' retreating defence.

The hosts had to wait until the 22nd minute for their first shot on target, and it resulted in a goal. Nuno Mendes skipped beyond Ethan Ampadu before laying the ball off to Joao Felix, who took a touch before seeing his attempt nestle into the bottom-left corner from the edge of the penalty area.
Ronaldo, in his quest to reach 1,000 career goals, then volleyed just wide before his tame effort after being found by Joao Felix was comfortably held by Danny Ward.

Portugal should have doubled their lead four minutes into the second half, but Ronaldo somehow turned Ruben Neves' cross over the bar, and he thought he had got his goal when he raced onto Bruno Fernandes' defence-splitting pass, only for it to be ruled out following a VAR check for offside.

But Wales spurned a glorious chance to draw level when Brennan Johnson ghosted in behind the Portugal backline and lofted an effort onto the crossbar, with Lewis Koumas' attempt on the rebound blocked off the line by Ruben Dias.

Daniel James and Mendes then fired wide at either end before substitute Goncalo Ramos stung the palms of Ward, with Portugal able to weather the Wales storm in the minutes that remained, getting themselves up and running in the Nations League.
Portugal fail to build on Joao Felix strike

With Wales missing several key players including Harry Wilson and Joe Rodon, many expected a comfortable outing for Portugal, and it looked as though it would be following Joao Felix's goal, which was his fifth in his last 10 starts for the Selecao.

He was teed up by the marauding Mendes, who registered his seventh assist for Portugal since the start of 2024. Overall, he's third for goal involvements in that time for his nation, behind Ronaldo (20) and Fernandes (17).

Portugal's 13 shots in the first half were also their most in the opening 45 minutes of a game since November 2025 against Armenia (17), but after the break, Wales looked the more likely to alter the scoreline.

Wales do, however, remain winless in their last five matches (D3 L2), their worst run under manager Craig Bellamy, but there will plenty of positives he can take from their performance ahead of facing Denmark in three days' time.

Jesus' side finished with an expected goals (xG) total of 2.36 from their 23 shots, only five of which were on target, compared to Wales' tally of 0.84 from their five attempts, with Portugal's next test seeing them take on Erling Haaland and Norway.

162qve87tj1fe1ffb7r6xmge7t.title: 'Full package' Kane deserves Ballon d'Or recognition, says Tuchel
162qve87tj1fe1ffb7r6xmge7t.subtitle: Bayern Munich and England striker Harry Kane is among the Ballon d'Or favourites, and he has the backing of his international manager.
paragraphs: England boss Thomas Tuchel firmly believes Harry Kane should win the Ballon d'Or this year, describing the striker as "the full package".
Kane is one of three players being tipped to contend for football's most prestigious individual award next month, alongside Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal.

That is off the back of a 2025-26 season in which he plundered 65 goals across all competitions for Bayern Munich, before hitting six more to help England finish third at the World Cup, the final tournament to fall in the 2026 Ballon d'Or eligibility period.
No other player from Europe's top five leagues scored more than 50 goals in all competitions last term, with Mbappe netting a half-century for Real Madrid.
But speaking in the build-up to England's 2026-27 Nations League opener against Spain on Saturday, Tuchel said Kane's game is about much more than his goals, highlighting his out-of-possession work.
Asked if Kane was his pick to be crowned the world's best player, Tuchel told ITV Sport: "Yeah. After this season, yeah.
"Seventy-plus goals [for club and country], three titles with Bayern Munich, the semi-finals at the World Cup and in the Champions League...
"He's getting better and better. I think he added a level of physicality to his match. He's just so committed to the high press and being involved in every part of the match.
"Be it in deep build-up, be it in finishing, be it in build-up play in the middle block, be it in defending. He's just the full package."

Last season, Kane recovered possession 124 times for Bayern, with 34 of those regains being in the final third. Those figures put him below Yamal (176 recoveries, 42 in final third) but ahead of Mbappe (65 recoveries, 30 in final third).
Kane also won 222 duels, less than Yamal's 381 but more than Mbappe's 162, and won 20 of his 28 tackles.
Yamal won 32 of 58 for Barcelona, while Mbappe – somewhat remarkably – only won two of six attempted tackles for Madrid, in 44 games.

After England fell short in the World Cup semi-finals, losing 2-1 to Argentina having gone ahead through Anthony Gordon's goal, many questioned whether Kane had played his final game at FIFA's showpiece tournament.
He will turn 37 shortly after the conclusion of the 2030 edition, which will be co-hosted by Spain, Portugal and Morocco, but Tuchel feels he has every chance of featuring.
"Yeah, there's no problem," Tuchel said when asked about Kane's longevity. "Age is age. It doesn't matter. It's only about quality, and he has a long way to go."

After hosting Spain on Saturday, England continue their Nations League campaign away to Czechia next Tuesday, before visiting Croatia and welcoming Czechia back to Wembley Stadium for a swift return fixture.
England have won just two of their last 13 games against the reigning World Cup holders, losing nine of those matches (D2).
However, one of those wins came at home to Spain in November 2011 (1-0), with the other being away to Germany in March 2016 (3-2).

17a93nv5v0pw1hjocx7gd3tbn.title: Klopp says Germany can do better after ill-tempered Netherlands draw
17a93nv5v0pw1hjocx7gd3tbn.subtitle: Jurgen Klopp's first match in charge of Germany, a 1-1 draw with the Netherlands, was marred by injuries to Kai Havertz and Jamal Musiala.
paragraphs: Jurgen Klopp was satisfied with a point on his debut as Germany's head coach, although he knows his side have plenty more gears to go through after their 1-1 draw with the Netherlands.
Felix Nmecha's 32nd-minute strike put Germany on course for victory against their old rivals on Thursday, on Klopp's eagerly anticipated international debut in the Nations League.

However, two minutes into second-half stoppage time, Cody Gakpo – who played 79 games under Klopp for Liverpool, scoring 23 goals in that time – met Ruben van Bommel's outside-of-the-foot cross with a sumptuous volley to snatch a point for the Netherlands.
The Oranje, who were playing their first game under Barcelona great Xavi, utterly dominated the second half, racking up 2.61 expected goals to Germany's 0.24 xG after half-time.
Overall, the Netherlands posted an xG figure of 3.12 from 22 shots, compared to Germany's 1.5 from 10 attempts, while they also had four Opta-defined 'big chances', with Klopp's men having two.

It was the first time the Oranje had created 3.0 xG or greater in a match against a team inside the top 30 of FIFA's world rankings since June 2019, when they had 3.1 in a Nations League semi-final win over England.
Speaking to RTL after full-time, Klopp acknowledged there was plenty for his team to work on ahead of Sunday's matchup with Greece, but his initial assessment was still positive.
"There were lots of things that worked. I'm very satisfied with many individual performances, with the passion as well," he said.
"But we can play better football, for sure. I would have loved to win, but I can live with the point."
Asked if he was nervous ahead of the game, Klopp replied: "I stood there over 1,000 times, so it was quite natural."

A high-octane and at times bad-tempered affair saw the Netherlands have two goals disallowed, with the first – a Virgil van Dijk header that was chalked off for Brian Brobbey backing into Marc-Andre ter Stegen – proving contentious.

And Germany's goal also came with a hint of controversy as Klopp's side played on while Brobbey was down injured, with the Netherlands' players reacting furiously after Nmecha swept into the top-left corner.

Brobbey had to be substituted when the game restarted, and his exit came after Germany striker Kai Havertz also hobbled off, having been on the receiving end of a high tackle from Quinten Timber – the twin brother of his Arsenal team-mate Jurrien.
Germany also lost Jamal Musiala to a thigh issue during the warm-ups, and Klopp is now waiting for updates on both players.
"Unfortunately, this happened to Jamal before the game, then Kai also said he felt it. They are both having an MRI at the moment. I hope we get the diagnosis tonight," he said.
"Of course, it's not great now. I hope it's just nothing bad. The boys are probably out of our next game, but hopefully they'll be ready to play again quite quickly."

17krq7bj4h1kr121kdkw5s68ve.title: Seattle Sounders 2-0 Real Salt Lake: Musovski and Rusnak end long winless streak
17krq7bj4h1kr121kdkw5s68ve.subtitle: Seattle Sounders had not tasted victory since mid-May, but they got three points on the board against a struggling Real Salt Lake side.
paragraphs: Seattle Sounders ended their long wait for a win in MLS as they beat Real Salt Lake 2-0 at Lumen Field.
The Sounders had not won a league game since May, but Paul Arriola got two assists to set up Danny Musovski and Albert Rusnak to secure all three points.
Arriola flashed an early shot just wide of the near post and into the side netting after the Sounders cut through RSL's defense.
Cristian Roldan also failed to hit the target, while RSL's only effort of the first half saw Sergi Solans bend a long-range shot well wide of the far post on the stroke of half-time.

But Seattle made a strong start after the break, taking just over two minutes to break the deadlock. Arriola laid it off to Musovski, whose low fizzer trickled past Rafael Cabral into the back of the net.

Solans forced a fine stop out of Andrew Thomas moments later from a tight angle, but Seattle continued to push, with Jordan Morris' effort – which could have been a cross – from the right of the box pushed away by Cabral.
A loose touch from Philip Quinton almost gifted Arriola a goal; the striker rushed onto the ball in the box, but Cabral rushed back to get his foot behind it.
Rusnak made sure of the points with 17 minutes remaining, though, as he was allowed to run through RSL's half before slotting it past Cabral.
Seattle taste victory again
After a strong start to the season, Seattle have slowly been sliding down the Western Conference table after failing to taste victory since a 3-2 win over the San Jose Earthquakes on May 13.

But on Wednesday, they ended a winless run of 13 straight MLS matches (D5 L8). They had lost eight straight before drawing each of their last five – including coming from 3-1 down to earn a point against the Colorado Rapids last time out.

The clear-cut chances were few and far between in the match, with the Sounders accumulating 0.91 expected goals (xG) from their 11 attempts, though four were on target. While RSL had 12 shots (0.43 xG), only two tested Thomas.
Arriola was the driving force, having a joint-game-high three shots and the only 'big' chance of the match, while he also got an assist from both of the chances he created.
While Seattle moved up to 10th in the West, level on points with the Portland Timbers, RSL sit 13th after extending their own winless run to 13 games, having lost each of the last four.

18kaq92nmwrzf1g1gvjiraypwh.title: Ter Stegen says Klopp call-up was extra special following injury woes
18kaq92nmwrzf1g1gvjiraypwh.subtitle: Marc-Andre ter Stegen has already been named as Jurgen Klopp's Germany number one, after more than a year in the international wilderness.
paragraphs: Marc-Andre ter Stegen says being named as Jurgen Klopp's first-choice goalkeeper for Germany was extra special, following his well-documented injury issues.

Germany will face the Netherlands in their first match under Klopp on Thursday, in the Nations League, with further games against Greece (home and away) and Serbia to come during this international break.
And, with Manuel Neuer retiring from international football in the aftermath of Germany's shock round-of-32 World Cup defeat to Paraguay, the former Liverpool boss had to name a new number one.
Despite calling up Besiktas' Alexander Nubel, Bayern Munich's Jonas Urbig, Eintracht Frankfurt's Noah Atubolu and Augsburg's Finn Dahmen, he has gone with the experience of Ter Stegen.
The most recent of Ter Stegen's 44 caps came against France in the previous edition of the Nations League in June 2025, with injuries restricting his gametime in recent years.
He only made 10 appearances across all competitions combined in 2024-25 and 2025-26, for parent club Barcelona and Girona, who he joined on loan for the second half of last season.
But, after starting eight straight games for his latest loan club, Ajax, Ter Stegen is excited to be back on the international stage.

"It's always something special for me, to be here again now," he told Sky Sport DE. "Especially if you had a time when things didn't go the way you imagined, when your body wasn't by your side, then of course, you appreciate it all the more.

"I believe that I have worked a lot to make this happen again. I'm also looking forward to meeting many new faces, some old friends who are here, and just to start again and give our best for the team.
"There's a smile on my face. I'm just happy to be 100% back, to be able to be with the national team and hopefully play successful football. That is the wish of all of us."

Klopp takes charge of his country after overseeing 674 games in the Bundesliga and the Premier League, across wildly successful spells with Mainz, Borussia Dortmund and Liverpool. That is more games in Europe's top five leagues than any previous Germany head coach had tallied before taking the job.
Ter Stegen said of Klopp: "He's one of one, as you know, with the joy he conveys and his interest in football, the enthusiasm he has for his own football.
"I don't think you need to say anything. I think everyone knows him and everyone knows how much he lives and feels football."

Klopp is one of only three bosses – alongside Pep Guardiola and Carlo Ancelotti – to have won the Bundesliga and Premier League titles, and he became famed for his "heavy metal" style of play with both Dortmund and Liverpool.

But Ter Stegen knows adopting that way of playing will be a learning curve for Germany, adding: "There are issues he would like to tackle, because he has his way of seeing football and understanding football. We have to try to internalise that as quickly as possible.

"For the time being, there are smaller levers that can and must be pulled, to then get into his philosophy. We want to play great football from the start, to defend not through individual actions, but really through the collective.
"We have very few training sessions to talk a lot about gameplan and so on, so we will keep it relatively simple now. We have to be attentive and implement that as quickly as possible."

18kqj4ll7crqczd8mfxkvej68.title: Branthwaite hopes injury issues are behind him following England recall
18kqj4ll7crqczd8mfxkvej68.subtitle: Injuries have restricted Jarrad Branthwaite to just one senior cap for England, but he will hope to add to that tally in the next two weeks.
paragraphs: Jarrad Branthwaite hopes he is back in the England setup for good after missing Euro 2024 and the 2026 World Cup, having earned a recall to the Three Lions' squad.
Branthwaite has been named in Thomas Tuchel's group for Nations League fixtures against Spain, Czechia (who they face both home and away) and Croatia.

He has been an ever-present for Everton so far this season, helping the Toffees keep three clean sheets in five games and concede the joint-fewest goals in the Premier League (three, alongside Leeds United).

Branthwaite won his only senior England cap to date in June 2024, when he was named in Gareth Southgate's preliminary Euro 2024 squad and appeared in a friendly against Bosnia-Herzegovina, only to miss out on the final party.
The 24-year-old also missed this summer's World Cup after an injury-hit 2025-26 season, in which he was restricted to just 10 Premier League appearances and seven starts.

But, having visited a specialist in Germany in a bid to combat his persistent hamstring issues during the off-season, Branthwaite hopes he can now challenge Marc Guehi and Ezri Konsa for an England starting spot.
"Being out for such a long time with injury didn't help, missing three or four of the camps and missing a lot of football," Branthwaite said of his England struggles.
"My aim is to stay injury-free and play as many games as I can and keep giving myself the best possible chance to be in the squad.
"I've not spoken to him [Tuchel] recently. When we get there, we'll have a chat. I can't wait to join up with the squad and enjoy the couple of weeks.

"It is a proud moment. In the last season or so, it has been a target of mine when I've been out to get back playing and give myself the best possible chance of being in and around the England squad after missing a length of time.
"The season has started well individually and as a team and that has definitely helped. I believe I am good enough to be in the England squad, so hopefully I can show that."

Branthwaite, Guehi, Konsa, Jarell Quansah and Trevoh Chalobah are the centre-backs in England's group for this international break, with their Nations League opener against world champions Spain taking place at Wembley on Saturday.
England have won 10 of their last 11 competitive home matches (L1), including each of their last five without conceding.
Only once before have the Three Lions won six competitive home fixtures to nil, doing so between March 2015 and March 2017.
However, Spain are unbeaten in each of their last 38 matches in all competitions (W29 D9), the longest ever streak by a European nation.

194kvzunupcho1w6yo91gg0suu.title: Bompastor will not risk James in Champions League as Arsenal clash looms
194kvzunupcho1w6yo91gg0suu.subtitle: Chelsea open their Women's Champions League campaign against Austria Wien, but with Arsenal next up in the WSL, squad rotation is likely.
paragraphs: Chelsea will not take any risks with Lauren James against Austria Wien in the Women's Champions League, as Sonia Bompastor looks to get her ready to face Arsenal on Sunday.

The Blues are overwhelming favourites to open their European league-phase campaign with three points on Wednesday, with the Opta supercomputer assigning them a 93.3% chance of victory over the tournament debutants.
Chelsea's only previous meeting with an Austrian side in the Champions League came last season, as they thumped St. Polten 6-0 in the league phase.
Having gone out at the quarter-final stage last term following three straight semi-final defeats, the Blues are hoping to go further in Europe this term, but rotation is likely this week.
With a huge London derby against Arsenal on the horizon in the Women's Super League, Bompastor has already confirmed James – who picked up a minor injury in training – will be rested.
"She should be available for the game on the weekend, but we don't want to take any risks for the game tomorrow," Bompastor said of James. "She's a bit short."
Bompastor also confirmed Erin Cuthbert, Manaka Matsukubo and Aggie Beever-Jones are all back in training, with the latter being the only one of that trio to appear in a WSL match this season.
"They are training again with the team, so a lot of players and it's good news. Manaka is back in training, not fully fit yet, but it's good to have her back," Bompastor said.
"It's really good to see Erin back. I'm always happy when I have most of my players on the pitch. It brings positivity around the team and the quality on the pitch progresses.
"It's always good to have that competition in the squad, with everyone happy to be on the pitch together."
Chelsea lost just one of their eight games in the Champions League last season (W5 D2), conceding the fewest goals of any side in the competition (six).

Austria Wien will become the fourth different side from Austria to participate in the Champions League, but those teams are winless in 21 games in the competition (D3 L18) since St. Polten beat Slavia Prague 1-0 in November 2022.
English sides have won all five of their meetings with Austrian opponents in the competition by an aggregate score of 17-2.

1b1jzurh3d3i4144cnru6aexc4.title: Real Madrid 'living in another galaxy' over referee claims, says LaLiga chief Tebas
1b1jzurh3d3i4144cnru6aexc4.subtitle: LaLiga president Javier Tebas has slammed Real Madrid for their treatment of referee Ortiz Arias following Sunday's loss to Atletico Madrid.
paragraphs: Real Madrid are "living in another galaxy" if they believe LaLiga's officials are biased against them, the competition's president Javier Tebas said amid a fierce debate over refereeing standards.
Madrid were beaten 2-1 by Atletico Madrid in Sunday's derby at the Estadio Metropolitano, but the controversial nature of their loss sparked a furious reaction from Los Blancos.

Jose Mourinho's team had Dean Huijsen sent off for a last-man foul early in the second half, but Madrid felt Lee Kang-in and Cristian Romero should have seen red for Atleti, the former for a high challenge on Federico Valverde and the latter for treading on Jude Bellingham.
Mourinho brought printed images of both incidents to his post-match press conference, saying they were the "story of the game" and describing referee Ortiz Arias as weak and inexperienced.
Atleti hit back on their social media channels on Monday, posting an image taken during Mourinho's press conference alongside the caption: "Stop referee harassment now."
Madrid used the title "a terrible refereeing performance decides the derby" for their official club-produced match report, accompanied by images of the Lee and Romero challenges.
And Tebas – who has criticised Madrid's treatment of referees and desire to set up a breakaway European Super League in the past – has now slammed the club's behaviour.

"Here they go again, the mouthpieces and the regime's television, building the same old narrative: the permanent conspiracy," Tebas wrote on X, responding to a Spanish media article that alleged referees routinely favour Madrid's opponents.
"Claiming that referees are directed against Real Madrid is living in another galaxy.
"That narrative serves as an excuse to cover up other shortcomings that are plain to see in these first matches of the season.
"It's more comfortable to point to a conspiracy than to explain what's happening on the pitch.
"GET THE BLINDERS OFF! It's September, and they're already claiming the League is tainted. Nobody with common sense believes that old excuse anymore."

Madrid previously sent a formal letter of complaint about LaLiga's referees to the Spanish Football Federation (RFEF) in 2025, prompting Tebas to accuse Madrid of harming the competition and "building a story of victimhood."

1bw4b4j8qe5t618na967le382d.title: Alaba joins Udinese as free agent following Real Madrid exit
1bw4b4j8qe5t618na967le382d.subtitle: Following five successful years with Real Madrid, David Alaba will now ply his trade in Serie A after joining Udinese on Thursday.
paragraphs: David Alaba has laid out his ambitions to "win again" after the former Real Madrid defender completed his move to Serie A side Udinese on Thursday.
Alaba has joined Udinese as a free agent on a contract that will run until the end of the 2026-27 season, following five successful years in the Spanish capital.
The 34-year-old brings with him a wealth of European experience, having also spent 13 years with Bayern Munich before making the move to Madrid in 2021.

He won 25 trophies with the Bundesliga giants, before going on to win two LaLiga crowns and two Champions League titles, in addition to a Copa del Rey, a Supercopa de Espana, a UEFA Super Cup, a Club World Cup and an Intercontinental Cup with Los Blancos.
Alaba was a regular in his first few seasons with Madrid and started their 2022 Champions League final win against Liverpool, but injuries have hampered him in recent seasons.
The Austria international missed 13 months of action after rupturing his anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) in December 2023, and failed to rediscover his impressive form.
He was restricted to 17 appearances in 2023-24, across all competitions, then made 14 in 2024-25 and 16 in 2025-26.

He only played 600 minutes in 2024-25 and was limited to 575 last season, with both of those campaigns ending without silverware, something he intends to change having now sealed his switch to Udinese.
"I've had a lot of different experiences, and I've won a lot during my career, but one thing hasn't changed. I want to compete and win again," Alaba said.
"I still want to achieve something special and that is the mentality I will bring to Udinese."
Alaba joins an Udinese side that sit 13th in Serie A this season, having taken four points from their opening five league games of 2026-27.
Only Venzia (13), Fiorentina and Monza (both 12) have conceded more league goals than Udinese (11) this term, something Alaba will be aiming to improve.
"The signing of David Alaba is a source of enormous pride for the whole club," said Udinese general manager Franco Collavino.
"We're welcoming an established champion, a leader and an exemplary professional. His arrival demonstrates Udinese's desire to grow and compete at the highest levels."
Udinese return to action after the extended international break on October 12, with a trip to Torino up next.

1clrgb6ichllh1tvuhpbqvdajn.title: Havertz and Musiala withdraw from Germany squad in double injury blow
1clrgb6ichllh1tvuhpbqvdajn.subtitle: Jurgen Klopp suffered two withdrawals from his Germany squad, but had replacements to call upon from his second party of players.
paragraphs: Germany have been dealt a double injury blow as Kai Havertz and Jamal Musiala have both withdrawn from the squad.
Musiala suffered a torn muscle fibre in his right thigh during the warm-up for their Nations League opener against the Netherlands.
Havertz started the match, which finished as a 1-1 draw, but was then withdrawn in the 30th minute due to a muscle strain – as announced by the German Football Association (DFB).
No timeline has been set for Havertz's return, but German media reports that Musiala will be out for three to four weeks for Bayern Munich.
Jurgen Klopp has named two squads for this extended international break, including 44 players, so Florian Wirtz and Jonathan Burkardt have now been called up one game earlier than originally planned.
Wirtz has come under criticism for his Liverpool performances so far this season, particularly after their 1-0 victory over Bournemouth.
He has made six appearances for Liverpool in all competitions this term, registering just one assist, despite creating 12 chances – the third-most of any Reds player.
Burkardt, meanwhile, has made a stellar start to the campaign for Eintracht Frankfurt, netting six goals in his five outings.
He is currently averaging a goal every 64.7 minutes and a 42.9% shot conversion rate.
Germany's second Nations League match sees them host Greece on Sunday.

1d278ewvzy6121v58olswbrifd.title: Xavi sees 'superior' Netherlands in second half against Germany
1d278ewvzy6121v58olswbrifd.subtitle: Xavi was forced to settle for a draw on his Netherlands debut against Germany, but he felt his team should have taken all three points.
paragraphs: Xavi believed his Netherlands team deserved more than a point in their Nations League opener against Germany following a "superior" performance in the second half.
The former Barcelona boss made his Netherlands bow at Johan Cruijff Arena on Thursday, with his team playing out a 1-1 draw against Jurgen Klopp's Germany.
Felix Nmecha had given Germany a 32nd-minute lead when he finished past Bart Verbruggen, though the hosts felt that Brian Brobbey had been fouled in the build-up.
But the Netherlands dominated after the break, with Denzel Dumfries denied by Marc-Andre ter Stegen before Mexx Meerdink's goal was disallowed for a foul by Virgil van Dijk.
However, Xavi's side were able to get the goal their performance merited in second-half stoppage time when Cody Gakpo brilliantly volleyed Ruben van Bommel's cross home.

The Netherlands improved their expected goals (xG) total from 0.57 to 2.61 in the second half, while also having more shots (14 to five), more big chances (five to none) and touches in the opposition box (26 to 11) than their opponents.

In fact, the Oranje recorded an overall expected goals (xG) total of 3.18 to Germany's 1.45 xG. It was the first time they had registered above 3.0 in that metric against a nation ranked inside the top 30 of the FIFA rankings since June 2019.
"We were a bit nervous in the first half," Xavi said. "So at half-time, I said that we had to show more personality. I asked for more ambition.
"I saw that in the second half. I'm glad that the players realised after the break that we were superior.
"We deserved more than this. We created a lot of chances, put on good pressure and took a lot of initiative.
"I'm less happy with the number of lost duels, I'm not happy about that. But I have a good feeling about it.
"The debutants also did a great job. Mexx Meerdink was easy to play and fought continuously, and Ruben van Bommel filled in excellently with his ball conquest and assist."
But there was concern for Xavi following the stalemate, with Brobbey replaced in the 35th minute by Meerdink because of what appeared to be an injury to his hamstring.
The Sunderland striker arrived into the international break fresh from scoring a hat-trick against Manchester City, but it remains to be seen how severe the injury is.
Xavi confirmed that Brobbey would take no further part in the rest of the Netherlands' fixtures, and he revealed another striker would be called up to fill that gap in the final third.
"Brian is indeed injured, unfortunately, so we will call up another striker. We haven't decided who yet. I haven't had time for that yet," Xavi said of Brobbey's issue.
Brobbey's injury led to Germany's opening goal, with the Netherlands frustrated by their opponents, who appeared as though they were going to kick the ball out of play.

The former Barcelona boss made his Netherlands bow at Johan Cruijff Arena on Thursday, with his team playing out a 1-1 draw against Jurgen Klopp's Germany. 

Felix Nmecha had given Germany a 32nd-minute lead when he finished past Bart Verbruggen, though the hosts felt that Brian Brobbey had been fouled in the build-up. 

But the Netherlands dominated after the break, with Denzel Dumfries denied by Marc-Andre ter Stegen before Mexx Meerdink's goal was disallowed for a foul by Virgil van Dijk. 

However, Xavi's side were able to get the goal their performance merited in second-half stoppage time when Cody Gakpo brilliantly volleyed Ruben van Bommel's cross home.

The Netherlands improved their expected goals (xG) total from 0.57 to 2.61 in the second half, while also having more shots (14 to five), more big chances (five to none) and touches in the opposition box (26 to 11) than their opponents. 

In fact, the Oranje recorded an overall expected goals (xG) total of 3.18 to Germany's 1.45 xG. It was the first time they had registered above 3.0 in that metric against a nation ranked inside the top 30 of the FIFA rankings since June 2019. 

"We were a bit nervous in the first half," Xavi said. "So at half-time, I said that we had to show more personality. I asked for more ambition.

"I saw that in the second half. I'm glad that the players realised after the break that we were superior.

"We deserved more than this. We created a lot of chances, put on good pressure and took a lot of initiative.

"I'm less happy with the number of lost duels, I'm not happy about that. But I have a good feeling about it.

"The debutants also did a great job. Mexx Meerdink was easy to play and fought continuously, and Ruben van Bommel filled in excellently with his ball conquest and assist."

But there was concern for Xavi following the stalemate, with Brobbey replaced in the 35th minute by Meerdink because of what appeared to be an injury to his hamstring. 

The Sunderland striker arrived into the international break fresh from scoring a hat-trick against Manchester City, but it remains to be seen how severe the injury is.

Xavi confirmed that Brobbey would take no further part in the rest of the Netherlands' fixtures, and he revealed another striker would be called up to fill that gap in the final third. 

"Brian is indeed injured, unfortunately, so we will call up another striker. We haven't decided who yet. I haven't had time for that yet," Xavi said of Brobbey's issue.

"We were pushing and we had opportunities. And that we still managed to score an equaliser, is nice."

1ex9mz1u93mlf1b37rwx3j1t42.title: Gordon urges England to focus on their strengths, not replicate Spain
1ex9mz1u93mlf1b37rwx3j1t42.subtitle: England's tactics in their World Cup semi-final loss were questioned, but Anthony Gordon believes they need to focus on their strengths.
paragraphs: Anthony Gordon agreed with Thomas Tuchel's comments about England's inability to control games and believes playing to their own strengths will help them win major tournaments.
England lost their World Cup semi-final to Argentina 2-1, before going on to beat France in the third-place play-off and record their best finish at the tournament since winning it in 1966.

However, England were levelled with a lot of criticism for how they played in the semi-final, having gone to a back five after taking the lead in the match, through Gordon, to try and see out a victory.
The tactical tweak saw the Three Lions sit back and defend deeper, with Enzo Fernandez equalising before Lautaro Martinez finished the turnaround in stoppage time.
Tuchel claimed it was "not in England's DNA" to control matches like Spain – their Nations League opponents on Saturday – or Argentina and Brazil, and Gordon backed up that view.
"England, as a nation, we don't have that strength, like the Spanish, where we control games like they do," said Gordon in a press conference. "It's not in us.
"[The] scar [of losing to Argentina] doesn't have to be a negative one, because it might lead us to victory in the next tournaments.

"We can't keep looking at other countries and trying to be like them, because we're not them – we're English, and we have our own strengths which they don't have, so maybe we start playing the way we're good at."
Gordon secured a move to Barcelona from Newcastle United before the start of the World Cup and has made an impressive start to life in Spain.
He acknowledged that the way they approach play is very different to how England do, though it is not a bad thing.
"I'm not sure it's something that can be [taught]," he added.
"Playing in Spain, I can speak with an educated view on the way they keep the ball is different. It's much different than I've ever experienced playing in this country.

"I'm not sure we can ever get that, but we can definitely get better or maybe go the other way and really play to our strengths, which is play physical, play direct football, and on the counter-attack."
England are looking to begin their Nations League campaign with a win when they host Spain at Wembley on Saturday.

However, they have won just two of their last 13 games against the reigning World Cup holders, losing nine times (D2); those wins came at home to Spain in November 2011 (1-0) and away to Germany in March 2016 (3-2).
England have, though, won 10 of their last 11 competitive home matches (L1), including each of the most recent five without conceding.

1fzdvkfezt9fe1nqwb3atnr56w.title: Mbappe: Working under Zidane 'like something from a movie'
1fzdvkfezt9fe1nqwb3atnr56w.subtitle: Current Real Madrid superstar Kylian Mbappe will link up with former Blancos hero Zinedine Zidane for the first time this week, with France.
paragraphs: Kylian Mbappe has likened being coached by Zinedine Zidane to "something from a movie", as France prepare to play their first game under the legendary former midfielder.
Zidane succeeded Didier Deschamps in the aftermath of the 2026 World Cup, which saw France reach the semi-finals before losing 2-0 to eventual champions Spain.

Deschamps led Les Bleus for 14 years and 187 matches in total (also 103 as a player), overseeing their second World Cup triumph in 2018 in addition to runner-up finishes at the 2022 edition and at Euro 2016, with the latter tournament being on home soil.
And France's new era begins with a Nations League trip to Turkiye on Friday, with matches against Belgium – both home and away – and Italy to follow in the next two weeks.
Zidane made 108 appearances for France during his illustrious playing career, scoring 31 goals including a brace in their win over Brazil in the 1998 World Cup final.
He also scored a Panenka penalty in the 2006 final before receiving a red card for an infamous headbutt on Marco Materazzi, as Italy went on to defeat Les Bleus on spot-kicks.
And Mbappe – who will keep hold of the captain's armband under the new regime – has a chance to pass Zidane in the all-time France appearance charts during the extended international break.
Mbappe's next cap will be his 107th, so he could potentially equal Zidane against Belgium next Monday and surpass him versus Italy on October 2, should he appear in all of those matches.

In an interview with AS, Mbappe recalled his first meeting with Zidane, which came when he was a youth player attracting interest from Europe's top clubs, while the former midfield icon was working in Real Madrid's academy.
"Years ago, he was the first to pick me up ‌and ⁠take me to Real Madrid, to the training complex. I was 13 or 14; it was ages ago," Mbappe said.
"And now he's my national team coach. It's like something from a movie, but he's top-level.
"It's real, we're in a new process in France, we have two years to prepare for the European Championships and we're working towards it now."

Zidane is the only manager to win three successive Champions League crowns, doing so with Real Madrid between 2015-16 and 2017-18, but he neglected to take another job in club football after leaving the Santiago Bernabeu for the second time in 2021.
He repeatedly outlined his interest in the France job during the latter years of Deschamps' tenure, and Mbappe is excited to see what changes he makes.
"It's a new phase with a new coach. It's going ⁠to be a new experience for everyone, since we've only ever had Deschamps," Mbappe said.
"It will be a change for us, but I think ⁠everything will turn out very well."

1gbxvraddlm741a2vdd005k0y5.title: Slegers: Big Arsenal squad is a 'luxury problem'
1gbxvraddlm741a2vdd005k0y5.subtitle: Renee Slegers is prepared to rotate her Arsenal squad ahead of their Women's Champions League opener against Koge.
paragraphs: Renee Slegers believes having a large squad is a "luxury problem" as Arsenal prepare for their Women's Champions League opener against Koge.
Arsenal won the Champions League in 2024-25 but fell at the semi-final hurdle last season, as Lyon came from behind to beat them on aggregate and reach the showpiece.
The Gunners, who also finished as runners-up to Manchester City in the Women's Super League last term, bolstered their squad over the summer as they aim to fight for silverware once again.

They brought in eight new signings, including Georgia Stanway, Ona Batlle and Misa Rodriguez, but so far, it has not had the desired effect, with Arsenal winning just one of their three WSL games (D2).
Slegers' side have a big week ahead of them, with a WSL clash with Chelsea to come after their Champions League outing.
But Slegers pointed out that Arsenal were prepared for their packed schedule.
"It's a luxury problem, of course," Slegers said when asked if a big squad was a nice problem to have.
"We have so many different options. The balance becomes, or the challenge becomes, how do you then choose certain things for certain games?
"We're still keeping the main ideas and consistency within the team. You don't chop and change everything.
"At the same time, if I look at where the players are at and where we are, from a game model understanding and players playing their roles, it's on a really high level throughout the squad.
"That also makes me really confident to say, 'I can make changes. These partnerships are working. This is working. This player knows her role on the pitch'.
"It's in a really good place, and that's where we wanted it to be. For the length of the season and all the games that we're going to play, we are able to do these things.

"The reason why we have the size of the squad with basically only senior national team players, so much quality doubled up in every position, is that we can use the whole squad. Especially when it's short turnarounds and we need freshness."
Arsenal are heavy favourites to beat Koge, with an 81.1% win probability according to the Opta supercomputer.
They have won both of their previous meetings with Koge in the Champions League, beating them twice in the 2021-22 group stage (3-0 home, 5-1 away).
However, Arsenal have lost their opening game in each of the last two Champions League seasons: 2-5 to Bayern Munich in 2024-25 and 1-2 to Lyon in 2025-26.
Slegers is also familiar with Koge herself, having faced them while in charge of Rosengard, and she is expecting a tough challenge.
"They're, of course, top of the league in Denmark," Slegers said. "They're a good team.

"I think they have a really good counter-attacking threat with the two players up top. They will try to close down spaces. We're expecting that, whether it's a back four or back five, we'll see when they come out.
"We're definitely respecting the threat that they can pose from fast attacks and counter-attacks. But, again, we're expecting to face a low block."

1gpk2w4i99ndh1glrfkpp13zyb.title: Cifuentes urges Portland to find clinical edge ahead of trip to San Jose
1gpk2w4i99ndh1glrfkpp13zyb.subtitle: The Portland Timbers will be looking to keep their playoff hopes alive when they make the trip to the San Jose Earthquakes this weekend.
paragraphs: Marti Cifuentes believes the only thing missing from his Portland Timbers team is the final product in attack after their disappointing defeat to Atlanta United last time out.
Portland were beaten 1-0 by the Five Stripes at Providence Park, with Aleksey Miranchuk's 28th-minute strike enough to compound the Timbers to a 12th defeat of the season.
That is despite Portland registering an expected goals (xG) total of 2.3 from their 21 shots at Lucas Hoyos' net to Atlanta's tally of 0.85 from their 10 attempts.

It was a result that left the Timbers in a precarious position in the Western Conference, with Cifuentes' side ninth in the division, but the Seattle Sounders, San Diego FC and Austin FC are all within striking distance.

Portland's struggles against teams below them in the standings has been a recurring theme in 2026, and ahead of a trip to PayPal Park to face the San Jose Earthquakes, Cifuentes wants his team to take their chances when they arrive.
"We created more shots, we regained the ball higher up the pitch and there was a lot of positives, but that does not explain the whole history," Cifuentes said.
"The whole history is that we need to be better in front of goal and we need to be more clinical. We need to be better in how we break down low blocks and so on.
"It's going to be a good challenge against San Jose because of the situations we are talking about. There are a lot of situations, but I do not want to spend my time there.
"I want to be focused, be positive and have a lot of energy to go to San Jose that are having a good season, and try to leave there with a good feeling."
San Jose, meanwhile, kept their playoff push going with a 2-2 draw against 10-man Los Angeles FC, with Reid Roberts scoring a 98th-minute equaliser for Bruce Arena's side.
Son Heung-min had given LAFC the lead before Aaron Long was sent off, but Denis Bouanga doubled the visitors' lead eight minutes into the second half at Levi's Stadium.
However, substitute Preston Judd halved the deficit, before Roberts' drive from distance nestled into the bottom-right corner to seal a share of the spoils.
The Earthquakes are fifth in the West and just two points off fourth-place FC Dallas, and Arena believes their draw with LAFC was a true test of his team's character against a difficult opposition.
"The fact that we went down two goals and came back and got a point out of the game is a tremendous test of character and competitiveness on our part," Arena said.
"I thought LAFC did an outstanding job in trying to close out the game. So give both teams credit. This was a really good MLS game today. A lot of quality out there.
"I think that was a very entertaining game for the people here, and to see players like Son [Heung-min] and [Denis] Bouanga and [Hugo] Lloris, he was fantastic.
"And to see quality like [Timo] Werner and have those kinds of players on the field, that was enjoyable and a great setting. The fan base was great. So a good day for MLS."
SJ Earthquakes – Reid Roberts
Roberts scored at 97:32 to secure a deserved point against LAFC last time out.

It was the latest result-changing goal by an Earthquakes player in an MLS match since Shea Salinas (97:34) scored a match-winning goal on July 15, 2020, in the MLS is Back Group Stage against the Vancouver Whitecaps.
Portland Timbers – Kristoffer Velde
Among players currently on the Timbers roster, Velde leads Portland in both goals (eight) and assists (nine).

With another assist, Velde would become the fifth player in club history have 10+ assists in a single MLS regular season, joining Diego Valeri (five), Sebastian Blanco (twice), Evander and Santiago Moreno.
MATCH PREDICTION: SJ EARTHQUAKES WIN

San Jose are unbeaten in their last four games with Portland (W3 D1) across all competitions, including a 3-1 win away from home in May. The Earthquakes have never swept the season series, while the four-match unbeaten run is their longest in the fixture since the Timbers joined MLS in 2011.

The Earthquakes' 12 victories this season are their most wins in a single season since the team's 13-win campaign in 2019. After having 11 wins in 2025, it marks the first time San Jose have recorded double-digit wins in back-to-back seasons since 2012 and 2013.

Portland, meanwhile, have failed to record a clean sheet on the road this regular season, one of four MLS teams without one. The Timbers have never gone a full MLS regular season without a road clean sheet after equalling their club record with five during the 2025 season.
Portland Timbers – 27.3%

1i1sr8r1omutk154g1rmdpvz1g.title: Saka: Scars still remain from England's World Cup defeat to Argentina
1i1sr8r1omutk154g1rmdpvz1g.subtitle: England are preparing to begin their Nations League campaign, but Bukayo Saka said their World Cup exit was still fresh in the memory.
paragraphs: Bukayo Saka believes England's players are still scarred from their heartbreaking defeat to Argentina in the semi-finals of this summer's World Cup.
England were on the brink of reaching the World Cup final for the first time since winning the tournament in 1966, after Anthony Gordon's 55th-minute strike gave them the lead.
However, a Lionel Messi-orchestrated comeback saw Argentina score two goals in seven minutes late on to end the Three Lions' dreams of lifting the trophy.
Argentina were trailing until the 85th minute against England, the latest a team has been behind but gone on to win in normal time in a World Cup semi-final.
The Three Lions did, however, achieve their second-best finish at the World Cup after beating France in a thrilling third-place match, with Saka scoring a hat-trick in a 6-4 win.

1ipyu2d1qzq1m1o208cjvigsew.title: Konate withdraws from France squad, Yoro called up
1ipyu2d1qzq1m1o208cjvigsew.subtitle: Ibrahima Konate has suffered a minor injury which has ruled him out of France's first four Nations League matches/
paragraphs: Ibrahima Konate has withdrawn from France's Nations League squad through injury, with Leny Yoro receiving his first call-up to the senior squad.
Konate felt pain in his right knee during Wednesday's training session and underwent an MRI.
He has been diagnosed with a minor sprain and released back to Real Madrid, for whom he has made seven appearances in all competitions since moving from Liverpool.
Following his withdrawal, Zidane has called on Manchester United's Yoro, who had initially been called up to the Under-21s squad.
Yoro is the seventh uncapped player in Zidane's France squad and will link up with the team to fly to Turkiye on Thursday.
The 20-year-old has had a mixed start to the season with United, making just two starts in all competitions – neither of which came in the Premier League.
He started their Champions League thrashing of Sabah and the EFL Cup loss to Brighton, but has played just 22 minutes in the top-flight, with both of his appearances coming from the bench.
Yoro could make his France debut against Turkiye on Friday, with Les Bleus also set to take on Belgium twice, on either side of their clash with Italy.

1iyf7aju7687szj7i373ue45u.title: Joao Felix confident goals will come under new Portugal boss Jesus
1iyf7aju7687szj7i373ue45u.subtitle: Jorge Jesus began his Portugal tenure with a win over Wales in the Nations League, and Joao Felix is excited about what the future holds.
paragraphs: Joao Felix believes it is only a matter of time before Portugal find their shooting boots under new boss Jorge Jesus after they beat Wales 1-0 in the Nations League on Thursday.
Jesus was taking charge of Portugal for the first time following Roberto Martinez's departure, and his team made a blistering start to the match at Estadio Jose Alvalade.
Portugal eventually took the lead in the 22nd minute through Joao Felix, who picked out the bottom-left corner from outside the box after good work from full-back Nuno Mendes.
Cristiano Ronaldo spurned two chances at the end of a dominant first half that saw Portugal register 13 shots, their most in the opening 45 minutes of a game since November 2025 against Armenia (17).

Ronaldo should have doubled Portugal's lead early in the second half, but he could only turn Ruben Neves' delivery over the crossbar, with the five-time Ballon d'Or winner then seeing a goal ruled out for offside soon after.

But the Selecao were made to work for their win, with Wales coming on strong as the match progressed. Brennan Johnson lifted an effort onto the crossbar, with Ruben Dias on hand to clear Lewis Koumas' rebound off the line.

Portugal are now unbeaten in their last 10 home matches in all competitions (W9 D1), while in competitive games it’s 13 unbeaten since a 1-0 defeat to Spain in September 2022 (W12 D1), and Joao Felix is confident things will only get better under Jesus.
"We knew it wasn't going to be an easy game. Wales are a good team," Joao Felix told Sport TV. "The first game under a new coach is always difficult.
"We had very little time to work on the coach's game patterns, but I think that, overall, we played a great game and we deserve to be commended.
"I think we could see our dynamic, very attacking football, high pressing, without giving the opponent any space to breathe.
"We had 13 shots before half-time, which is a lot for the first half. I don't remember a single clear chance for them, when we had several.
"That's what people can expect. Attacking football, pressing, not letting opponents breathe and creating chances.
"We only scored one today, but in the next few games, if we continue like this, we will surely score more."

Joao Felix has now scored five goals across his last 10 starts for Portugal, while each of his last two goals have come from outside the box, as many as his first 11 for the national team, and he looks set to play a big role under Jesus.
The 26-year-old has worked with Jesus before at Al-Nassr, scoring 20 goals in 33 appearances on their way to the Saudi Pro League title in 2025-26.
Jesus made the decision to deploy Joao Felix in the second striker position, just behind Ronaldo and with Bruno Fernandes, Vitinha and Pedro Neto around him.
"I've always been myself; I always tried to do my best for the team, no matter what position I was playing," Joao Felix added.
"As I've always said, my position is right here, as a second striker. If this is the case, there is a much higher chance that things will go well.
"This is what happened last year. Today, the whole team delivered a good performance, and that's where I can help them the most."
It proved to be a frustrating match for Ronaldo, whose seven shots without scoring is his most in a game since a World Cup qualifier against Republic of Ireland in October 2025 (also seven).
Ronaldo was replaced by Goncalo Ramos in the 67th minute, and Jesus said the decision to substitute the Portugal captain was pre-planned.

"I took him out 25 minutes before the end of the game because I thought it was important to have a fresh player on the pitch who was able to defend with pressure and not let the central defenders of Wales build the game," Jesus said.
"I wanted to have a player at the first line with speed, and I knew that Goncalo Ramos could do that.
"I knew that Cris could stay a little longer, five to 10 minutes. But I would have taken him out anyway. I planned it."
