1jdlty23ofll61aneb4fxs4e83.title: Schmetzer senses positive momentum after end to Seattle's winless run
1jdlty23ofll61aneb4fxs4e83.subtitle: The Seattle Sounders finally ended their 13-game winless run in MLS this week, and they have a home match against Minnesota United next up.
paragraphs: Brian Schmetzer already believed the Seattle Sounders were building some momentum even before they ended their four-month wait for a victory on Wednesday, as they look to go back-to-back against Minnesota United.
The Sounders went 13 games without victory after beating the San Jose Earthquakes on May 13, prior to the World Cup break.

They lost eight straight matches before turning the corner somewhat by drawing five in a row, prior to overcoming Real Salt Lake – who are also on a long winless streak of their own – by a 2-0 scoreline in midweek.
Now only outside the playoff spots on games won in the Western Conference, Seattle will look to inject some more impetus at home to Minnesota on Saturday.
But Schmetzer believes they were already on an upward trajectory of sorts, saying: "Well, I think we've already been starting to build – the five draws have been something.
"It's been a long time – May 13, for the guys that are publishing the facts. I think all the people in this room are good reporters. There's no fake news in here!
"I told those guys in there to enjoy the moment. And on a personal note, there were fans behind the bench saying, 'Congratulations Brian, enjoy this moment'.

"So I listened to those fans, and I told the same thing to the guys in there. I think we've been building some momentum, but this really gives them a lot of belief and that’s what we discussed before the game."
Minnesota are second from bottom in the West, albeit only three points behind the Sounders, after losing four straight games.

Their most recent defeat came by a 3-2 scoreline against the LA Galaxy last weekend, and if the Loons are to make a late push for the postseason, head coach Cameron Knowles knows it will take a collective effort.
"We're going to need everyone. We need everyone to push, whether it's in training during the week or whether it's coming into a game," he said.
"We need guys to step up and everyone to give exactly what they're capable of. Everyone in that locker room has shown they're capable of contributing."
PLAYERS TO WATCH
Seattle Sounders – Paul Arriola
Arriola assisted both Seattle goals against RSL on Wednesday, while he also had a joint-game-high three shots and the only Opta-defined 'big' chance of the match.
He also scored his first MLS goal for the Sounders earlier this month, to salvage a point against the Galaxy in a 1-1 draw on September 12.
Minnesota United – Kelvin Yeboah
Only Lionel Messi (20), Petar Musa (18), Brian White and Sam Surridge (16 each) have scored more goals in MLS this year than Yeboah's 14.
The Minnesota forward – who was on target against the Galaxy last weekend – also ranks third in the league for expected goals (14.6 xG), only behind Messi (17.2) and White (16.1).
MATCH PREDICTION: SEATTLE SOUNDERS WIN
When these two sides last met in MLS action, they played out a 0-0 draw at Allianz Field in March.
All of a sudden, Seattle's club-record winless streak has turned into a six-game unbeaten run, even if they did play out five draws in that time.
And they are the Opta supercomputer's favourites for this one, with Minnesota only managing one win in their last six MLS games (D1 L4).

Away from home, the Loons have lost their last two matches while conceding a total of nine goals (5-4 at Portland Timbers, 4-2 at St. Louis City SC), so without a big defensive improvement, they could be up against it.
Seattle Sounders – 45.8%
Minnesota United – 30.5%

1k04g4etmfgnl19sy429smr8pm.title: Carrick understands jeers from Man Utd fans after Mainoo substitution
1k04g4etmfgnl19sy429smr8pm.subtitle: Manchester United's travelling fans made their feelings known when Kobbie Mainoo was substituted with 10 minutes to play against Fulham.
paragraphs: Michael Carrick understands the "emotional" reactions to Manchester United's recent struggles, after his decision to withdraw Kobbie Mainoo against Fulham was booed by their travelling fans.
With just five points on the board after five games, United have made their joint-worst start to a Premier League campaign, having also taken five at this stage of 2014-15.

Things could have been worse for the Red Devils at Craven Cottage on Sunday, too, as Matheus Cunha's deflected strike snatched a point in the 89th minute, after Lisandro Martinez's calamitous own goal had put them on the back foot.
With United 1-0 down and chasing the game, Carrick's choice to replace Mainoo with Mason Mount in the 80th minute was loudly jeered by the away end.
Mainoo had completed 64 of his 68 passes, 27 of which were in the final third, with only Bryan Mbeumo (100%) and Harry Maguire (95.8%) bettering his 94.1% pass accuracy among United's starters.
But Carrick feels that reaction came from a place of frustration and understands the disgruntled feeling among the fanbase.
"There are always going to be certain reactions when you're making changes," Carrick said. "I've spoken to Kobbie after the game and he's absolutely fine.
"I understand at times when we are chasing the game, everyone's a little bit emotional. The supporters are – as they should be – desperate for us to do the right thing.
"But I don't take any negatives or offence to it. I think we've just got to try and keep doing the right things to get back into the game.
"The supporters were unbelievable, I have to say, all the way through. They stuck with the boys and supported them.
"At least we've given them something small at the end to take from it, and I'm sure there's more to come."

With United 12th in the Premier League table going into the extended international break, the Opta supercomputer only assigns them a 17% chance of qualifying for the Champions League, but Carrick is sure there are plenty of twists and turns ahead.
"It's still a big season ahead," Carrick said. "It's a long season, and you're going to have these spells through a season. That's part of the journey. It's not a sprint; it's a long effort.
"I'm not playing it down. We wanted more points, so I'm not saying everything's great. I understand the frustration. We wanted to be better, and we wanted to do other things.
"But deflation is certainly not what we have within the club and within the group. The players didn't have that on the pitch, and that's what will carry us through the season, without a doubt."
United face Tottenham, who are still winless and prop up the table, in their next Premier League game on October 10.

1krsbncizt2sz1vrqelj0p9i2y.title: Norway 3-2 Denmark: Haaland brace decides Scandinavian scuffle in Nations League
1krsbncizt2sz1vrqelj0p9i2y.subtitle: Erling Haaland carried his World Cup and Premier League form into the 2026-27 Nations League, as Norway downed rivals Denmark 3-2.
paragraphs: Erling Haaland scored twice as Norway opened their Nations League campaign with an entertaining 3-2 win over Denmark, despite finishing the game with 10 men.

Having trailed 2-0 after just 18 minutes, Denmark fought back valiantly to level Thursday's matchup between Scandinavian rivals, but Haaland's second goal proved to be the winner, with the hosts surviving a late red card for David Moller Wolfe.

Two of Norway's other Premier League stars combined to give them the advantage in the 14th minute, as Oscar Bobb took in Martin Odegaard's cute pass, then shaped a curling finish around Denmark defender Oliver Provstgaard and into the far corner.

And Norway did not have to wait long for their second goal, as Antonio Nusa skipped infield and played a clever reverse pass in behind for Haaland, whose driven finish went straight through Filip Jorgensen.

Denmark found a route back into the contest in the 25th minute, with Mikkel Damsgaard's free-kick dipping over the Norway wall and beating Orjan Nyland, though only a superb reflex stop from Jorgensen prevented Patrick Berg from making it 3-1 late in the first half.
And the visitors drew level on the hour mark, with Rasmus Hojlund reacting quickest to nod home when Nyland blocked Morten Hjulmand's downward header from a corner.

But Haaland re-established Norway's lead when he lashed inside the near post following a well-worked corner routine that saw Odegaard receive a short pass from Nusa, reach the byline, and cut the ball back for the Manchester City talisman.
Moller Wolfe received his second yellow card three minutes into stoppage time, having blocked Gustav Isaksen's run down the right as Denmark chased another equaliser, but Norway held on.
New Nations League campaign, same old Haaland
Haaland's staggering form was one of the stories of this summer's World Cup, as he almost single-handedly powered Norway into the quarter-finals with seven goals in five games.

And he picked up where he left off at the start of their Nations League Group A4 campaign, scoring twice from a game-high five shots (four of which were on target), although his goals were hardly put on a plate, with all those efforts adding up to 0.35 expected goals (xG).
Haaland has now scored in 10 of his last 13 competitive games for Norway and Man City combined (16 goals in total), and in each of his last six (nine goals).

He last enjoyed a longer run between August and October 2025, going 12 straight matches with a goal. With two meetings against Cristiano Ronaldo's Portugal to come during this international break, either side of a trip to Wales, Stale Solbakken will be desperate to see that streak continue.

Moller Wolfe received his second yellow card three minutes into stoppage time, having blocked Gustav Isaksen's run down the right as Denmark chased another equaliser, but Norway held on.

New Nations League campaign, same old Haaland

Haaland's staggering form was one of the stories of this summer's World Cup, as he almost single-handedly powered Norway into the quarter-finals with seven goals in five games.

And he picked up where he left off at the start of their Nations League Group A4 campaign, scoring twice from a game-high five shots (four of which were on target), although his goals were hardly put on a plate, with all those efforts adding up to 0.35 expected goals (xG). 

Haaland has now scored in 10 of his last 13 competitive games for Norway and Man City combined (16 goals in total), and in each of his last six (nine goals).

He last enjoyed a longer run between August and October 2025, going 12 straight matches with a goal. With two meetings against Cristiano Ronaldo's Portugal to come during this international break, either side of a trip to Wales, Stale Solbakken will be desperate to see that streak continue.

1lt0gsy8rcp0m114v5x2uuvnoz.title: Amorim vows not to repeat Man Utd errors with Milan
1lt0gsy8rcp0m114v5x2uuvnoz.subtitle: AC Milan's unbeaten start in Serie A under Ruben Amorim rolled on, and he intends to continue allowing his team to play with freedom.
paragraphs: Ruben Amorim insists he will not be pushed into making the same tactical mistakes he made during his stint with Manchester United, now he is in charge of AC Milan.
Amorim's unbeaten start in Serie A continued on Sunday with a comfortable 3-0 win against Lecce at San Siro, with the result moving Milan up to fifth in the standings.
Christian Pulisic's sensational touch and finish put Milan ahead early on, before Adrien Rabiot and Diego Moreira sealed the win for the Rossoneri during a dominant second half.
Milan's victory saw them remain unbeaten in their opening five Serie A matches of a season for the first time since 2022-23 (W3 D2).

Amorim (W3 D2) has become only the third foreign manager in Milan's history to not taste defeat in each of his first five Serie A games in charge, after Luis Carniglia (W3 D2) and Nils Liedholm (W4 D1), both in 1963-64.

Speaking after the game, Amorim revealed he allowed his side to play with "freedom", and when asked about the reasoning behind that decision, he highlighted his turbulent tenure at Old Trafford, where he was reluctant to adapt his style of play.
"It's an observation of the games and the characteristics," Amorim told DAZN, as quoted by Football Italia.

"Of course, I listen to the players, but a manager, especially in a big team, is always listening to the players, seeing and understanding them, but every player wants to push the game towards their characteristics, and if you want to have an identity, that is hard.
"It's always my decision. What I felt in the last games is the same that I felt at Manchester United, and I cannot make the same mistake.
"Sometimes we don't have the perfect characteristics to play in that way, and if we don't have them, we have to adapt. I think today worked.
"In another game, we can return to the build-up with three [at the back]. The important thing is to have different ways of playing.

"That's especially important in Italy, because the managers are really smart, they mark really well one against one, and when they lose the reference to what we want to do, it's harder for them to understand their mobility, just as they make it harder for me to understand their teams."

Milan have now won their first two home Serie A matches of a season while keeping a clean sheet in both for the first time since 2020-21, when they beat Bologna 2-0 and Spezia 3-0 under Stefano Pioli.

Their dominance was backed up by the underlying metrics, too. They finished with an expected goals (xG) total of 1.93 from their 10 attempts, while also restricting Lecce to a measly xG total of 0.17 from six shots.
It was a much-needed victory heading into the international break, with Milan coming into the clash with Lecce without a win in three matches in all competitions (D2 L1).
Roma, Inter and Lazio are the early pace setters in the division, all sitting two points clear of Milan, and Amorim feels his team are on the right track.
"If you look at the way we play, Roma and Inter had more time as a team, you can see the patterns are there," Amorim added.
"We didn't lose so many points, we dropped two to Lazio and Juventus away, so not everything is bad.

"Sometimes it looks like that, especially after recent results, but we have to see the balance. We won today against a good team that is doing well, but it is a different team, and sometimes we will have issues.
"It's a process, I think we should have more points, as against Juventus we weren't playing so well, but we were 30 seconds off getting three points.
"Even against Lazio, if you look at the balance of the game, I feel we deserved a little bit more."

1m9ymt7iknsn317sgev2gjguoq.title: Man Utd striker Sesko withdraws from Slovenia squad due to shin issue
1m9ymt7iknsn317sgev2gjguoq.subtitle: A shin injury troubled Benjamin Sesko at the end of last season, and a flare-up of the issue has ruled him out of Slovenia's upcoming games.
paragraphs: Manchester United have confirmed striker Benjamin Sesko must undergo tests after withdrawing from the Slovenia squad with a shin injury.
Sesko was a notable absentee as United drew 1-1 with Fulham on Sunday, with Matheus Cunha's deflected strike salvaging a point for the Red Devils following Lisandro Martinez's calamitous own goal.
Having joined from RB Leipzig in a £74m deal last August, Sesko scored 12 goals in 32 appearances across all competitions last term.
That tally was only matched by Bryan Mbeumo among his Red Devils team-mates, despite 13 of Sesko's outings coming from the bench.
The 23-year-old missed the final few games of 2025-26, however, as well as United's entire pre-season campaign, with a shin problem.
Sesko has played six times for Michael Carrick's side this season, scoring twice, though he has only started twice – against Sabah in the Champions League and Brighton in the EFL Cup.
In the aftermath of last week's cup defeat to Brighton, Carrick revealed that the same issue was bothering Sesko again, and he has now withdrawn from Slovenia's squad.
Sesko was initially named in Bostjan Cesar's party for Nations League fixtures against Scotland – who they will face home and away – plus North Macedonia and Switzerland.
In a medical update released on Monday, United said: "Benjamin will undergo tests this week before defining his individual recovery plan."
Sesko has almost three weeks of recovery time if he is to feature in United's next Premier League game, against bottom club Tottenham on October 10.
They also face Leeds United, Bournemouth and Chelsea in the league next month, having made their joint-worst start to a Premier League season through five matchdays (also five points in 2014-15).

1muk7ea3o972z15gjzre3t9mhj.title: Kane and Bayern 'fairly close' to agreeing new contract
1muk7ea3o972z15gjzre3t9mhj.subtitle: Harry Kane is keen to extend his stay at Bayern Munich and is in talks over a reported two-year extension with the Bundesliga giants.
paragraphs: Harry Kane hinted his Bayern Munich contract renewal is "fairly close" and could be announced soon.
Kane joined Bayern from Tottenham in August 2023 and has gone from strength to strength with the Bundesliga giants, winning two straight titles and a DFB-Pokal trophy.
He has also written his name into the Bundesliga history books this term, having netted his 100th and 101st goals in the competition last time out in a 7-0 hammering of Union Berlin.
Kane reached the 100-goal landmark in his 98th appearance, making him the quickest player to hit that tally, smashing Dieter Muller's previous record of 129 games.
Overall, the England captain has netted 152 goals in 154 appearances, and in 2025-26 alone, he scored a whopping 64 times in all competitions (including the Club World Cup).
Kane's current contract is due to run out at the end of this season, but a new deal – reportedly through to June 2029 – is in the works.
"We're in good talks. We're fairly close," Kane told The Independent.
"There's still some things that we need to iron out. I'm happy there. I think it won't be too long before there's some sort of announcement."
Bayern are chasing a third straight Bundesliga title this term and are also among the favourites to clinch the Champions League.
They went into the international break second in the German top-flight, behind Borussia Dortmund, but Kane is excited to see what the team can achieve.
"I feel really comfortable in the team, with the coach, the environment," Kane added. "I want to just be at this level and push this level for as long as possible.
"Especially as you're getting a bit older, if you don't have a great season somewhere, or you don't play as well, the drop-off is maybe more than what it would have been when you're younger.
"So, it's just about extracting as much as I can, with the boss there, with the players I have in the team, I think they're getting the best out of me. I'm helping them as well."

1oo6jjpc45ake1uj9k7ei6gwnd.title: Colwill expects Chelsea to be better after international break
1oo6jjpc45ake1uj9k7ei6gwnd.subtitle: Chelsea's strong start to the season fizzled out before the international break, but Levi Colwill is confident they can improve after it.
paragraphs: Levi Colwill has backed Chelsea to come out on the other side of the international break "flying".
Chelsea made a strong start to life under Xabi Alonso, winning four of their first five matches across all competitions (L1).

However, having had to come from behind to draw 2-2 with high-flying Hull City, the Blues were then thrashed 3-0 by Brentford in their final match before the extended international break to leave them winless in three league games.
Chelsea have already lost more Premier League matches in 2026 (11) than they did in the entirety of 2025 (10).

Alonso became only the sixth Premier League boss to see his side concede at least two goals in each of his first five games, after Mick McCarthy, Sammy Lee, Terry Connor, Slavisa Jokanovic, and Scott Parker.

And Chelsea's defensive woes have been highlighted on multiple occasions, even before Alonso's appointment; since the start of last season, they have conceded 23 Premier League goals from non-penalty set-pieces, now the joint-most of any side, along with Bournemouth.
Colwill admitted the start of the season was not what Chelsea expected, but he wants to use the extended international break to get back on track.
"[There have been] some good bits, some other not so good bits," he said, as quoted by Chelsea's website.
"Luckily, we've got a while now to try and improve.
"Hopefully, we will come out the other side flying, pick up our play, and become a better team."
Chelsea return to action at home to Bournemouth on October 10.

1ozwcpqd6jbfw1jzlxdbbxe577.title: Chelsea 1-0 Austria Wien: Bompastor's side survive scare in Women's Champions League opener
1ozwcpqd6jbfw1jzlxdbbxe577.subtitle: Wieke Kaptein's early goal was enough for Chelsea to see off Austria Wien, but it was from a convincing display from Sonia Bompastor's side.
paragraphs: Chelsea began their Women's Champions League campaign with a nervy win as Wieke Kaptein's first-half stunner sealed a 1-0 victory over tournament debutants Austria Wien.
The Blues looked far from the team that reached the quarter-finals of the competition in 2025-26, but a moment of individual quality was enough to get them over the line.

Chelsea needed just 11 minutes to take the lead through Kaptein. Katharina Schiechtl's tackle on Melvine Malard saw the ball drop kindly to the midfielder, who took a touch before crashing her shot in off the crossbar from the edge of the box.
Sonia Bompastor was forced into making an early change as Keira Walsh left the field with an injury, but the Blues continued where they left off in their search for a second.
The lively Alyssa Thompson drilled a shot just wide of the left post following a driving run down the right, but Wien had their chances to level things up going into the break.
Virginia Kirchberger could only turn over after Modesta Uka's wicked delivery was spilled by Livia Peng before Louise Schoffel's effort whistled past the bottom-left corner.

Wien grew in confidence as the second half wore on as Uka's shot on the swivel was repelled by Peng, with the Chelsea goalkeeper then on hand to thwart Valentina Potzl after Veerle Buurman had played herself into trouble.

The visitors continued to get closer and closer to levelling things up, with Uka chopping inside before curling her attempt onto the post, but Wien were unable to find the equaliser their performance merited in the closing stages.
Chelsea ride their luck

Ahead of kick-off, Bompastor stressed the need for her Chelsea team to be more clinical, having stumbled to a 2-0 victory against Birmingham City in the Women's Super League last weekend, and once again her team looked vulnerable at both ends of the pitch.

In what was a historic match for Wien, becoming the fourth Austrian side to participate in the competition after Neulengbach, St. Polten and Sturm Graz, they announced their arrival on the European stage in some style, and were extremely unlucky not to leave with at least a point.

Uka was the particular standout for the visitors. She finished with team-high totals for shots (five), touches in the opposition box (seven), crosses (six) and attempted dribbles (three), while also coming within inches of scoring an equaliser in the second half.

The Blues were, however, able to hold on to begin their campaign with a win. They finished with an expected goals (xG) total of 1.43 from their 13 attempts compared to Wien's 0.87 from two more shots at Peng's net.
Bompastor will be hoping for improvements in the WSL this weekend, but things do not get any easier, with London rivals and two-time Champions League winners Arsenal their next opponents this Sunday.
Elsewhere, there was no such trouble for last year's runners-up Lyon, who thumped Servette 8-0, with Marie-Antoinette Katoto scoring a hat-trick at Stade de Geneve.

Defending champions Barcelona also got their campaign up and running with a win. They came from a goal down to beat Paris FC 5-2, with Caroline Graham Hansen and Ewa Pajor starring in the turnaround. Roma, meanwhile, played out a 0-0 draw with OH Leuven.

1pdab9mi3roft1tudzxduqx8gf.title: Xavi promises 'intensity and passion' in new-look Netherlands approach
1pdab9mi3roft1tudzxduqx8gf.subtitle: Xavi will take charge of the Netherlands for the first time this international break, and he is preparing his team for a new approach.
paragraphs: Xavi has promised to bring "intensity, passion and a good rhythm" to the Netherlands' play as he prepares to take charge for the first time.
The Spaniard was named as the Oranje's head coach on a four-year deal after Ronald Koeman left in the wake of a disappointing World Cup campaign over the summer.
While the Netherlands enjoyed an unbeaten group stage, they fell at the first hurdle in the knockouts, losing on penalties to Morocco.
Xavi, a former World Cup winner with Spain, will face Germany in his first game in charge in Amsterdam on Thursday, as the Netherlands kick off their Nations League campaign.

Koeman was criticised at times for taking a defensive approach with his tactics, and while Xavi did not give away too many hints about his approach, he outlined what he expects from his players on Monday.
"Everything is new ​for me and for the staff, so it will first be to get to know each other, ​know all the players, insist or convince them about our way to play," Xavi told reporters.
"We don't have too much time. But no excuses; every coach is in the same situation.

"I want to explain the values that ​we want from the squad. I want to show them that I'm open to them; I want ​to help them. I want to enjoy the process with them. We want to create a family; we want ‌to ⁠create a big group.
"The players must come to the national team with happiness, but at the end, the main goal is to win.

"You cannot promise results, but ​we will work ⁠for results. I can promise that we will play with intensity, with passion, with a good rhythm, trying to be competitive and trying to ​take the initiative in the game. This is for sure.
"There's going ​to be ⁠a different way of playing. I don't want to compare, and I don't want to talk about the past. I respect Ronald a lot. But I'm focused on the present."
Virgil van Dijk will remain the Netherlands' captain, having revealed on Sunday that he plans to keep representing his national team until Euro 2028.
"It ​was a really good meeting," Xavi said of meeting Van Dijk in Liverpool to discuss his Netherlands future.
"He was very honest. He has the capacity to continue. He's a good leader. He's positive, ​he's motivated. He's ready to be the leader."

1qjt6hutsp8xs131lm5v95llkq.title: Palmer and Rice withdraw from England squad as Gibbs-White, Garner come in
1qjt6hutsp8xs131lm5v95llkq.subtitle: Thomas Tuchel will be without Declan Rice, Cole Palmer and Marcus Rashford for England's upcoming Nations League fixtures.
paragraphs: Cole Palmer and Declan Rice are part of a quintet of players who have withdrawn from England duty.
Palmer, who missed out on England's World Cup squad, was selected by Thomas Tuchel for the Three Lions' upcoming Nations League matches.
He has already registered four Premier League goal involvements this season (two goals, two assists).
However, the Chelsea playmaker has now opted out of the squad as he nurses an injury.
It is the same case for Rice, Marcus Rashford, Tino Livramento and Kobbie Mainoo.
Tuchel has called up Morgan Gibbs-White and James Garner as replacements.
No player has scored more Premier League goals in 2026 than Nottingham Forest attacker Gibbs-White (13, level with Erling Haaland).

Garner, meanwhile, made his England debut during the March international window, and impressed against Uruguay and Japan, but the Everton midfielder ultimately missed out on a call-up for the World Cup.
The pair will now get a chance to impress in fixtures against world champions Spain, with a double-header against Czechia following, either side of a clash with Croatia.

1qojeh2n1l0bn1lthi9ii0jc3a.title: 'No gameplan and no ideas' – Makelele slams Mourinho's Madrid after derby defeat
1qojeh2n1l0bn1lthi9ii0jc3a.subtitle: Jose Mourinho criticised Ortiz Arias after Real Madrid's loss to Atletico Madrid, but Claude Makelele says the referee was not to blame.
paragraphs: Ex-Real Madrid midfielder Claude Makelele did not hold back on his former team's performance in their derby defeat to Atletico Madrid, saying they had "no gameplan and no ideas."
Madrid slipped to a 2-1 loss against their cross-city rivals on Sunday, their second in the first seven games of their LaLiga campaign.
With defending champions Barcelona making a perfect start, Los Blancos are already six points off the title pace, and Makelele feels there are glaring issues in their side.

During Sunday's game, Madrid only managed eight shots and 0.3 expected goals, compared to Atleti's 18 attempts and 2.35 xG, though that latter figure was boosted by the penalty from which Alejandro Grimaldo opened the scoring early in the second half.

Dean Huijsen was sent off and conceded that spot-kick for denying Giuliano Simeone a clear goalscoring opportunity, though Madrid had been flat in attack even with 11 men on the pitch, only posting 0.16 xG and one shot on target in the first half.
And Makelele, who represented Madrid 145 times between 2000 and 2003, before working under Mourinho at Chelsea, was bemused by their lacklustre display.
"There is no understanding between the players, nor with the coach. Mourinho must talk to them," he told ESPN.
"The team is weak, there is no gameplan and no clear ideas. There is nothing. Nothing, nothing, nothing... Absolutely nothing. We must demand more from them."

In stark contrast to Madrid's stuttering performance, Atleti scored their second goal – via Jonathan David – at the end of an 18-pass move – the most for any goal scored by either team in a Madrid derby in LaLiga since at least 2005-06.

Afterwards, Mourinho said "the story of the game" was an inept refereeing performance from Ortiz Arias, arguing both Lee Kang-in and Cristian Romero should have seen red for Atleti, the former for a high challenge on Federico Valverde and the latter for treading on Jude Bellingham.
Mourinho brought printed images of both incidents to his post-match press conference, prompting Atleti to hit back on social media, posting: "Stop referee harassment now."
But Makelele was not interested in playing the blame game, saying: "The problem is not the referee; there is an obvious deficiency in the team."
After the extended international break, Madrid host Villarreal in LaLiga on October 10, before visiting Roma in the Champions League four days later.

1swnm130vactq13ofzh6lz9vl9.title: Sunderland hand Le Fee new five-year contract
1swnm130vactq13ofzh6lz9vl9.subtitle: Having helped Sunderland qualify for the Europa League and scored their first European goal in 53 years, Enzo Le Fee has penned a new deal.
paragraphs: Sunderland's creative midfielder Enzo Le Fee has signed a new five-year contract with the club.
Le Fee joined the Black Cats on loan from Roma in January 2025, with that deal containing a purchase obligation if they were to be promoted from the Championship.
The Frenchman immediately assumed a key role under Regis Le Bris, starting in a 2-1 play-off final victory over Sheffield United, which led to him becoming a permanent Sunderland player for £19m.
And he has continued to shine in the Premier League, making 41 appearances in the competition while scoring six goals and providing seven assists.

His 13 goal involvements and 61 chances created are both team-high totals since the start of 2025-26, and those figures helped propel Sunderland to a seventh-place finish and Europa League qualification last term.
Last week, Le Fee scored from the penalty spot to secure a 1-0 victory over AZ at the Stadium of Light, in Sunderland's opening match in that competition.

That made him the Black Cats' first goalscorer in Europe since October 1973, when Micky Horswill scored their second goal in a 2-1 victory at home to Sporting CP in the Cup Winners' Cup, only for the Lisbon giants to recover in the return fixture and progress 3-2 on aggregate.
"I'm really happy to have signed a new contract with Sunderland," Le Fee told the club's website, having agreed fresh terms to run until 2031.
"From the moment I arrived, I've felt the passion of the supporters and the ambition of everyone at the club – I've loved my time here.
"We've achieved something special together over the past couple of seasons, but I believe this is just the beginning.
"I feel very settled here and I'm excited to continue developing, competing at the highest level and helping the club move forward.
"I'm very proud to wear the Sunderland shirt and I can't wait to see what we can achieve together in the years ahead."

Having lost 5-3 to Manchester City in a thrilling encounter prior to the international break, Sunderland have four points from five Premier League games this season, with Brighton their next opponents on October 10.

1t4mz1zeypxyb1g5ybxdunw0es.title: Cucurella reveals attempt to try and tempt Rodri to join Real Madrid
1t4mz1zeypxyb1g5ybxdunw0es.subtitle: Rodri was of interest to Real Madrid before joining Barcelona, with Marc Cucurella saying he tried to tempt him to the Spanish capital.
paragraphs: Marc Cucurella revealed he sent Rodri a "subtle message" to join him at Real Madrid this summer before the midfielder opted to join Clasico rivals Barcelona.
Cucurella was a part of a summer rebuild at Madrid, with the Spanish international joining Los Blancos for a reported €55m (£47.5m) transfer fee from Chelsea.
The likes of Yan Diomande, Ibrahima Konate, Denzel Dumfries and Bernardo Silva also moved to the Spanish capital, with Rodri another player linked with a move to Madrid.
However, Rodri decided against linking up with Jose Mourinho and instead joined Hansi Flick at Barcelona, signing for a reported €76.5m (£65m) from Manchester City.
Cucurella and Rodri's moves came after helping Spain to the second World Cup crown this summer, with the latter scooping the Golden Ball along the way for his performances.
Spain are preparing for their first match since beating Argentina in the final, with England their opponents in the first match of their Nations League campaign this Saturday.
But speaking ahead of their trip to Wembley Stadium, Cucurella said that he openly tried to sway Rodri's decision in an attempt to play alongside him at club level.
"I don't really like pressuring or influencing team-mates," Cucurella said. "These are personal things.
"It's true that I sent him a subtle message, before the news broke, saying I hoped we'd become team-mates.
"He replied, but didn't give anything away. I'm happy for him [at Barca], though I hope he doesn't have too much success."
Rodri has enjoyed a perfect start to life with Barcelona, helping the Blaugrana begin their LaLiga title defence with seven wins from seven matches so far.

Only Pau Cubarsi (456), Eric Garcia (393), Pedri (391) and Gerard Martin (378) have completed more successful passes in the league for Barcelona than Rodri (368), while he also ranks third in Flick's squad for tackles won (eight).

Barcelona have started a LaLiga season with seven wins in their first seven games for the fourth time, after doing so in 2013-14, 2017-18 and 2024-25, and they already find themselves six points ahead of Madrid in the table.
Madrid lost their second league game of the season last Sunday, going down 2-1 to city rivals Atletico Madrid after Dean Huijsen was sent off early in the second half.
Mourinho is already coming under pressure early in his second stint in the Madrid dugout, though Cucurella believes his team are more than capable of turning things around.
"We didn't finish the period before the break in the best way," Cucurella added. "It's all a process, but the important thing is to build a solid foundation.
"Let's see if we can find a good balance and build a strong, united group. If the season ends the way we all want it to, no one will remember the start."

1txtajxy2emvc142q1fpyttcl5.title: Luis Enrique not taking Classique triumph for granted
1txtajxy2emvc142q1fpyttcl5.subtitle: Marquinhos struck the winner as Paris Saint-Germain overcame Marseille in Sunday's matchup between France's two most successful clubs.
paragraphs: Luis Enrique said Paris Saint-Germain can never take a win over Classique rivals Marseille for granted, after they battled to a 2-1 success at the Stade Velodrome.
Marquinhos' 74th-minute strike settled the contest as PSG claimed back-to-back Ligue 1 victories, having started their campaign with three winless games.
The Brazilian's goal came just two minutes after Angel Gomes got Marseille back on level terms, with that strike also coming hot on the heels of Ferran Torres' opener.
Marseille had captain Timothy Weah sent off shortly after going 2-1 down, with the United States international hauling Nuno Mendes down from behind while already on a yellow card.

PSG have now won 10 of their last 14 away Ligue 1 games against Marseille (D3 D1), though Nayef Aguerd missed a huge chance to snatch a point for OM deep into stoppage time, as he headed wide on the stretch.
And Luis Enrique says three points will never come easily for any visiting side at the Velodrome.
"It was the match we had planned for, with a lot of difficulties. Everyone said it would be easy, but playing at the Velodrome is not an easy thing," he told Ligue 1+.
"We tried to play, we created fewer chances in the first half because the opponent defended very well. In the second half, everything changed, we made a very good effort."

The result piles more pressure on Bruno Genesio, who is the first Marseille boss to lose four of his first five league games in charge of the club since the duo of Willy Kohut and Andre Gascard in 1938.

Marseille will spend the three-week international break 17th in the Ligue 1 table, with this the latest point into a season that they have sat in the relegation zone since 2011-12, when they were 20th with three points after six games and ultimately finished 10th.
But Luis Enrique expects them to come good eventually, saying: "Nothing was easy, we saw a very good OM team, with the way they defended. They have a great coach, I'm sure they will improve."
Genesio himself, however, admits Marseille's results have fallen well short of the required standard and has revealed he will hold talks with the club's hierarchy during the break.
"It's funny, everyone wishes me good luck. I'm a coach, so obviously I'm linked to the performances and results, especially at a club like OM," he said.
"This is insufficient, I assume my share of responsibility, as others will have to assume it too.
"I'm not there yet, I'm going to digest this defeat, talk to my staff, talk to my directors.
"Because I think – and I'm trying to weigh my words – that it's not normal for OM to be in this situation."
While PSG host Le Mans in their next Ligue 1 game on October 10, Marseille go to Troyes the following day.

1tytdnqt0jdlu181prjod107ue.title: Richter: Sporting KC comeback proved Philadelphia are far from perfect
1tytdnqt0jdlu181prjod107ue.subtitle: The Philadelphia Union are the team in form in the MLS, and their 11-game unbeaten run is on the line against Orlando City SC this weekend.
paragraphs: Ryan Richter described the Philadelphia Union's thrilling comeback against Sporting Kansas City as "outrageous", but said it was a warning sign to not get complacent.
Philadelphia's unbeaten run in MLS extended to 11 matches at Sporting Park last weekend, despite finding themselves three goals down against Sporting KC.
Andre Luiz's brace and a goal from Wyatt Meyer blew the Union away in the opening 16 minutes, with their sensational stretch under interim boss Richter looking set to end.
However, Philadelphia turned the game on its head in the space of four second-half minutes, with Bruno Damiani, Cavan Sullivan and Milan Iloski hauling their team level.
The turnaround was complete thanks to an own goal from Zorhan Bassong, with the result helping Philadelphia move up to sixth in the Eastern Conference.

And while he was pleased with the mentality of his players to complete the turnaround against Sporting KC, Richter acknowledged that better sides in the division will punish them should Philadelphia hand them an advantage like that again.

"The mentality of this group is outrageous," Richter said. "It would have been easy for us to quit at half-time. We're on the road, long journey, down 3-0, guys going away with their national teams after the game.

"But the way the guys responded in the second half was fantastic. I am proud of them and congratulations to them for showing again the way they believe in each other right now and what is possible with this group.
"It's fun to be a part of, and it's fun to watch, but we have to keep going. We got a reminder that we're not perfect and when we're not at our best, any team can beat us."
Philadelphia's next MLS outing sees them welcome Orlando City SC to Subaru Park this weekend, with the Lions also in the hunt to secure their spot in the playoffs.
Just two points and one place separate the two sides in the standings after Orlando fell to a 4-2 defeat against the New England Revolution last time out.
Martin Perelman's side saw their three-match winning run in the league come to an end, with late goals from Peyton Miller and Carles Gil sealing the win for New England.

"Very frustrated, of course, with the result. It was a big challenge for us because we came here after the game on Wednesday and were facing, of course, a team that is doing well in the league," Perelman said of Orlando's defeat to the Revolution.
"The context of the game was difficult. We knew that. Taking that into account, I think we made a very big effort. We made some mistakes, especially in the first half.

"And then we were able to come back in the second half, compete, tie the game, and then, I think there we have some gaps to improve as a team. I think we grew a lot during this season in many things. We are competing. We are up there. Everybody knows how we started.

"I think the process of the team is there, but if something we need to improve is this. We need to close these kinds of games. So, that's the frustration, but I also need to recognise the effort of the players. I have to do it because it was there."
Philadelphia Union – Bruno Damiani
With the in-form Sullivan away on international duty with the United States, the emphasis will fall on Damiani to continue Philadelphia's excellent run of form under Richter.
Only Iloski (13) has scored more MLS goals for Philadelphia than Damiani's eight, though the Uruguayan does have five goals in his last three league appearances.
Orlando City SC – Martin Ojeda
Ojeda recorded his team-leading 12th MLS goal of the season and his 46th across all competitions this year against New England last time out.

The Argentine has recorded three goal contributions in his last four matches across all competitions (two goals, one assist) and he is now just one goal short of tying Facundo Torres' club record of 47 goals across all competitions.
MATCH PREDICTION: PHILADELPHIA UNION WIN
As predicted, Philadelphia are the clear favourites in the Opta supercomputers pre-match simulations. The Union are now 11 games unbeaten in the MLS, tying the club record.

However, wins at Subaru Park against Orlando have proved hard to come by in recent years. Indeed, Philadelphia have failed to win their last three home league matches against the Lions (D1 L2) since a 5-1 victory back in September 2022.

But they come up against an Orlando side that have managed just three away league wins all season, though prior to their defeat to New England in their last such match, had drawn against Minnesota United and beaten Atlanta United.
Philadelphia Union – 65%
Orlando City SC – 16.4%

But they come up against an Orlando side that have managed just three away league wins all season, though prior to their defeat to New England in their last such match, had drawn against Minnesota United and beaten Atlanta United.

Philadelphia Union – 65%

1u05b3hp5sign1kt8f0qhsjiid.title: Australia 1-1 Brazil: Rayan nets last-gasp equaliser for Ancelotti's new-look side
1u05b3hp5sign1kt8f0qhsjiid.subtitle: Australia came within touching distance of stunning Brazil, but Rayan popped up with a late equaliser to seal a share of the spoils.
paragraphs: Brazil denied Australia a famous victory in Queensland as Rayan's stoppage-time header earned the Selecao a 1-1 draw in Thursday's international friendly.
Carlo Ancelotti said the match was the beginning of a new generation for Brazil, but his team fell behind to Nestory Irankunda's stunning second-half free-kick.
However, Bournemouth forward Rayan made Brazil's late pressure count, with the two sides squaring off once again next Tuesday at Suncorp Stadium.
Connor Metcalfe helped Australia make a quick start, with his shot whistling over Hugo Souza's crossbar after Vinicius Junior was cheaply dispossessed by Jacob Italiano.

Irankunda then fired way wide before the Australian defence put their bodies on the line to keep out Vinicius and Raphinha, with the hosts going close to the opening goal just before the break, but a deep corner just evaded Alessandro Circati at the far post.

Brazil thought they had taken the lead on the stroke of half-time when a neat one-two between Endrick and Estevao saw the latter finish past Patrick Beach, but the goal was ruled out after a VAR review for a foul on Harry Souttar by Bruno Guimaraes in the build-up.
Ancelotti's side built on that momentum after the break, with the in-form Raphinha first seeing his shot smothered by Beach before he drilled narrowly wide of the right post.

Estevao then fired over after Vinicius' attempt deflected kindly to him, and Australia made the most of that reprieve in the 68th minute through Irankunda, who curled a sensational free-kick past Souza and into the top-left corner.

Brazil penned Australia back into their own penalty area in their search for a late equaliser, and their persistence was rewarded in the fifth minute of second-half stoppage time, with Rayan's thunderous header from a Raphinha corner going in off the crossbar.
Irankunda and Herrington star for Australia's young guns

With both nations playing in their first matches since their respective exits from this summer's World Cup, many predicted Brazil's quality in the final third to be too much for Australia, but Popovic's side proved they are more than capable of mixing it with the established nations.

And Australia's combative performance at the back was spearheaded by Lucas Herrington. After becoming the youngest player to start a knockout match at the World Cup for the Socceroos this summer, he proved why he was worthy of his switch to the Premier League with Hull City.

Herrington won all three of the duels he contested, while only Circati (eight) and Souttar (six) made more clearances than his four. He also made two interceptions, but it was another exciting talent in Irankunda that shone at the other end.

Irankunda was handed a third consecutive start, his longest such run for Australia, and he delivered by becoming only the second player to score against Brazil for the Socceroos, after Shaun Murphy back in June 2001.

But after restricting Brazil to very little in their search for an equaliser, Australia will be frustrated after being undone by a set-piece. Ancelotti's side will, however, feel they were deserving of the result. They finished with an expected goals (xG) total of 1.15 from their 16 shots to their opponents' tally of 0.45 from their seven attempts.

1ur5y32ga6uu512tn6izb1ktkt.title: 'Stop referee harassment now' – Atleti hit back at Mourinho following derby comments
1ur5y32ga6uu512tn6izb1ktkt.subtitle: Jose Mourinho launched into a rant about refereeing standards following Real Madrid's defeat to Atletico Madrid, who have now hit back.
paragraphs: Atletico Madrid have hit back at Jose Mourinho following his rant about referee Ortiz Arias in the aftermath of their derby win over Real Madrid.
Alejandro Grimaldo and Jonathan David were on target on Sunday as Los Colchoneros overcame their cross-city rivals 2-1 at the Estadio Metropolitano.
The victory lifted Diego Simeone's side to second in LaLiga, five points behind leaders Barcelona, going into the three-week international break, with Los Blancos a point further back in fourth.

But their win was not without controversy, as Madrid had centre-back Dean Huijsen sent off for denying Giuliano Simeone a clear goalscoring opportunity, and Mourinho felt Atleti were fortunate to keep all 11 men on the pitch.
Lee Kang-In avoided punishment for a high challenge that caught Federico Valverde on his ankle, leaving the Uruguay international requiring medical tests.
Cristian Romero, meanwhile, was only cautioned for what Madrid believed was a stamp on Jude Bellingham's knee, despite Arias being sent to the VAR monitor to check the incident.

Mourinho appeared at his post-match press conference with printed images of both incidents, saying they were both "clear red cards" and arguing Arias was not equipped to handle the pressure of such a big game.
Simeone subsequently said it was important that referees are protected and told his Madrid counterpart: "Not everything goes, even for Mourinho."
And on Monday, Atleti's club account on X posted an image of Mourinho discussing the incidents at his press conference, along with the caption: "Stop referee harassment now."
Atleti have only lost one of the last eight derbies between the teams in LaLiga (W3 D4), winning four of the last six meetings to take place at the Metropolitano (D1 L1).
Los Colchoneros have also won seven straight home games against teams from the Community of Madrid, the longest such winning streak in their history.

1vj9a3vafo6cs1a6krcb93q86u.title: 'Alvarez is the past' – Barcelona move on from summer target
1vj9a3vafo6cs1a6krcb93q86u.subtitle: Barcelona were open about their pursuit of Julian Alvarez in the summer, but have closed the door on the Atletico Madrid striker for now.
paragraphs: Barcelona sporting director Deco insists their interest in Julian Alvarez "is the past" after failing to sign the Atletico Madrid striker this summer.

Barca reportedly saw an offer of over €100m rejected by Atleti, who later revealed they would refuse to negotiate with their rivals due to the Blaugrana's public pursuit of the Argentina international.
Real Madrid's €150m bid was also rejected by Atleti, while reports suggested Alvarez turned down interest from Premier League side Arsenal.
Alvarez has featured four times for Diego Simeone's side this term, with only one of those appearances coming as a starter, registering just one assist across all competitions.
The 26-year-old made his return from a brief injury in Atleti's Madrid derby before joining up with the Argentina national team.
Barca managed to sign Gabriel Jesus late on in the window after the exits of Robert Lewandowski and Ferran Torres, and Deco revealed any immediate interest in Alvarez is now over.
"Julian Alvarez is the past," Deco said at the Portugal Football Summit.
"Barcelona now have to look forward. It wasn't possible in the end. We made an offer. [Atleti] said they would not transfer him and we had to look for other solutions.
"I hope things go well for him and that he can help his club."
Barca have also been linked with a move for 15-year-old Manchester United prospect JJ Gabriel in recent weeks.
Widespread reports emerged stating Gabriel had asked to leave United, with Barca and Madrid among the teams said to be monitoring the situation.
Deco, however, has put an end to the speculation, saying: "There's nothing to say about this boy.
"It's normal that players are linked with us. It always happens. There's a huge market for that with a lot of interests involved, even when [players] are young.
"But we are not interested in any player in his situation. I'm not sure what's happening, and if he's still a Manchester United player. We are not involved in that.
"First of all, we need to understand how the situation is before we try to do something. To speak about young, teenage players, it is not our business."

1vti29e1jbzts1xjheqztrgw5c.title: Aguirre returns to Spain with LaLiga strugglers Valencia
1vti29e1jbzts1xjheqztrgw5c.subtitle: After spending two years away from LaLiga, Javier Aguirre is back in Spain, being tasked with trying to turn Valencia's fortunes around.
paragraphs: Javier Aguirre has been appointed as the new head coach of Valencia on a contract that will run until the end of the campaign.
Aguirre arrives at the Estadio de Mestalla following a two-year stint in charge of Mexico, who he led to the round of 16 at this summer's World Cup.
The 67-year-old's deal contains an option for him to remain at the helm for a second season in Valencia, who have made a dismal start to 2026-27.
Valencia are 19th in LaLiga with four points from their opening seven games, with Carlos Corberan sacked just two months after extending his deal until 2028.
Oscar Sanchez took interim charge and helped Valencia to their first win of the season against Alaves, before overseeing a 3-2 defeat to Real Sociedad last Sunday.
Aguirre arrives with plenty of experience. He has managed 468 matches in LaLiga, the fifth-highest total of any foreign coach in the history of the competition.

The Mexican will be the fourth foreign manager to coach seven different teams in LaLiga, after Roque Olsen (seven), Ferdinand Daucik (nine), and Marcel Domingo (11), having previously taken charge of Osasuna, Atletico Madrid, Real Zaragoza, Espanyol, Leganes and Mallorca.
Aguirre's arrival comes after he announced ahead of this summer's World Cup that he would be leaving Mexico, with Rafael Marquez coming in to take over.
He was unable to end Mexico's wait for a first quarter-final appearance since 1986, after they were beaten 3-2 by 10-man England on home soil.

The defeat was Mexico's first at the Azteca in a competitive match for 13 years, since losing to Honduras in a qualifier for the 2014 World Cup, while it was the first time they had conceded three goals at the venue since a 4-3 triumph over Brazil in August 1999.
But Aguirre will now turn his attention back to club football, having last been in charge of Mallorca, who he helped avoid relegation from LaLiga in 2021-22.
Aguirre also led Mallorca to the Copa del Rey final in 2024, but they were beaten on penalties by Athletic Club before he parted ways with the club that summer.
His first home game in charge will come against Athletic on October 17, but he will make his bow for Valencia six days earlier, away to Racing de Santander.

1wrp7lzqo8je81mup9pt0psejb.title: Netherlands 1-1 Germany: Gakpo denies former Liverpool boss Klopp in stoppage time
1wrp7lzqo8je81mup9pt0psejb.subtitle: Jurgen Klopp was just a minute away from a debut win in charge of Germany, only to be denied by his former Liverpool attacker Cody Gakpo.
paragraphs: A stoppage-time equaliser from Cody Gakpo denied his former Liverpool boss Jurgen Klopp a winning start with Germany, as the Netherlands salvaged a 1-1 draw in the Nations League.

It looked like Felix Nmecha's 32nd-minute strike would settle an entertaining and at times fractious affair between two old rivals under new coaches, with Barcelona great Xavi also making his Netherlands bow.
But in the second of three minutes of second-half stoppage time, Gakpo met a cross from debutant Ruben van Bommel brilliantly on the stretch, ensuring the points were shared in Group A2.

The first moment of drama came after 12 minutes, as Virgil van Dijk – another of Klopp's former Liverpool stalwarts – glanced Tijjani Reijnders' inswinging corner beyond Marc-Andre ter Stegen. But a VAR review led to the goal being chalked off, due to Brian Brobbey backing into the Germany goalkeeper.

Germany then saw Kai Havertz limp off following a high challenge from Quinten Timber, the twin brother of his Arsenal team-mate Jurrien, though substitute Younes Ebnoutalib almost made an immediate impact as Bart Verbruggen blocked his near-post drive.

And another injury to a Premier League forward played a role in the opening goal. As the Netherlands appealed for a foul on the stricken Brobbey, Germany looked set to kick the ball out, but Nadiem Amiri and Joshua Kimmich instead kept the attack going, and Nmecha swept home after Nathaniel Brown's centre flicked into his path.
A glaring miss from Karim Adeyemi prevented Germany from going 2-0 up late in the first half, but it was one-way traffic from then on with the Oranje laying siege to Ter Stegen's goal.

He thwarted Denzel Dumfries from close range with his right boot, then Mexx Meerdink – another Netherlands debutant – put the ball in the net but saw a foul given against Van Dijk. The young AZ forward also turned Dumfries' cross wide on the slide as Germany closed in on a big three points, but they would be denied with time almost up.

Gakpo showed tremendous athleticism to divert Van Bommel's cross past Ter Stegen while in mid-air, though the Dutch forward was arguably fortunate to avoid a very late red card after the restart, when he trod on Yannik Engelhardt.
Gakpo denies Klopp as the Netherlands impress
Few international coaching debuts in recent years have been as eagerly anticipated as this one.

Indeed, Klopp oversaw 674 games as a manager in the Bundesliga and the Premier League across spells with Mainz, Borussia Dortmund and Liverpool, the most matches in Europe's top five leagues that any Germany coach had accumulated before taking charge.

But this game showed the size of the task awaiting him, as Germany were penned back throughout the second half by an impressive Netherlands side. The Oranje racked up 3.12 expected goals (xG) and 22 shots, compared to Germany's 1.5 xG from 10 attempts.
And in the end, it was Gakpo – who played 79 games under him for Liverpool, scoring 23 goals in that time – that made Klopp wait for his first victory in charge of his country.

There was at least a notable landmark for Klopp's captain Kimmich, who was at the centre of the controversy leading up to Nmecha's goal, on his 115th cap. He has now surpassed Toni Kroos (114) to sit seventh outright in Germany's all-time charts.

Both teams are back in action on Sunday, with Germany hosting Greece and the Netherlands visiting Serbia, but with Havertz and Brobbey both hobbling off, both came out of a bruising encounter with injury concerns.

1wzp4sylqp3g14dctwhmxr2c7.title: Martinez: Argentina must forget World Cup heartache and celebrate Messi
1wzp4sylqp3g14dctwhmxr2c7.subtitle: Lionel Messi will make his farewell appearance for Argentina during the international break, before he steps away from the Albiceleste.
paragraphs: Lisandro Martinez says Argentina's players are determined to put their World Cup final heartache behind them and savour Lionel Messi's international send-off next month.

The Albiceleste could have become the first back-to-back winners of FIFA's showpiece tournament since Brazil in 1958 and 1962, after Messi inspired them to a final appearance in North America this summer.
However, Enzo Fernandez's red card proved costly as Spain beat them 1-0 in extra time, with Ferran Torres scoring the all-important goal.

Argentina have now been World Cup runners-up four times (also in 1930, 1990 and 2014), the joint-most of any nation alongside West Germany/Germany, and they became the first team to not attempt a single shot in regulation time of a World Cup final.
But Manchester United defender Martinez says the time has come for Lionel Scaloni's side to put that defeat behind them, as they prepare to say goodbye to a legend.
Having announced his decision to retire from international football following the World Cup, Messi will make a farewell appearance at a friendly against Benin on October 5.

Bolivia and Burkina Faso will be Argentina's opponents before that match, which will see members of the 2022 World Cup-winning squad come together for a celebration of Messi's career at the Estadio Monumental in Buenos Aires.
"There's a lot of pain, preferably we don't remember it, but we must also highlight the tremendous effort we made throughout the tournament," Martinez told ESPN Argentina.
"Without a doubt, we had a great World Cup, but it hurts us all to have lost the final.
"Now we are here, back in our country, and we are going to enjoy ourselves."

Messi has scored 125 goals in 207 appearances for Argentina, leading his country's all-time charts in both categories, with his last strike coming in their dramatic World Cup round-of-16 victory over Egypt this summer.
No player has directly contributed to more goals at the World Cup on record (since 1966) than Messi (33 – 21 goals and 12 assists), who has also featured in the most games at the finals (34).

Messi's 12 assists in the competition are also the most of any player, four more than the great Diego Maradona (eight), while only Kylian Mbappe (22 goals) has netted more often, though Messi was the first to surpass Miroslav Klose's previous record of 16 goals this year.

"There's a lot of pain, preferably we don't remember it, but we must also highlight the tremendous effort we made throughout the tournament," Martinez told ESPN Argentina.

"Without a doubt, we had a great World Cup, but it hurts us all to have lost the final. 

"Now we are here, back in our country, and we are going to enjoy ourselves."

Messi has scored 125 goals in 207 appearances for Argentina, leading his country's all-time charts in both categories, with his last strike coming in their dramatic World Cup round-of-16 victory over Egypt this summer.

No player has directly contributed to more goals at the World Cup on record (since 1966) than Messi (33 – 21 goals and 12 assists), who has also featured in the most games at the finals (34).

Messi's 12 assists in the competition are also the most of any player, four more than the great Diego Maradona (eight), while only Kylian Mbappe (22 goals) has netted more often, though Messi was the first to surpass Miroslav Klose's previous record of 16 goals this year.

1x7hu16c5gm981s0dwvjv1xjol.title: Spalletti relieved to see Juventus banish Sassuolo 'doubts' against Atalanta
1x7hu16c5gm981s0dwvjv1xjol.subtitle: Having seen their unbeaten Serie A start halted by Sassuolo on matchday four, Juventus bounced back with an impressive win over Atalanta.
paragraphs: Luciano Spalletti admitted Juventus' defeat to Sassuolo last week had created doubt in the Bianconeri's ranks, and he was delighted to see them banish that feeling by beating Atalanta.
Juve suffered their first defeat of the Serie A campaign on matchday four, conceding a stoppage-time winner to Vasilije Adzic in a 3-2 loss to Sassuolo.
However, they bounced back in style on Sunday with a 2-0 success against Atalanta and their former head coach Maurizio Sarri, with Francisco Conceicao and Bremer on target.

Juve have now won three of their first five games of a Serie A season while keeping a clean sheet in each victory for the first time since 2017-18, when they went on to win the Scudetto under Massimiliano Allegri.
And with a three-week international break now on the horizon, Spalletti was relieved to see his team cast aside the negativity of their previous Serie A outing.
He told Sky Sport Italia: "There was a moment when we were forced to defend, then we had to change something and, from there, we got back on track and played on an equal footing in the second half.
"We can certainly get better with the start of our actions and in the build-up. We could have hurt Atalanta more.
"But that's okay, also because the defeat against Sassuolo had created some doubts for us."

Spalletti also reserved particular praise for Randal Kolo Muani, whose performances he criticised last month, despite the Frenchman missing a big one-v-one chance with an expected goals (xG) value of 0.35 – the highest of any shot in the match.
"He had a really good game. I was disappointed when he popped up one-on-one with the goalkeeper because he deserved to score," Spalletti said of Kolo Muani.
"But he was still very happy at the end and we joked about it. We're all happy because now we can recover some of our strong players, who would have been useful to us recently."
While Juve are seventh in the table going into the break with 10 points on the board, Atalanta are four points worse off in 11th.
Sarri – a Scudetto winner in his only season in charge of Juventus in 2019-20 – has now lost nine Serie A matches against the Bianconeri, his joint-most against any club (also Roma).
Though La Dea have now lost three straight games, Sarri insists there is no crisis brewing in Bergamo.
"I don't think so, the first three games were a lower level of performance, but we have been improving," he said.
"This team needs to have more character, to light up that fire in its soul. This is a side with certain capabilities and we need to access them."

2208B0258C566247C168DE0E73060A38.title: The FotMob TOTW for the Premier League: Matchday 5’s Best XI includes Brobbey, Manzambi, Groß and Semenyo
2208B0258C566247C168DE0E73060A38.subtitle: FotMob
paragraphs: NewsAboutTV schedulesThe FotMob TOTW for the Premier League: Matchday 5’s Best XI includes Brobbey, Manzambi, Groß and SemenyoShareMatchday 5 of the Premier League season is done and dusted, with Manchester City establishing a three-point advantage at the top of the table courtesy of Arsenal’s defeat against Brighton.
It will be a sad time when Alisson finally leaves Liverpool, especially as he is still more than capable of producing excellent displays like the one against Bournemouth.

The Brazilian made two saves during the game, including an impressive effort to prevent Evanilson from opening the scoring in the first half – a shot worth 0.78 xGOT. That was his third Premier League clean sheet in a row.
The Barcelona loanee makes it into FotMob’s Team of the Week for the second time in three weeks thanks to another solid display.

Araújo wasn’t quite at his best in the final third, yet the right-back made five defensive contributions including two tackles, while also registering six recoveries throughout the game. He even won 86% of his aerial duels and played a massive part in Liverpool keeping that clean sheet for Alisson.
Everton kept their fifth clean sheet across seven matches in all competitions against Ipswich at the weekend and James Tarkowski played a big part in the 1-0 win.
The defender provided the assist for Everton’s only goal while also notching up 12 defensive contributions throughout the 90 minutes.

Seven of those were clearances, and Tarkowski was also a rock when it came to duels, winning 100% of his ground and 83% of his aerial duels in the contest. He was certainly more than deserving of his 8.5 rating.
Brentford’s 3-0 victory over Chelsea was arguably the result of Matchday 5 and Jannik Schuster was rock solid at the heart of the defence.

With 16, the Austrian centre-back registered the most defensive contributions in the game, and he even chipped in at the other end of the pitch, grabbing an assist and making three passes into the final third.
Aged just 20, Schuster could be the future of Brentford’s defence over the next few years.
Jay Dasilva’s thumping effort against Nottingham Forest gave Coventry their first Premier League win since 2001 and he fully deserves his spot in the Team of the Week.

The left-back was a menace on the left flank, succeeding with 100% of his dribble attempts while also making six passes into the final third. Frank Lampard will be expecting more of the same when domestic action returns next month.
Chema Andrés provided an assist on his Premier League debut last weekend, but he went one better against Arsenal, netting the third goal in Brighton’s victory against the champions.
It was a splendid performance by the midfielder who looked equally adept whether he was defending or trying to make things happen in the final third against the Gunners.
Five passes into the final third, nine defensive contributions, and winning five out of five aerial duels ensure he makes his FotMob Team of the Week debut.
Pascal Groß is ageing like a fine wine, isn’t he? The German midfielder covered the most ground against Arsenal (12.6 km), despite being the oldest player on the pitch.
He not only scored, but provided an assist during the contest, and also made eight passes into the final third.
Groß added five defensive contributions and was well deserving of making the Team of the Week for the second consecutive matchday.
🤯 Pascal Gross has won FotMob Man of the Match in ALL of Brighton’s last three games, averaging a rating of 8.8!He’s 35-years-old, by the way. pic.twitter.com/i2tV5QHRht

257387683964B2C1903D4A98BE49BBAA.title: Pochettino is bringing through the USA’s brightest crop of youngsters since Pulisic and co.
257387683964B2C1903D4A98BE49BBAA.subtitle: FotMob
paragraphs: NewsAboutTV schedulesPochettino is bringing through the USA’s brightest crop of youngsters since Pulisic and co.ShareMauricio Pochettino has called up a youthful squad for the USA’s first fixtures since co-hosting the 2026 World Cup.

The hype around Cavan Sullivan has been intense for years. From the moment the American wonderkid joined Manchester City at the age of only 14, Sullivan has been built up as the USA’s greatest individual hope for the future. Now 16 years old, the future is now with Sullivan expected to make his national team debut in the current international break.

Picked by Mauricio Pochettino for the friendly matches against Peru, Chile, Mexico and Canada, Sullivan is part of a youthful contingent the US men’s national team head coach has turned to as part of his process to prepare his side for the 2030 World Cup. A new cycle signifies a fresh start for the USMNT.

Sullivan earned his call-up by catching the eye for the Philadelphia Union. The teenager is on a run of six goals in six games with only Lionel Messi more impactful as an individual difference-maker in Major League Soccer right now than Sullivan. The wonderkid is in wonderful form and could become the USMNT’s youngest debutant since Freddy Adu.

RBNY's Adri Mehmeti is another teenage talent called up by Pochettino for the first time. The 17-year-old is the sort of midfield pace-setter the USA have lacked for years, decades even. Physically, Mehmeti still has some growing to do, but the potential is clearly there for him to become a key figure for the national team.

Neil Pierre’s emergence for Philadelphia is timely for the USA considering their desperate need for defensive reinforcement. Tim Ream has been a reliable performer for the national team, but the former Fulham centre back is now 38. He will be into his 40s by the time of the 2030 World Cup.

Justin Ellis has broken through as a key figure for Orlando City this season with the Red Bulls’ Julian Hall yet another teenage talent who has made a profound impact in MLS recently. The number of young players using the league as a platform has been a big storyline of the 2026 season.

No fewer than 13 uncapped players have been called up by Pochettino for the September and October international window. Among them are a contingent of youngsters who appear ready for regular game time. Sullivan could be in this group. So too could Zavier Gozo who made the move to Crystal Palace from Real Salt Lake this summer.

There is also another contingent who might not be ready for prime time for a number of years. Prospects like Brooklyn Raines, Mathis Albert and Diego Kochen must use the experience of being involved in a USMNT camp to continue their development. Pochettino is firmly focused on the future.

Noahkai Banks might have been another young player called up. Pochettino courted the Augsburg defender only for Banks, who played for the USA at youth level, to file a one-time switch to represent Germany last week. Supporters reacted with disappointment, but Pochettino made clear that he wouldn’t dwell on Banks’ rejection.

“We want players who show commitment,” said Pochettino when asked about US Soccer’s recruitment of dual-nationals which will surely continue even after the failure to land Banks. “Commitment is not 50%, it’s 200%. It’s good, he was honest. We want players who want to commit and are desperate to play for the badge. That’s the most important thing.”

While the USMNT’s 2026 World Cup campaign ended abruptly with a heavy (and controversial) defeat to Belgium in the last 16, Pochettino established a tactical framework for the tournament that will give him a headstart now that he is at the start of a new cycle. A lot of the hard work has already been done.

Now, it’s about finding players who can execute his instructions at an even higher level. Pochettino is bringing through the most exciting crop of young American talent since Christian Pulisic, Weston McKennie and Tyler Adams surfaced. He could elevate the USMNT’s level by integrating new players in a position or two.

The squad for the September and October international window is unashamedly experimental. Pulisic hasn’t been called up despite the fact he is the USA’s most reliable attacking difference-maker. Folarin Balogun has been given the time to settle back into life at Monaco after his failed deadline day transfer to Everton. McKennie is similarly out of this current squad.

Pochettino will call on these established stars again, but the next three weeks are about finding new players for the USMNT to build around. The road to the 2030 World Cup (via a possible Copa America, a Gold Cup and an Olympics) starts here. Sullivan and co. are ready to step up.

          Five Knee-Jerk Reactions to Premier League 2026-27 Matchday 5
        
      
                          
                      Sep 21, 2026
          
                      Ali Tweedale / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
We’re back with our weekly dose of knee-jerk reactions to the weekend’s Premier League action.
Every week here on Opta Analyst, we do something we don’t normally do and come to a load of conclusions based on just a single round of Premier League matches.
We usually rely on large data sets to make our judgements, but in this weekly column we react quickly and maybe a little too hastily.
It’s all a bit of fun, and many of our five reactions for this week will swiftly prove to be nothing more than exactly what we called them: knee-jerk.
But some might just hold up in the weeks to come. Read on to see which way you think these week’s conclusions will eventually go.

Coming into Matchday 5, it felt like there was no stopping Arsenal. They’d won all four Premier League games, as well as three more in other competitions, and few of their opponents had caused them any real problems at all.
Fabian Hürzeler’s side had produced some impressive results early in the season, but nobody expected them to blow Arsenal away quite like they did on Saturday.

They pressed the champions with a vicious and suffocating relentlessness that meant Arsenal just could not get any kind of grip on the game. Brighton forced a colossal 15 high turnovers (winning possession within 40 metres of the opposition's goal line), which is the second most by any team in the Premier League this season, behind only Brighton against an Aston Villa side who played most of that game with just 10 men (19).

They also recognised how difficult it is to carve out clear-cut chances against this Arsenal side, so shot on sight, often from distance. They scored twice from range to take Arsenal’s total to a league-high three goals conceded from outside the box this season.

Was this the blueprint for how to take the champions down, or a mere – and very natural – day off for the best team in the world right now? We’ll see if anyone else can do this to them after they’ve gathered their thoughts during the international break.
Some say you make your own luck, but there’s no denying that Spurs have been incredibly fortunate not to be relegated in the last two utterly dismal seasons.

In 2024-25, they were entirely reliant on the dreadful form of the promoted sides, who were so bad that there was never really a relegation battle of any sort. Then, last season, they escaped by the skin of their teeth after failing to address their myriad of problems in either transfer window.

Now, five games into 2026-27 and after a summer of upheaval, they are bottom of the table and staring at the very real possibility of another flirtation with the drop despite spending more than £300 million.

They have a lot of talent in their squad now, and certainly appear to have more potential, particularly in attack, than they did last term. Against Aston Villa on Saturday, they created more than enough, notably when the game was still level, to take control of the game, but failed to take their chances and were punished in brutal fashion. They won on xG but remain winless in actuality, with just two points from five games and a goal difference of -6.
It is now their worst ever start to a Premier League season and has left them with a lot of improving to do to avoid the possibility of another 17th-place finish – or worse.

We’ve learned over the last two years that nothing can be taken for granted with this club, and with no other team looking anything like as hopeless so far this season, there is every chance they get themselves into yet more trouble.
Brian Brobbey isn’t the most fashionable of footballers, and his physical approach to the game may mean he never gets the chance to play for a big-six club.

But even if he doesn’t play for a Champions League club that never lifts the ball off the floor and always has more than 60% possession, there is absolutely no denying what a handful he is. He deserves far more respect than many give him.

In Sunderland’s defeat to Manchester City this weekend, he scored three times from just five shots and became only the fourth player in Premier League history to score a hat-trick against the side starting the day top of the table, after Robbie Fowler vs Aston Villa in November 1998, Dirk Kuyt vs Manchester United in March 2011, and Romelu Lukaku vs United in May 2013.

He was extremely unfortunate to also end up on the losing side, too, becoming the sixth player ever to score a hat-trick and lose a Premier League game, and the first since Roque Santa Cruz for Blackburn vs Wigan in December 2007.
