          UEFA Women’s Champions League: Opta Supercomputer Matchday 1 Predictions
        
      
                          
                      Sep 22, 2026
          
                      Matt Furniss / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
With the help of the AI-powered Opta supercomputer, we provide our UEFA Women’s Champions League match predictions across Matchday 1 in 2026-27.

The Opta supercomputer will be with us every step of the way in the 2026-27 UEFA Women’s Champions League as the model works to provide you with data-backed predictions for all matches and season outcomes.

Matchday 1 kicks off on Tuesday 22 September with five games, including the reigning WSL champions Manchester City’s return to the UWCL after a one-year absence. Andrée Jeglertz's side will take on seven-time German Frauen-Bundesliga winners Bayern Munich away from home.
Four more matches follow on Wednesday, when the reigning European champions Barcelona host Paris FC, and eight-time UWCL winners OL Lyonnes travel to Swiss side Servette.
Below, Opta Analyst provides predictions for each game from MD1, powered by thousands of simulations from the Opta supercomputer.

The 2026-27 competition gets underway on Tuesday with two early 5.45pm kick-offs in Milan and Munich. The most eye-catching fixture of the two is between the reigning league champions in Germany and England, as Bayern Munich host Manchester City.

It is a daunting opening assignment for City. Bayern are ranked second in Opta's Power Rankings (95.9) and boast an enviable record on home soil in this competition. They went unbeaten across their five UWCL home matches last season (W4 D1) and have lost just one of their last 16 at home in Europe (W11 D4), a 2-0 defeat to Lyon in the quarter-finals of the 2024-25 campaign.

The supercomputer expects Bayern to make the most of that home advantage, with the German champions winning 52.4% of its 10,000 pre-match simulations. City, meanwhile, came out on top in 23.3%, underlining the size of the challenge awaiting them on their return to the competition.

The other early kick-off on Tuesday is between Inter and Häcken, with the home side making their UWCL debut in front of their own fans. While the Italians will be hoping to mark the occasion with a statement result, the Swedish club are slight favourites according to the supercomputer, winning 55.9% of simulations as they return to the competition for the first time since reaching the quarter-finals in 2023-24.
Arsenal, winners of the competition in 2024-25, begin their latest European campaign at home to HB Køge.

The Gunners have yet to fully hit their stride domestically, opening the WSL season with a 1-0 win at Brighton before being held by Crystal Palace and Manchester United at Emirates Stadium. Despite registering 47 shots across those two home matches, Arsenal scored just once, relying on a stoppage-time equaliser against United to extend their unbeaten run.

No English team have lost to Danish opposition in the UWCL since the north London club’s 5-1 defeat to Fortuna Hjørring in the 2002-03 semi-final (W7 D3 since), and the Opta supercomputer expects Arsenal to secure all three points in this one. Renée Slegers' side won 81.1% of its pre-match simulations – the highest percentage of any side playing on Tuesday night.

The supercomputer struggled to find a clear winner in its pre-game sims for Juventus vs Benfica, but the Portuguese club have the slight edge (39.9%). That's despite Juve beating Benfica 2-1 in last season’s league phase thanks to a brace from Cecilia Salvai.

Tuesday’s other clash is between Real Madrid and Paris Saint-Germain, with PSG looking to end a miserable eight-game winless streak in the UWCL (L6 D2) – their longest such run in the competition. The Opta supercomputer isn’t confident of them doing that though, as Madrid won 45.6% of its 10,000 pre-game sims.
Record UWCL champions, and last season’s losing finalists, OL Lyonnes make their 2026-27 bow on Wednesday night, travelling to Swiss club Servette in one of the early evening kick-offs.

It’s a daunting start for Servette, with Jonatan Giráldez's side unbeaten across their last 23 group/league stage games in the UEFA Women’s Champions League (W18 D5) since a 5-1 defeat to Arsenal in 2022-23.

Considering all of Lyon’s previous UWCL meetings with Swiss sides have ended in big wins (all vs Zürich: 8-0, 9-0, 3-0 and 4-0) it’s understandable that Lyon are given a 73.7% chance of victory on MD1 – the biggest chance of an away win across the two nights of action.
The Opta supercomputer also makes the away side favourites in the other early Wednesday fixture, with Roma travelling to Belgium to face OH Leuven.

The Italian side came out on top in 60.8% of the model's pre-match simulations, reflecting both their growing European pedigree and OH Leuven's struggles in last season's competition, where the Belgians won just one of their eight matches (D3 L4).

Attention then turns to Wednesday's later kick-offs, which feature two of the three highest-ranked teams in the women's Opta Power Rankings. Defending European champions Barcelona host Paris FC, while Chelsea welcome Austria Wien to The Cherry Red Records Stadium.

3jnohid0gubi1ibj9w14pv78y.title: Spain extend De la Fuente's contract through to Euro 2032
3jnohid0gubi1ibj9w14pv78y.subtitle: After he led Spain to European and world titles, Luis de la Fuente's future is secured for another six years.
paragraphs: Luis de la Fuente will stay on as Spain's head coach through to 2032, after the Spanish Football Federation extended his contract.

De la Fuente took over in December 2022 following Luis Enrique's resignation in the wake of Spain's disappointing showing at the World Cup in Qatar, and he has enjoyed huge success in his first four years.

The 65-year-old, who spent nine years with Spain's youth teams before taking over the senior team, led them to the 2022-23 Nations League title, as well as triumphs at Euro 2024 and the 2026 World Cup.
La Roja beat Argentina 1-0 in extra time in the World Cup final in July to secure their second title.
De la Fuente's current deal was due to run until the end of Euro 2028, but he will now remain in his post for an additional four years, which includes a World Cup title defence as co-hosts in 2030.
"We are seeking a project of stability and confidence," RFEF president Rafael Louzan said.
"This proposal is based on confidence in Luis de la Fuente and the sporting project he leads, for a multi-year cycle of competitions and major tournaments.
"We are talking about the most decorated coach in the history of the national team, and after fourteen years with us, Luis de la Fuente deserves a long future at the RFEF."
Spain are unbeaten in their last 38 matches in all competitions, the longest-ever run by any European or South American team in history.
At this summer's World Cup, they lifted the trophy having conceded just one goal in their eight games, the fewest goals conceded by any team in a World Cup-winning campaign.
In total, De la Fuente has taken charge of 49 matches across all competitions, winning 37 of those (D10 L2). His team have scored 126 goals during that time and conceded just 35.
He will now look to reach another Nations League final – having also done so in 2024-25 before losing to Portugal on penalties.
Spain begin their new campaign away to England on September 26, with a double header against Croatia to come on either side of hosting Czechia.

          Liverpool's Evolution: From Survival Mode to WSL Top-Four Contenders
        
      
                          
                      Sep 24, 2026
          
                      Maya Shah / Author, Jakob Abrahamson / Design
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
Are Liverpool genuine top-four contenders in the WSL? We look at the transformation behind their impressive start, the performance that almost earned them a result against Man City, and how their players are helping to drive renewed hope.
Just four months ago, the idea of Liverpool challenging for a UEFA Women's Champions League place would have seemed improbable.
The Reds finished 11th in the Women's Super League in 2025-26, ending the season eight points clear of bottom-placed Leicester City but recording their second-lowest finish in the competition.
Their 2025-26 campaign began in disastrous fashion under the former Manchester City boss Gareth Taylor, as the Reds failed to win any of their opening 12 league matches (D4 L8).
A six-game losing streak at the start of the season set the tone, including an opening weekend loss to rivals Everton at Anfield (4-1) followed by a shock defeat at Leicester City on MD2.
Liverpool found themselves rooted to the foot of the table across the winter break with just three points collected, and facing serious questions about their future direction.
Their struggles continued into the start of 2026 as Liverpool's winless league run reached 15 matches, the longest in their WSL history.
Yet, even amid the poor results, there were signs they could compete.

During that difficult run, Liverpool lost to both Arsenal and Man City by just a single-goal margin, with both winning goals coming in the final four minutes. It was enough to suggest that the gap to the league's elite was not quite as wide as the table implied.
There were also off-field circumstances surrounding the club that cannot be ignored when looking back at Liverpool's 2025-26 WSL campaign.

The passing of former manager Matt Beard in September 2025 cast a shadow over the season. Beard was one of the most influential figures in the club's history, overseeing 106 WSL matches across two spells and guiding them to back-to-back league titles in 2013 and 2014. Against that backdrop, Liverpool's struggles became easier to contextualise.
Taylor’s first WSL victory with the Reds came at home against Tottenham in January, and while Liverpool won only three more league matches across the campaign, it proved enough to secure survival.
Now, less than a year later, the picture looks very different.

Liverpool began 2026-27 with a convincing 4-0 victory over Charlton Athletic, their first win in a season opener since 2023. The four-goal margin was also their biggest in a WSL match since a 4-0 victory over Leicester in May 2024.

They followed that with a 1-1 draw against Tottenham on MD2, a result that arguably failed to reflect the balance of play, before pushing Man City all the way on MD3. An unfortunate 89th-minute own goal by Grace Fisk ultimately denied Liverpool what would have been their first point against City since May 2023.

Results alone, however, only tell part of the story. The underlying numbers point to a Liverpool side that are playing with greater ambition than we saw for much of last season. They are pressing higher, spending more time in possession, and showing a greater willingness to take the game to their opponents rather than simply react to them.

Of course, there are still areas to improve, but the early season data suggests a meaningful shift in Liverpool’s approach. A side that spent much of last season battling at the bottom end of the table are showing signs of being better equipped to compete with the division’s leading teams.
So, can Liverpool turn that promising start into a genuine push for a top-four finish?
They may have left Manchester empty-handed on Friday night, but Liverpool's performance arguably told a more encouraging story than the result itself.

Too often in recent seasons have meetings with the WSL's elite been exercises in damage limitation. Liverpool's approach at the Joie Stadium was markedly different. They pressed aggressively, played through City's pressure and repeatedly forced the hosts into uncomfortable situations.

480kzgt5dqwq1euhyhwf837zn.title: Greenwood: Man City there to win in Champions League
480kzgt5dqwq1euhyhwf837zn.subtitle: Manchester City return to the Women's Champions League after a season-long absence, and Alex Greenwood is eyeing a deep run.
paragraphs: Alex Greenwood says Manchester City are "going to give it absolutely everything" to try and win the Women's Champions League this season.
City were absent from last season's campaign, but they are back in the competition following their Women's Super League title success in 2025-26.
Andree Jeglertz enjoyed a stellar first season with the team, and they have started their title defence in equally fine form, having won all three of their league games so far.
But their attention now turns to the Champions League, and they will begin their campaign away to Bayern Munich on Tuesday.

City are given the fourth-highest chance of winning the Champions League by the Opta supercomputer, though their 9.1% win probability is significantly lower than outright favourites Barcelona (41.2%).
Greenwood insists City have their eyes on the trophy, though.
"To qualify was massively important; it's an expectation that we have at this football club," Greenwood told UEFA's website.
"But every competition that we play in, we're there to win.

"We know it's going to be a challenge, but it's fantastic for the club. We're going to give it absolutely everything, like we do in every other competition, take it game by game and see how far we can go."
City are facing a German side for the first time in the Champions League.

Bayern, meanwhile, have won seven of their previous 11 matches against English teams in the competition (L4), including both legs of last season's quarter-final against Manchester United (3-2 A, 2-1 H).
On their last Champions League appearance in 2024-25, City lost their last two away games, both by a 3-0 scoreline to Barcelona and Chelsea, respectively.
"I've played in this competition enough times to know what it presents and what the challenges are," Greenwood added.
"We worked really hard to get back in this competition where I think we belong. I'm just excited to embrace the challenge.
"Champions League, Women's Super League, whatever competition we're in, we're in it with a real elite mindset to go and win, and that's been our mentality for the last 18 months."

4sv8g3qeperh1e4w49upqy18l.title: Women's Super League predictions: Can Man City pull clear as Chelsea and Arsenal face off?
4sv8g3qeperh1e4w49upqy18l.subtitle: Manchester City's 100% start will be put to the test against Charlton Athletic, while Chelsea face Arsenal in the blockbuster clash of MD4.
paragraphs: After three matchdays in the Women's Super League season, defending champions Manchester City remain the only team with a 100% record, following their frantic 4-2 victory over Liverpool last time out.

After drawing 2-2 with Bayern Munich in their Champions League opener on Tuesday, City visit Charlton Athletic – who are the only team yet to pick up a point – to kickstart the week's action on Saturday, before the focus turns to their potential title rivals.
Neither Chelsea nor Arsenal have suffered a defeat yet this term, but with both sides already off City's pace, their head-to-head clash at Stamford Bridge on Sunday looks vital.
There is also a Merseyside derby between Liverpool and Everton, while Manchester United will look to finally earn their first league victory under Eva Olid, at home to West Ham.
Who will come out on top in the WSL this weekend? We have a look at the Opta supercomputer's predictions for matchday four.
CHARLTON ATHLETIC V MANCHESTER CITY

With Manchester City making a perfect start and Charlton recording three straight defeats since their promotion, it should come as little surprise that our predictive model makes Andree Jeglertz's champions the clearest MD4 favourites, with a 75.6% win probability to Charlton's 10.6%.
Only once in the last eight campaigns have City enjoyed a longer winning start than this one, winning each of their first four matches in 2019-20.
But they will be supremely confident of matching that feat at The Valley, in what will be their first competitive meeting with Charlton in the WSL era.
Promoted sides have won just one of their last 28 meetings with the reigning champions in the competition (D3 L24), with Liverpool recording a 2-1 home victory over Chelsea in September 2022.

Last time out, Khadija Shaw became the first player to score in each of City's first three games of a WSL campaign, and she could become the fifth player to do so in the first four matches of a season for any club, after Kim Little in 2018-19 (four for Arsenal), Vivianne Miedema in 2020-21 (five for Arsenal), Martha Thomas in 2023-24 (four for Tottenham) and Aggie Beever-Jones in 2025-26 (four for Chelsea).
LONDON CITY LIONESSES V BRIGHTON
Charlton's last game was a thumping 4-1 defeat to the ambitious London City Lionesses, who have six points on the board after three games and sit fourth in the table ahead of facing winless Brighton.
Alexia Putellas and company are assigned a 52.9% win probability on Saturday, with Brighton only winning 23% of the supercomputer's pre-match simulations.

London City's three wins in their last four WSL matches (L1) are more than they managed across their previous 12 in the competition (W2 D3 L7), and their nine 'big' chances against Charlton last week were the most by any team in a WSL game since October 2020 (when Man Utd had 10 versus Brighton).

The Seagulls could fail to win their opening four matches of a WSL campaign for the third time after 2018-19 (first six) and 2019-20 (first five), and they have lost seven of their last nine league games in London.
MANCHESTER UNITED V WEST HAM
Olid got her first win in charge of Manchester United in the Women's League Cup on Wednesday, with a 10-1 thrashing of Sheffield United, and they will now look to translate that into a WSL victory.
They are given a 68% chance of beating West Ham – whose chances sit at 14.3% – having gone unbeaten in their last 12 league games against the Hammers (W8 D4).

United are winless in their first three WSL matches (D1 L2) for the first time and have lost two of their last three home games in the competition (D1), as many defeats as they suffered in their previous 20 (W12 D6).
West Ham struggle on their travels against the Red Devils, though, having lost each of their six such games in the WSL by an aggregate score of 1-19.
They have only won one of their three games this term (L2), but given United have attempted just 10 shots in the WSL in 2026-27, they might feel this is a good chance to get one over on them.
BIRMINGHAM CITY V CRYSTAL PALACE
Two of the new teams at this level face off, with Birmingham City seeking their first victory since promotion while Crystal Palace try to get back to winning ways.
Palace were the only team to do the league double over WSL2 champions Birmingham last season – the Eagles have actually won each of their last four league matches against the Blues.
However, it is Birmingham who are backed to come out on top on Sunday with a 44.7% win probability to Palace's 28.4%. Though at 26.9%, this is one of the most likely draws of the weekend.

Birmingham could start a WSL campaign without a win in four games (D1 L2 so far) for the third time, but Amy Merricks will be determined to halt her nine-match winless streak as a manager in the top flight (D3 L6).
Liverpool were 3-2 winners against Everton back in March and could win consecutive WSL games against the Toffees for the first time since 2013 and 2014 (three straight).

The Reds are marginal favourites to prevail in Sunday's derby, despite losing eight of their nine previous league games played at Anfield, including five against Everton. They are given a 44% chance of victory.

Only Man City (11), Chelsea and Arsenal (both 10) have won more WSL games in 2026 than Everton (seven), who could win three league matches in a row for the second time this calendar year (won four in a row in February).
Everton's chances of winning away to their Merseyside rivals are 29.1%, but this is the other most likely draw of the weekend, with 26.9% of the simulations finishing level.
TOTTENHAM V ASTON VILLA
After three matchdays, Tottenham are in the mix at the top, sitting second and just two points behind Man City, having made an unbeaten start to the season (W2 D1).

They are actually unbeaten in their last six league games and could go seven straight without defeat for the first time in the league's history; they have a 57.7% chance of extending that run with a win.

Aston Villa have won three of their last five WSL away games against Spurs (D1 L1), but they come into this match having drawn their last two league games on the road. There is a 22% chance of them adding a third draw to that run.
The Villans have not yet gone ahead in any of their three league games, something they must do if they are to turn their 20.3% win probability into a first victory of the season.
The spotlight clash of the matchday sees Chelsea and Arsenal look to keep the pressure on Man City and extend their respective unbeaten starts.
Arsenal (20) and Chelsea (11) are on the two longest unbeaten runs in the WSL currently.

And Chelsea are looking to go unbeaten in their opening four games for the fourth successive WSL season, while Arsenal could win as few as five points from their first four matches for the second time in the last three seasons (after 2024-25).

This will be the 10th meeting between Chelsea and Arsenal in all competitions since the 2023-24 season, with both teams picking up four wins apiece in that time (D1), though the Gunners won the most recent league meeting at Stamford Bridge 2-0, back in January.
Chelsea are the favourites to triumph, winning 51.9% of the supercomputer's simulations, compared to Arsenal's 23.6%.
And Renee Slegers will be determined to have her say, having already beaten Sonia Bompastor twice in all competitions this calendar year – no manager has ever won three in a row against her.

Everton's chances of winning away to their Merseyside rivals are 29.1%, but this is the other most likely draw of the weekend, with 26.9% of the simulations finishing level.

TOTTENHAM V ASTON VILLA

After three matchdays, Tottenham are in the mix at the top, sitting second and just two points behind Man City, having made an unbeaten start to the season (W2 D1).

They are actually unbeaten in their last six league games and could go seven straight without defeat for the first time in the league's history; they have a 57.7% chance of extending that run with a win.

Aston Villa have won three of their last five WSL away games against Spurs (D1 L1), but they come into this match having drawn their last two league games on the road. There is a 22% chance of them adding a third draw to that run.

The Villans have not yet gone ahead in any of their three league games, something they must do if they are to turn their 20.3% win probability into a first victory of the season.

CHELSEA V ARSENAL

The spotlight clash of the matchday sees Chelsea and Arsenal look to keep the pressure on Man City and extend their respective unbeaten starts.

Arsenal (20) and Chelsea (11) are on the two longest unbeaten runs in the WSL currently.

And Chelsea are looking to go unbeaten in their opening four games for the fourth successive WSL season, while Arsenal could win as few as five points from their first four matches for the second time in the last three seasons (after 2024-25).

This will be the 10th meeting between Chelsea and Arsenal in all competitions since the 2023-24 season, with both teams picking up four wins apiece in that time (D1), though the Gunners won the most recent league meeting at Stamford Bridge 2-0, back in January.

Chelsea are the favourites to triumph, winning 51.9% of the supercomputer's simulations, compared to Arsenal's 23.6%.

And Renee Slegers will be determined to have her say, having already beaten Sonia Bompastor twice in all competitions this calendar year – no manager has ever won three in a row against her.

4ugjg5li8qod1oy7dyoc6i1kb.title: Juventus goalkeeper Grabara undergoes successful ACL surgery
4ugjg5li8qod1oy7dyoc6i1kb.subtitle: Kamil Grabara faces up to seven months on the sidelines after sustaining a serious injury on his debut for Juventus in the Europa League.
paragraphs: Juventus have confirmed Kamil Grabara has undergone successful surgery to reconstruct the anterior cruciate (ACL) ligament in his knee.
Grabara sustained the injury during a training session just two days after making his debut for Juventus during a 5-0 victory over NEC in the Europa League.
The 27-year-old, who is on a season-long loan with the Serie A giants from Wolfsburg, provided the assist for Nico Gonzalez's opener at Allianz Stadium.
However, it is believed the Poland international will now face up to seven months on the sidelines, following a summer of changes in the goalkeeping department at Juventus.
The Bianconeri allowed Michele Di Gregorio and Mattia Perin to leave the club, while also bringing in Guglielmo Vicario on loan from Premier League side Tottenham.
"Kamil Grabara underwent surgery this afternoon to reconstruct the anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee," Juventus said in a statement.
"The procedure, performed at the Guardian Clinic in Konin by Dr Andrzej Pyda, in the presence of Juventus Club Doctor Dr Marco Freschi, was a complete success.
"The player will begin his rehabilitation programme in the coming days, with a view to returning to competitive action."
With the transfer window now shut, Juventus are reportedly close to agreeing a deal with Neto, who previously played in Turin between 2015 and 2017.
Neto is a free agent following the termination of his contract with Botafogo in June, and he is set to sign until the end of the season, according to reports.
The Brazilian played 22 times across all competitions during his previous stint with Juventus, keeping 12 clean sheets and winning five major honours.
Since his exit from Juventus nine years ago, he has gone on to represent Valencia, Barcelona, Bournemouth, Arsenal and most recently, Botafogo.
Juventus are seventh in Serie A after their first five games of the season, and they return to action after the international break against Cagliari on October 11.

4x2jogj427ih1sthlaz3k388x.title: Hall says Newcastle contract renewal was 'a no-brainer' amid Man Utd rumours
4x2jogj427ih1sthlaz3k388x.subtitle: Manchester United were tipped to move for Lewis Hall this summer, but the left-back eventually signed a new contract with Newcastle United.
paragraphs: Lewis Hall says it was "a no-brainer" to sign a new long-term contract with Newcastle United, despite attracting interest from Manchester United throughout the summer.
Earlier this month, Hall ended speculation over his immediate future by penning fresh terms with the Magpies, with his new deal reportedly running until 2031.
Having joined his boyhood club from Chelsea in 2023, Hall has made 109 appearances for Newcastle in all competitions, with 82 of those being starts.
He helped Newcastle end their 70-year domestic trophy drought by winning the EFL Cup in 2025, though a foot injury caused him to miss their victory over Liverpool in the final.
Hall has also started 2026-27 strongly under new boss Mathias Jaissle, providing two assists in all competitions and scoring his first goal of the campaign in Saturday's 2-1 home win over Hull City.
Asked by Chronicle Live if he ever felt like he had a difficult decision to make amid loud transfer speculation, Hall said: "No, honestly, it didn't.
"I guess whenever you're linked to another team, you know that you're doing something right. It's a credit to your own performances and how you are as a player, and how you are as a person.
"I took that as a positive, but at the same time, I love playing here and since the manager came in, I knew the ambitions and what we wanted to achieve.
"After not many conversations, not many training sessions, I knew that the manager was going to be really good for this club.
"I knew that as a team, bringing in new players and improving the squad was really important and as soon as we did that, it was a no-brainer to sign."

Hall was recently recalled to the England squad by Thomas Tuchel ahead of Nations League fixtures against Spain, Czechia (home and away) and Croatia, having missed out on the Three Lions' group for the World Cup.
And looking long-term, Hall believes being at St James' Park allows him to fulfil his ambitions, saying: "When you're with a team, you don't think too far into the future.
"Obviously, I'm really grateful for the contract that I've received and the trust that I've been given from the board and from the manager.
"I'm just taking it game by game, just trying to do the best I can for this club. We've got ambitions and as long as we achieve what we want to achieve, I'm sure I'll be here for a long time."
With eight points on the board from five Premier League games, Newcastle face Coventry City in their first game after the international break, on October 12.

50D8E5F6D50030B36E27C4C6F51ACF5D.title: Raphinha: The most in-form player in Europe has made a blistering start to 2026/27
50D8E5F6D50030B36E27C4C6F51ACF5D.subtitle: FotMob
paragraphs: NewsAboutTV schedulesRaphinha: The most in-form player in Europe has made a blistering start to 2026/27Share“It’s a joke!” Luis García didn’t mince his words following Sevilla’s 3-1 defeat to Barcelona at the weekend. And no, he wasn’t referring to a dodgy refereeing decision, or a defensive mishap that caused his side to crumble on home turf. Rather, he was referring to the 2026 Ballon d’Or.

Specifically, Raphinha’s omission from 30-man nomination list. Barcelona are well represented in the lead up to the individual award. Spanish trio Lamine Yamal, Rodri and Pau Cubarsí are the Blaugrana contingent in the running for the accolade, though in truth; only the former pair are genuine contenders for the 2026 award.

Even so, Raphinha at present is outperforming the trio, and, in truth, the other 27 players to make the cut for the prestigious gong. Indeed, the brilliant Brazilian has been directly involved in a goal in every competitive appearance for Hansi Flick’s men this season. He’s scored in all but one of eight outings, and even then; he provided a brace of assists as the defending LaLiga champions claimed a 4-2 win at Levante.

Saturday’s perfect hat-trick – the former Leeds United scored one with his right, another with his left, and the third with his head – took him to 12 league goals for the season. Even the great Lionel Messi failed to achieve the feat after the opening seven games of a league campaign at Barcelona.

What’s all the more important is that Raphinha’s form has come at a time when Barcelona ended the summer transfer window, arguably, a forward short. Marcus Rashford was replaced by Anthony Gordon. Karim Adeyemi’s arrival eased Ferran Torres’ move to Paris Saint-Germain. They ruthlessly pushed for Atlético Madrid hitman Julián Alvarez in their quest to replace Robert Lewandowski.

Naturally, Barcelona were never going to trigger Alvarez’s €500m release clause, and they needn’t have bothered with their pursuit of the Argentine. Turns out Barcelona had the perfect Lewandowski successor the whole time.

Joining for £69.3m, Gordon was never going to sign as a backup for the Brazil international on the left. Yamal is one of the first names on the team sheet down the right. Crowbarring Raphinha into the side could have backfired on Flick and Barcelona. In hindsight, it’s proven a masterstroke.

The 29-year-old has been granted the license to drift across the pitch not just in search of possession, but in order to drag markers out of position. Flick deploys inverted widemen in his favoured 4-3-3 setup. Left winger Gordon favours his right foot. Right winger Yamal prefers his left.

Raphinha’s willingness to drop a little deeper opens up space for the pair to exploit. He’s not a conventional number nine by any stretch, so there is no point acting like one. What is key, though, is that Raphinha is also capitalising upon the space he creates.

Speed has so often been a strong point of the forward’s game. When Raphinha switches on the afterburners, good luck keeping up with him. In wide areas, he had to cover greater distances to get into goalscoring areas. Now, his speed off the mark means he really comes alive inside the opposition box when he makes darting runs into the penalty area.

42 touches inside the opposition box ranks fifth in LaLiga this season. For context, Real Madrid’s Kylian Mbappé (85) tops this metric. The Frenchman spends more time in the area, because this plays to his strengths. For Raphinha, that lightning quick turn of pace so often bamboozles opposition defences.

It’s no coincidence that all 12 of his league goals this season have been scored inside the penalty area. Granted, three of them are penalties. Yet even so, Barcelona are proving even more potent when they break forward then last season, which is some going for a team that scored more goals (95) than any other team in the 2025/26 LaLiga campaign.

After all, their average of 4.43 league goals per game is almost double last season’s haul (2.5). Much of that is due to the speed of their attack having scored more counter-attacking goals (4) than any other team in Spain’s top tier. Raphinha has struck two of those. 14 shots following a counter attack is the third most in the division.

Crucially, too, is that not only is Raphinha able to get on the end of the ample chances that are created by this rampant Barcelona side, he’s proving incredibly efficient in front of goal. Of the 135 players to have managed at least five shots, only Pape Gueye (50%) boasts a better conversion rate than Raphinha (48%). The former has managed six shots. The latter has had 25. 11 of his 12 goals have been deemed big chances.

Back to García’s comments, however, and recency bias does play a part. That’s not suggesting Raphinha doesn’t deserve his flowers. He’s the most in-form player in Europe at present. Rather, over the course of the calendar year, the Barca star hasn’t quite hit the lofty heights, and that is through no fault of his own.

Injuries have wreaked havoc on both his playing time and his consistency. It’s denied Raphinha the chance to gain a head of steam for both club and country. As such, Flick’s use of the forward will prove beneficial for the player as he relies on shorter, sharper bursts rather than prolonged sprints that increase the likelihood of muscle injuries.

And if he can avoid a reoccurrence of those pesky problems going forward, then he’ll undoubtedly be in the running for the 2027 award. Barcelona are tearing opponents to shreds without showing a modicum of sympathy. If he can fire them to domestic and continental glory, then he’ll be in the running.

5f3te9ge6hyk1dia3ufms1lxc.title: Pocognoli using experience of Belgium's 'golden generation' to handle Scotland pressure
5f3te9ge6hyk1dia3ufms1lxc.subtitle: Scotland start the Sebastien Pocognoli era on Saturday, and he wants pressure to become something that motivates, not hinders, his team.
paragraphs: Sebastien Pocognoli feels his experiences in the early days of Belgium's "golden generation" can help him manage expectations with Scotland, as he prepares for his first game in charge.

Scotland open their Nations League campaign in Slovenia on Saturday, with Switzerland and North Macedonia their other opponents in Group B1, having been relegated from the competition's top tier under Steve Clarke in 2024-25.

Clarke did lead Scotland to a second successive major tournament – and a record third under his watch – at the World Cup, but they suffered a meek group-stage exit following defeats against Morocco and Brazil.
Pocognoli is returning to international management, having coached Belgium's under-18 side before having stints in charge of Union Saint-Gilloise and Monaco in the club game.
And he feels he has learned plenty about managing the pressure that comes with the international game, having been part of Belgium's much-feted "golden generation".

Pocognoli played alongside Vincent Kompany, Thomas Vermaelen, Jan Vertonghen and Mousa Dembele at the 2008 Olympic Games – a tournament where Belgium lost the bronze-medal match – before winning 13 senior caps between 2008 and 2014.

He never appeared at a major tournament for his country, with his final cap coming in 2014 World Cup qualifying, but he saw how the pressure to deliver silverware weighed on a squad that also featured Eden Hazard, Kevin De Bruyne and Romelu Lukaku.
"In my own case, I was part of the 'golden generation' at the start," he said. "I made the first step. We made the Olympic Games, and I was part of the [2014] qualification.

"But for me, there were high expectations on the Belgian players – an over-expectation. It was too much. It is a country of 12 million people, and you have to deal with France and Germany next to you, and England.
"There were fantastic players and that Belgium team reached third place in the [2018] World Cup. Fantastic. They were first in the FIFA rankings for five or six years. You can't do more than that.
"Maybe with some luck you can win a medal, but there was over-expectation and I think that generation reached its best, to be honest."
Though the expectations surrounding Scotland are not as sky-high as those that Belgium failed to meet, Pocognoli wants to make pressure a motivating factor for his team.
"Yes, the bar is very high," Pocognoli said. "I know this. But you have to deal with this heritage. The heritage is massively positive, so use it.
"If I put this as a pressure, we are not going to go the right way. I have to use it as a benefit to embrace."
Scotland – who are building towards a home European Championship campaign in 2028 – will welcome Switzerland to Hampden Park next Tuesday, for their first home game under Pocognoli.

5xpun2m97xi71abl4ti4mrx2n.title: Wales have 'puncher's chance' against Portugal and 'alien' Ronaldo, says James
5xpun2m97xi71abl4ti4mrx2n.subtitle: Wales visit Portugal for their opening Nations League match on Thursday, with the Selecao still led by Cristiano Ronaldo.
paragraphs: Wales have a "puncher's chance" of upsetting Portugal in their Nations League opener on Thursday, even if the Selecao can still call upon an "alien" in Cristiano Ronaldo.
That is the view of midfielder Jordan James, as Craig Bellamy's side prepare for their League A campaign following promotion from the second tier in 2024-25.
Wales topped Group B4 in the last edition of the Nations League, ahead of Turkiye, Iceland and Montenegro, and their reward is a place in Group A4 this time around, with Portugal, Denmark and Norway.
While Wales went unbeaten in the 2024-25 Nations League (W3 D3), their last campaign in the top tier saw them go winless and earn the fewest points of any nation (D1 L5).
Portugal are, of course, the reigning Nations League holders, having beaten Spain on penalties in the 2024-25 final to win the competition for the second time.

And ahead of Thursday's matchup at Sporting CP's Estadio Jose Alvalade, they have won 11 of their 14 home matches in the competition overall (D1 L2), only losing to France (in November 2020) and Spain (September 2022).
But James – who has helped Wolves make a strong start in the Championship after arriving in a loan-to-buy deal from Rennes – says that fixture will hold no fear for Wales.
"Obviously, they're the best players in the world at the end of the day, you can't really sugarcoat it," James said, as quoted by BBC Sport.
"They've got Champions League winners, they've got these kinds of things. I think we're always underdogs. We're used to it, so hopefully we can use that to benefit ourselves.
"You can't count us out. We've got a puncher's chance at the end of the day and we're going there to cause an upset."
Thursday's game will be Portugal's first under Jorge Jesus, who succeeded Roberto Martinez following their round-of-16 exit from the World Cup.
Jesus previously managed Ronaldo at Al-Nassr last season, with the five-time Ballon d'Or winner scoring 29 goals in 33 appearances under him, hitting the net once every 99 minutes on average.

Ronaldo opted against following Lionel Messi's example and retiring from international football following the World Cup, with the 41-year-old set to continue representing his country for the time being.
Asked about Ronaldo's quality, James said: "We're all trying to achieve the same thing, to be the best player in the world. But you get those aliens that don't seem human.

"You look at Messi, Neymar, Ronaldo – they've just got that extra little quality where, in big moments, they turn up and can do it again and again and again. I think that's the main thing. The longevity of how they're able to do it is unbelievable."

Wales missed out on the World Cup after losing on penalties to Bosnia-Herzegovina in a play-off semi-final in March, and their current four-match winless run (D3 L1) is both their worst under Bellamy and their worst start to a calendar year since 2012 (five straight losses).

607geboi7jtx1xo74xelclhr8.title: Malen withdraws from Netherlands squad through injury
607geboi7jtx1xo74xelclhr8.subtitle: Donyell Malen will not get the chance to extend his brilliant start to the season with the Netherlands, with injury ruling him out.
paragraphs: Donyell Malen has withdrawn from the Netherlands' squad for their upcoming Nations League matches.
Malen has been in red-hot form for Roma in Serie A so far this season, and despite playing the full 90 minutes against Inter on Saturday, he will not represent his country due to injury.
It has not been specified what Malen's issue is, but he is one of two withdrawals, with Justin Kluivert also pulling out.

Since his Serie A debut on January 18, Malen has scored 20 goals in 23 appearances, at least twice as many as any other player in the competition in that period (Tasos Douvikas and Lautaro Martinez are next with 10).
Across Europe's big five leagues, he has scored more than any other player (Harry Kane and Raphinha have 18).
Malen has already netted six goals in Serie A this term, more than any other player, over-performing his 4.6 expected goals (xG).
He has also had more shots on target (10) than any other player and currently boasts a 57.5 minutes per goal rate in the Italian top-flight.
Xavi Hernandez, who is taking charge of the Netherlands for the first time during this extended international break, has called up Guus Til and Mexx Meerdink as replacements.
The Netherlands face Germany in their opening Nations League match on September 24, before facing Serbia away and at home on either side of their clash with Greece.

Across Europe's big five leagues, he has scored more than any other player (Harry Kane and Raphinha have 18).

Malen has already netted six goals in Serie A this term, more than any other player, over-performing his 4.6 expected goals (xG).

He has also had more shots on target (10) than any other player and currently boasts a 57.5 minutes per goal rate in the Italian top-flight.

Xavi Hernandez, who is taking charge of the Netherlands for the first time during this extended international break, has called up Guus Til and Mexx Meerdink as replacements.

The Netherlands face Germany in their opening Nations League match on September 24, before facing Serbia away and at home on either side of their clash with Greece.

7f7vw8sd056e14cgu0lejgtqu.title: Mac Allister says 'no firm decision' over Liverpool future amid contract dispute
7f7vw8sd056e14cgu0lejgtqu.subtitle: Alexis Mac Allister recently said he had opportunities to leave Liverpool during the summer transfer window, with no new contract on offer.
paragraphs: Alexis Mac Allister says there is still "no firm decision" on his future with Liverpool, with the Reds yet to offer the midfielder a new contract.
Earlier this month, Mac Allister made headlines by saying Liverpool had informed him they were not in a position to offer him fresh terms, after he entered the final two years of his deal.

Mac Allister, who has won a Premier League title and the EFL Cup since arriving from Brighton in 2023, said he was "very sad" to have had no negotiations with the club, after his fellow midfielders Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai penned new deals.
Mac Allister has retained a key role for Liverpool since Andoni Iraola took charge, making seven appearances in all competitions this season with five of those being starts.

The 27-year-old has now linked up with Argentina for a series of friendlies against Bolivia, Burkina Faso and Benin, the latter of which will serve as a farewell match for Lionel Messi after he announced his international retirement.
And in an interview with ESPN, Mac Allister said there had been no progress on resolving his contract stand-off.
"There's no firm decision yet. I still have two years left on my contract. As I said, I'm going to give it my all. A lot can happen in that time; there are plenty of options," Mac Allister said.
"Hopefully it'll be for more years, but if it's just two, I'll have to enjoy them with my family, because I have no doubt that I'm at one of the best clubs in the world."

The nature of Messi's involvement in the game against Benin – set for October 5 at the Estadio Monumental in Buenos Aires – remains unclear, but it will bring the curtain down on one of the all-time great international careers.
Messi has scored 125 goals in 207 appearances for La Albiceleste, with eight of those coming at the 2026 World Cup.

No player has directly contributed to more goals at the World Cup on record (since 1966) than Messi (33 – 21 goals and 12 assists), who has also featured in the most games at the finals (34). Messi's 12 assists at FIFA's flagship competition are also the most of any player, four more than the great Diego Maradona (eight, since 1966).
And though he fell narrowly short of delivering a second straight title in North America this year, Mac Allister feels Messi should be in contention for a record-extending ninth Ballon d'Or.
"Obviously, as Argentines we'd love for Messi to win it. He had an incredible World Cup and I don't see why he shouldn't be awarded it," he said.

"Also, it's understood that these days the numbers play a big part – something that didn't carry as much weight in the past – and you don't know exactly what people are voting for either. But everyone in the running is a great player; anyone who comes close will deserve it.
"We all know that Leo has always prioritised the team over individual achievements, so it wouldn't be a big deal for him."

7hm5xdmmefsy13b5vntbu54rb.title: Quill backs Dallas to 'be better' than in Austin draw
7hm5xdmmefsy13b5vntbu54rb.subtitle: Both FC Dallas and Los Angeles FC are looking to get back to winning ways after draws last time out, with hopes of climbing the table.
paragraphs: FC Dallas head coach Eric Quill is confident his team will "be better" than their last performance when they host Los Angeles FC in MLS on Saturday.
Dallas head into the match on the back of a five-match unbeaten streak, but after three straight wins, they were held to a 0-0 draw by Austin FC last time out.
It was just the seventh time this season they have been shut out – as they are the second-highest scorers in the Western Conference.
They currently sit fourth in the West, but are one of three teams on 44 points, and they know a win could help them close the gap to the leaders Vancouver Whitecaps.
Quill is looking for a big improvement from the performance against Austin, especially in the final third.
"It wasn't our typical game," Quill said of the draw with Austin. "I think everybody's used to four goals from us, so it wasn't there.
"But it wasn't for a lack of trying or a lack of opportunities that we created.
"We'll work in front of goal, get our confidence up and go into LAFC ready.
"[The players were] down because ties don't excite us, but there's plenty more football to come from us, and we're going to be better for this game."
LAFC, meanwhile, are sixth in the West, three points behind Dallas after failing to win their last two matches.
Following a shock 3-1 loss to Sporting Kansas City, they threw away a lead against the San Jose Earthquakes, conceding a 98th-minute equaliser.
Son Heung-min and Denis Bouanga both scored in that game but are among the list of absentees due to international duty. Head coach Marc Dos Santos is not making any excuses, though.
"We never approach the week crying about who's not here," he said.
"We have seven players out, but we embrace from day one of preparing as best as we can for the Dallas game with everybody that is here."
FC Dallas – Joaquin Valiente
Joaquin Valiente has recorded 11 assists for Dallas this season, the first player to have double-digit assists in a single season for the club since Michael Barrios had 15 in 2019.

Over the last 15 seasons, four Dallas players have had 10+ assists in a season and all hail from South American countries (Valiente – Uruguay, Barrios – Colombia, Maximiliano Urruti and Mauro Diaz – Argentina).
Los Angeles FC – Mathieu Choiniere
Son and Bouanga are both on international duty and will miss the match have combined to score half of LAFC's regular-season goals (20/40 excl. own goals) in 2026.

With David Martinez (six goals) also departing in September, that means Mathieu Choiniere is the club's next highest scorer with two goals, but he did not manage a single shot against San Jose and only had one touch in the opposition box.
MATCH PREDICTION: FC DALLAS WIN
Dallas have won four of their 15 regular-season meetings with Los Angeles FC (D3 L8), with all four of those wins coming at home.
They have lost just once (W4 D2) at home to LAFC, conceding multiple goals only once, while scoring two or more goals five times.

Dallas have also scored two or more goals in seven of their last 10 home games, and four of their last five. Since the start of the 2024 season, they have registered two or more goals in 29 home games, with only Inter Miami (37) having more in that time.

LAFC surrendered a late goal to San Jose for their fourth draw in their last six road games (L2). They have now drawn six road games this regular season and 13 total over the last two seasons combined after drawing 12 total road regular-season matches from 2022-24.
Los Angeles FC – 29.1%

867tayfi2f0r1ccqj3oifli5s.title: Jansen insists NYCFC 'will deal with' international absentees
867tayfi2f0r1ccqj3oifli5s.subtitle: Both New York City FC and Atlanta United will be without key players for their MLS clash at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on Saturday.
paragraphs: Pascal Jansen expressed his disappointment in losing New York City FC players to the international break, but insists they "will deal with it" ahead of their trip to Atlanta United.
NYCFC are 10th in the Eastern Conference with just one MLS win since the Leagues Cup break after losing to rivals New York Red Bulls last time out.
Jansen will now be without goalkeeper Matt Freese against Atlanta, as well as defender Tayvon Gray and midfielder Aiden O'Neill, among a group of five players on international duty.
Jansen admitted some adjustments will be needed when they face Atlanta, but he is eager to pick up three points at Mercedes-Benz Stadium.
"That's something that still amazes me in this league, that we have to play during a national team break," said the NYCFC boss.
"But it is what it is and we will deal with it. Unfortunately, we're coming off a tough game against Red Bull [a 1-0 loss]. I think we deserved more from that game.

"But now it's all full focus on Atlanta and we know we have a chance there, but we have to adjust a couple of things because there’s a few guys not available and this time not because of injury, because of international duty."
Atlanta, meanwhile, ended a four-game winless run in MLS with a 1-0 win over the Portland Timbers last time out.
The Five Stripes will also be missing key players against NYCFC, with Miguel Almiron and Aleksey Miranchuk both on international duty.

Since the start of last season, Miranchuk has recorded 95 chances created while Almiron has 87. They are the only pair of teammates to each create 80 or more chances since the start of the 2025 campaign, with both players setting up at least 40 shots for team-mates in each of the last two seasons.
Atlanta United – Matt Edwards
Due to players on international duty, Matt Edwards could start in defence for Atlanta.
After coming off the bench against Portland last time out, Edwards led his team-mates in interceptions (three) and aerial duels won (two), while winning five of his 10 duels overall.
New York City FC – Nicolas Fernandez Mercau
Nicolas Fernandez Mercau has been involved in 22 goals in his first full season with New York City FC (15 goals, seven assists).
Only three players in club history have contributed to more goals in a single regular season (David Villa, Maxi Moralez, Valentin Castellanos) with Castellanos the last to do so, in 2021 (27).
MATCH PREDICTION: ATLANTA UNITED WIN

Atlanta have suffered only two defeats in eight matches since returning from the Leagues Cup break in August (W4 D2). Only four Eastern Conference teams have collected more points than the Five Stripes (14) over that time.
And they have lost only one of nine all-time home matches against New York City FC (W4 D4), including a 4-3 win in the last meeting at Mercedes-Benz Stadium in March 2025.
Atlanta are one of two Eastern Conference teams (also Nashville SC) against whom NYCFC do not have multiple road wins.

NYCFC have managed just one win in their last nine regular-season matches (D4 L4), while their defeat to NYRB was their 10th loss of the year. NYCFC have lost 11 or more games in each of the previous five seasons after recording 10 or fewer losses in five straight seasons from 2016 to 2020.
Atlanta United – 44.4%
New York City FC – 31.3%

          Man City's Resilience, Lyon Dominate, Questions for Chelsea & Arsenal: UWCL Matchday 1 Lessons
        
      
                          
                      Sep 24, 2026
          
                      Maya Shah / Author, Yash Thakur / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
Matchday 1 of the 2026-27 UEFA Women's Champions League delivered drama, dominant displays and plenty of talking points. We dive into the data to analyse the key stories from the action.
The 2026-27 UEFA Women's Champions League is underway and Matchday 1 delivered a little bit of everything.
There were narrow wins, thrashings and end-to-end contests as Europe's elite began their quest for continental glory.
Using Opta data, we break down the standout performers and biggest talking points from the opening matchday of this season's UWCL.
The reigning WSL champions began their UWCL campaign with one of the toughest assignments possible, travelling to Munich to face a Bayern side ranked second in the Opta Power Rankings.
The contest delivered everything expected of two European heavyweights: goals, a missed penalty and late drama, with the points ultimately shared in a 2-2 draw.
In doing so, City became the first English side to avoid defeat at Bayern Munich in the UWCL.

It was the first time in City’s history in the competition they had avoided defeat when trailing by two or more goals, while it was just the second time Bayern had failed to win a UWCL game in which they had led by 2+ goals, last doing so against Roma in November 2023.
José Barcala's team asserted themselves early, racing into a two-goal lead before the break. Their aggressive pressing forced City into mistakes, with Bayern recording 16 high turnovers.
Since 2019-20, only against Barcelona in December 2024 (25) and March 2021 (17) have City conceded more high turnovers in the competition.
City struggled to gain a foothold before half-time, managing only three attempts. But Beth Mead's goal shifted the momentum after the interval.

The visitors were then handed a golden opportunity to level from the penalty spot, only forEna Mahmutovic to brilliantly deny Khadija Shaw. It was the first penalty Shaw has missed since joining Manchester City.

Despite that setback, City continued to push and their persistence was rewarded in the 86th minute when Carlotta Wamser found the equaliser to complete the comeback with her first goal in light blue, and secure a valuable point on the road.
Andrée Jeglertz's influence from the bench again proved significant, as had been the case against Liverpool.

Second-half substitute Laura Blindkilde Brown provided the assist for Wamser's goal and helped City gain greater control in possession, offering composure against Bayern's intense press as the visitors finished the stronger of the two sides.
Arsenal and Chelsea both opened their European campaigns with 1-0 victories against HB Køge and Austria Wien respectively, but neither performance fully convinced.
With a heavyweight WSL meeting at Stamford Bridge looming this weekend, both sides left MD1 with three points, but just as many questions remain.
Arsenal needed a stoppage-time Mariona Caldentey penalty to overcome Danish champions Køge in a game they largely controlled but struggled to break open.
Renée Slegers' side monopolised possession, recording 69.7% of the ball and completing 620 passes at an 86% success rate, but their dominance rarely translated into clear-cut opportunities.

Despite attempting 19 shots, Arsenal generated only one big chance and managed just a single effort on target prior to Caldentey's winning penalty. It was another example of a recurring issue for the Gunners: controlling games without creating enough high-quality chances.

8aqj1c1phdxczwjolw9tv6cf.title: Bayern Munich 2-2 Manchester City: Wamser rescues draw in Women's Champions League opener
8aqj1c1phdxczwjolw9tv6cf.subtitle: Bayern Munich led 2-0 against Manchester City, but the Women's Super League champions fought back to salvage a point at Uhlsport Park.
paragraphs: Khadija Shaw missed a penalty but Carlotta Wamser's late goal saw Manchester City rescue a 2-2 draw in their Women's Champions League opener against Bayern Munich.
Bayern, last season's semi-finalists, charged into a 2-0 lead inside the first 28 minutes at Uhlsport Park.
Giulia Gwinn was played in by Linda Dallmann and made no mistake with a crisp, powerful finish.

Bayern were then in cruise control when they capitalised on a defensive mix-up from Man City, with Pernille Harder's cross causing havoc, and Kerstin Casparij was only able to turn it into her own net.
Yet, on the cusp of half-time, Beth Mead dragged City back into the contest as Casparij's cross found its way through to her, and she duly tucked home.
City looked all set to draw level around the hour mark, after Aoba Fujino was brought down by Ena Mahmutovic in Bayern's box.
Shaw, though, showed unusual profligacy as she saw her attempt saved by Mahmutovic, who atoned for her mistake.
Yet City did get their equaliser in the 86th minute, with Wamser whipping a fine effort in at the near post after she met Laura Blindkilde Brown's tee-up.
Man City show powers of recovery
City have made a fantastic start to their Women's Super League title defence, winning all three of their matches so far, but they endured a miserable opening half-an-hour of their European campaign.
This was their first meeting against Bayern, or indeed any German team, in this competition, although City should probably have expected their hosts to make a fast start.
After all, Bayern had won seven of their previous 11 Champions League matches against English teams, including both legs of last season's quarter-final against Manchester United (3-2 A, 2-1 H).
Harder is just one off scoring her 50th Women's Champions League goal. She is aiming to become only the third player to reach this milestone, after Ada Hegerberg (69) and Eugenie Le Sommer (50).
And though Harder did not score, she was a threat throughout, and she laid on two great chances late on for Edna Imade, who could have done better with her finishes.
As it was, Andree Jeglertz will at least be able to reflect on a spirited City comeback, and they rounded out with a fairly even stat sheet.

Bayern created chances worth 2.03 expected goals from 15 shots, while City had opportunities worth a combined 2.31 xG from just eight attempts. Room for improvement, but definitely a decent showing in attack.

Bayern were then in cruise control when they capitalised on a defensive mix-up from Man City, with Pernille Harder's cross causing havoc, and Kerstin Casparij was only able to turn it into her own net.

Yet, on the cusp of half-time, Beth Mead dragged City back into the contest as Casparij's cross found its way through to her, and she duly tucked home.

City looked all set to draw level around the hour mark, after Aoba Fujino was brought down by Ena Mahmutovic in Bayern's box.

Shaw, though, showed unusual profligacy as she saw her attempt saved by Mahmutovic, who atoned for her mistake.

Yet City did get their equaliser in the 86th minute, with Wamser whipping a fine effort in at the near post after she met Laura Blindkilde Brown's tee-up.

Man City show powers of recovery

City have made a fantastic start to their Women's Super League title defence, winning all three of their matches so far, but they endured a miserable opening half-an-hour of their European campaign. 

This was their first meeting against Bayern, or indeed any German team, in this competition, although City should probably have expected their hosts to make a fast start.

After all, Bayern had won seven of their previous 11 Champions League matches against English teams, including both legs of last season's quarter-final against Manchester United (3-2 A, 2-1 H).

Harder is just one off scoring her 50th Women's Champions League goal. She is aiming to become only the third player to reach this milestone, after Ada Hegerberg (69) and Eugenie Le Sommer (50).

And though Harder did not score, she was a threat throughout, and she laid on two great chances late on for Edna Imade, who could have done better with her finishes.

As it was, Andree Jeglertz will at least be able to reflect on a spirited City comeback, and they rounded out with a fairly even stat sheet.

Bayern created chances worth 2.03 expected goals from 15 shots, while City had opportunities worth a combined 2.31 xG from just eight attempts. Room for improvement, but definitely a decent showing in attack.

8r4cscg9vsoe11iz2zvr06c76.title: Tuchel: England have a plan for Spain
8r4cscg9vsoe11iz2zvr06c76.subtitle: England begin their Nations League campaign against world champions Spain, and Thomas Tuchel is determined to start with three points.
paragraphs: Thomas Tuchel revealed England "have a plan" to defeat Spain in their Nations League opener on Saturday.
The Three Lions host the world champions at Wembley Stadium in both of their first matches since the World Cup in the summer.

Spain lifted the trophy for the second time in their history after defeating Argentina 1-0 in the final, while England beat France 6-4 in the third-place play-off – their best finish at the tournament since 1966.
Luis de la Fuente's side are unbeaten in each of their last 38 matches in all competitions (W29 D9), the longest-ever such streak by a European nation.
Tuchel conceded England will have their work cut out against Spain and believes La Roja's possession-based style is a disadvantage for his side.
"I think it is an advantage in general. Not only against us, but against everyone," said Tuchel.
"This is how they play. I think they rely on that. This is how they train and they were brought up. This is clearly part of them.
"But at the moment, I think the more you analyse Spain and their last matches they played in, you have to admire the way in which they defend. They added this to their game.
"It is so difficult for every single team in the world to create chances against them. We have a plan, and we have ambition, and we want to prove the opposite.
"We want to be the exception to the rule, but at the moment they are a very complete team."

England have won just two of their last 13 games against the reigning World Cup holders, losing nine times (D2); those wins came at home to Spain in November 2011 (1-0) and away to Germany in March 2016 (3-2).
Spain have also won six of their last nine meetings with England across all competitions (D1 L2), most recently winning 2-1 in the final of the 2024 European Championship.
England winger Anthony Gordon previously stated the Three Lions must play to their own strengths, but captain Harry Kane believes they can mirror Spain's style if needed.

"I get what he's saying," Kane said about Gordon's comments. "It's culture for Spain, playing a certain style from five, six or seven years old until they're professionals. In England, it's not so much like that.
"It doesn't mean we can't play under pressure or keep the ball. We still have a lot of amazing technical players – but we have a lot of strengths that they don't have; physicality, pace and power.
"They way we press and win duels, a lot of Premier League style football in a way.
"I think at our best we combine both. We're not just a team that play like Spain, but we have a lot of strengths that we can showcase."

          What Did We Learn From Jürgen Klopp’s First Game Back in Management?
        
      
                          
                      Sep 25, 2026
          
                      David Segar / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
After over two years away from the dugout, Jürgen Klopp returned to the touchline on Thursday as Germany boss. How did it go, and were there signs that he can revive Die Nationalelf?
For a long time, Jürgen Klopp insisted he may never return to football management.

The 59-year-old left Liverpool in May 2024 after admitting he was “running out of energy” following nine years at Anfield. After a break from the game altogether, he returned with Red Bull as its head of global soccer, overseeing the running of their various teams around the world.
The managerial bug can be infectious, though, and following Germany’s disappointing 2026 World Cup and the departure of Julian Nagelsmann, Klopp was asked to come to the rescue.
On Thursday, he took charge of his first game since May 2024 as Germany travelled to face old rivals the Netherlands in their 2026-27 UEFA Nations League opener.

Expectations were high. Klopp leading the German national team always felt like it would happen eventually, and there is optimism the former Mainz and Borussia Dortmund boss can have the same revolutionary impact he had at all three clubs he’s managed.

As mentioned, Germany had a poor World Cup this summer. They started by thrashing Curaçao 7-1, though they needed a late winner to overcome Ivory Coast after that, before losing 2-1 to Ecuador in their final group game.
That was not ideal preparation for a tough last-32 clash with Paraguay, and so it proved. Germany struggled with their opponents’ physical approach and were ultimately eliminated on penalties.
Klopp signed a four-year deal to take over from Nagelsmann, overseeing the Euro 2028 and 2030 World Cup campaigns. His primary challenge is the Nations League, though, and it was a big test first up.

Not only was he taking on the Netherlands in Amsterdam, complete with their own new gaffer in Xavi Hernández – also managing his first game since May 2024 after leaving Barcelona – but he was set to face three of his former Liverpool players. Virgil van Dijk, Ryan Gravenberch and Cody Gakpo all started for the Dutch, and one of them went on to deny his old boss a debut victory.

Klopp took the unusual step of naming a 44-man squad, with Augsburg goalkeeper Finn Dahmen the only player set to be present for all four Nations League games in this international window. One group of players will be available for the first two (vs Netherlands and Greece) and then others will join up for the last two (vs Serbia and Greece).

The move was met with general approval in Germany, allowing Klopp to look at many players, introduce new and exciting faces, and also protect players from too much football across the elongated international break.

That doesn’t entirely eradicate the risk of injury, though, and that was apparent when Jamal Musiala pulled up in the warm-up in Amsterdam. On top of that, Kai Havertz could only play the first half hour after being on the receiving end of a nasty challenge by Quinten Timber, the brother of Havertz’s Arsenal teammate Jurriën.

An early scare came from one of Klopp’s former charges, with Van Dijk converting a Tijjani Reijnders corner, only for the goal to be ruled out after a VAR check judged Brian Brobbey to have fouled Marc-André ter Stegen.
There was some familiarity in the first XI Klopp named as Germany manager. Joshua Kimmich was handed his 115th cap, taking him past Toni Kroos (114) and into seventh place outright.

There was also a new face in the side, with Freiburg right-back Philipp Treu earning his first cap, and he played a key role in the first goal of the Klopp era. Treu’s low cross into the Dutch box from the right was blocked by the sliding Jan Paul van Hecke, but the loose ball fell kindly for Felix Nmecha, who finished calmly. It was somewhat appropriate that a Dortmund player scored the first goal under Klopp, given the outstanding success he had with BVB between 2008 and 2015.

It wasn’t without some controversy. Brobbey was down hurt on the turf at the time and Germany played on while Dutch players were imploring them to kick it out. Ultimately, it was at the referee’s discretion and despite some disagreements between Denzel Dumfries and Kimmich, Klopp’s side were well within their rights to play on, and it was 1-0.

It was familiar shape from Klopp’s side. Havertz was the striker but dropped deep – indeed, Nadiem Amiri had a more advanced average position in the first 30 minutes – while the two full-backs got forward with regularity. The wide forwards, Karim Adeyemi and Kevin Schade, were the two most-advanced German players in that first half hour before Havertz was forced off.

Another new face, Younes Ebnoutalib, replaced Havertz, and if anything, Germany looked even better with the Eintracht Frankfurt man up top. It wasn’t entirely polished but there was energy, there was effort, and there was counter pressing so synonymous with Klopp.
After the game, Treu told RTL: “We wanted to press them from the front, put them under pressure, be difficult to play against and play with intensity.
