          How Problematic is Manchester City’s Leaky Defence?
        
      
                          
                      Sep 23, 2026
          
                      Ali Tweedale / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
Manchester City are top of the Premier League with a perfect record of five wins from five, but they haven’t been entirely convincing at the back. Is there any cause for concern?

Enzo Maresca’s comments after watching his Manchester City side’s rollercoaster victory over Sunderland on Sunday afternoon sparked an interesting philosophical debate. Rather than lean towards the are-you-not-entertained ethos of an Ange Postecoglou, Maresca intimated he would like to see rather more control from his team, and a little less excitement than they provided in this win.

The Italian may well prefer to watch a game with lots of goals, but he was likely stating this preference on this particular occasion because the chaos of City’s win, in which they needed to retake the lead three times in the first half alone – something that has only happened six times in Premier League history to any team – was not exactly the mark of champions. As the scoreline suggests, City allowed their opponents far too many opportunities to score.

Sunderland are a very good team but not one that routinely creates a lot of chances. On this occasion, away to title hopefuls, they had chances worth 3.57 expected goals, which is by far their highest since their return to the Premier League last year.

In fact, in 43 games since the start of last season, they’ve only managed more than 2.0 xG twice, with their previous best being 2.44 vs Newcastle in March. They’ve had under 1.0 xG in more than half (22) of their matches.

But they carved City open time and again. Brian Brobbey scored a hat-trick of what were essentially tap-ins, allowed into areas where he could not miss, time and time again. And at 4-3, Sunderland came within a Rúben Dias goal-line clearance of equalising again.

While match-going fans got their money’s worth and neutrals were thoroughly entertained, even though City won and kept up the only remaining 100% record in the Premier League, it's understandable that Maresca came away a little dismayed at his side’s defensive display.
“It’s much better to win games,” he said. “In this moment, it’s better to have three points more than less, no doubt. We scored five. We could have scored probably more goals.
“So that means that we created enough, but at the same time we need to avoid conceding goals like today. We had four clean sheets in a row and today we conceded three goals.”

It is a fact that City had kept four successive clean sheets before the Sunderland game, but it was slightly disingenuous of Maresca to try and reframe their form that way. That run included the midweek win over Championship side Norwich in the EFL Cup and a 1-0 win at home to newly-promoted Coventry, who caused City all manner of problems and could quite feasibly have scored three goals, let alone one.

Credit where it’s due: City were mightily impressive defensively in their 1-0 win at Manchester United, keeping their rivals at arm’s length despite playing most of the derby with 10 men. But across that four-game run of clean sheets, they conceded chances worth 2.82 xG. So, in other words, they could reasonably have been expected to concede three goals.
They do have Gianluigi Donnarumma in goal, so perhaps they just felt confident that they could rely on one of the best shot-stoppers and most commanding goalkeepers of his generation.

But the evidence from the Sunderland game suggests that is not a reliable method of defence. Sunderland’s 3.57 xG is the third highest ever by a team that went on to lose a Premier League game since xG data is available (2013-14). On another day, Sunderland would have won that match, just like United will feel aggrieved not to have won the derby, and Coventry were left rueing missed chances against City.
On the opening weekend of the season, too, City required 84th- and 91st-minute goals to come from behind and rescue a win at home to Bournemouth.

In other words, their ‘perfect’ record of five wins from five has been rather less convincing than it might appear from a quick glance at the league table. They are clearly feeling the loss of Rodri from the base of their midfield.

They have, though, still won each game, which is something no other team can say. They are able to rely on the goalscoring of perennial golden-boot winner and early leader in the top-scorers’ stakes, Erling Haaland (five goals).

Rayan Cherki (three goals, two assists) and Antoine Semenyo (two goals, three assists) have started the season very well, too, while Enzo Fernández (one goal) provides further attacking threat from the double pivot. Iliman Ndiaye looks to have settled well following his summer move from Everton, and Phil Foden (two assists) is another exceptional attacker when he’s not kicking Bruno Fernandes in the you-know-wheres.

But is their arguably unrivalled attack enough? Can they rely on being bailed out often enough to win the title? “Attack wins you games, defence wins you titles,” as goes the famous Sir Alex Ferguson quote. If that’s true, then City might have something to worry about.

Indeed, only Brighton (who have played two halves of football against 10 men) have scored more goals (16) in the Premier League this season than City (13), but six teams have conceded fewer than them (5). Those teams are Leeds, Everton, Brentford, Hull and, perhaps crucially, likely title rivals Arsenal and Liverpool.

“There’s no way Manchester City win the league,” Sky Sports pundit Paul Merson said after the Sunderland game. “Going forward, [they] were good but at the back they were all over the place. [That] catches up with you.”

9cna4pd5zgf3zcjqd3ndy6j5.title: Semenyo confident he can be Man City's Haaland backup
9cna4pd5zgf3zcjqd3ndy6j5.subtitle: Having scored twice against Sunderland, Antoine Semenyo backed himself to play as a makeshift number nine for Manchester City if needed.
paragraphs: Antoine Semenyo is confident he has the attributes to deputise for Erling Haaland as Manchester City's striker if required, following his brace against Sunderland.
Semenyo netted either side of half-time as City claimed a thrilling 5-3 victory over the Black Cats on Sunday, maintaining their 100% Premier League record going into the international break.
The Ghanaian also laid on an assist for Rayan Cherki, scoring and assisting in the same Premier League game for the fourth time in his career, and the second as a City player.

Since joining from Bournemouth in January, the Ghana international has scored 13 goals in 34 appearances for City in all competitions – only Haaland (19 goals in 32 games) has outscored him in that span.

In that same time, Semenyo has overperformed his expected goals (xG) total of 7.74 by a greater margin than any other City player (+5.26), while his conversion rate of 20.6% is slightly better than Haaland's 20.4%.

With City not signing another recognised striker in the summer transfer window, some have suggested Semenyo may have to deputise as a number nine at some point this season, and he is up for the challenge.
"I've heard about his backup striker thing. I don't know where it's come from! But, yes, if I need to, then I'll do it. I've no problem with doing that," he said, as quoted by ESPN.
"I think that [finishing] just comes naturally. Once I'm in front of the goal, I know it doesn't move. So as long as I hit it in the corner with a good connection, I know it will go in."
Another City attacker who has enjoyed an outstanding start to the season is Cherki, who showed quick feet inside the Sunderland area to score City's second goal on Sunday.
The Frenchman's six goal involvements in all competitions this season (four goals, two assists) are the second-most of any City player, behind Haaland (seven goals).
"I'm very happy because it was the goal to make it 2-1. I needed to help my team-mates," Cherki told City's website. "I want to give them good passes.
"I need to score a lot of goals for my team. I love the fans. And I think the fans saw a big game, so I'm very happy about that."

City now have three weeks off before travelling to Anfield to face Liverpool in their next Premier League game on October 11, having started a top-flight season with five straight wins for only the fifth time (also 1912-13, 2015-16, 2016-17 and 2023-24).
"Everyone feels good," Semenyo said of the mood around Enzo Maresca's squad.
"It's where we want to be, but we're not going to get too complacent or too relaxed. We know there are a lot more games to go.

"We just want to continue winning; we just have to keep going. It's seven or eight weeks we've been together now, so it's not been too long, but we're doing well. We're winning our games, and we'll keep improving."

"I need to score a lot of goals for my team. I love the fans. And I think the fans saw a big game, so I'm very happy about that."

City now have three weeks off before travelling to Anfield to face Liverpool in their next Premier League game on October 11, having started a top-flight season with five straight wins for only the fifth time (also 1912-13, 2015-16, 2016-17 and 2023-24).

"Everyone feels good," Semenyo said of the mood around Enzo Maresca's squad. 

"It's where we want to be, but we're not going to get too complacent or too relaxed. We know there are a lot more games to go.

"We just want to continue winning; we just have to keep going. It's seven or eight weeks we've been together now, so it's not been too long, but we're doing well. We're winning our games, and we'll keep improving."

          Premier League 2026-27 Title Predictions: Updated Opta Supercomputer Projections After Five Matchdays
        
      
                          
                      Sep 21, 2026
          
                      Oliver Hopkins / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
We’re five matches into the 2026-27 Premier League season, meaning we now have more information than we did at the start of the campaign. So, how have the title predictions changed in the Opta supercomputer’s model?
It’s still very early days, but the nascent Premier League table is beginning to take shape as we head into the international break.

With five wins from five, Manchester City sit at the summit as the only team with a 100% winning record. Opta’s pre-season favourites, Arsenal, are second, three points behind, with Brighton and Brentford, who have both made hugely impressive starts, rounding out the top four.
But how have those early-season results affected the Opta supercomputer’s predictions for the title? Let’s find out.
As a reminder, Arsenal were the model’s pre-season favourites. The Opta supercomputer gave them a 40.6% chance of defending their 2025-26 title on the eve of the season.
Manchester City (19.6%) were comfortably second favourites, followed by Liverpool (9.2%) and Manchester United (6.6%).
Despite suffering a heavy defeat to Brighton at the weekend, Arsenal remain the Opta supercomputer’s favourites to lift the trophy, with a 43.7% chance of winning the title.

Manchester City (39.8%) are hot on their heels. Their perfect start, as well as Arsenal’s weekend defeat, means the title race is now definitely a two-horse contest in the supercomputer’s eyes, rather than the procession many thought it might be for Arsenal.
Together, Arsenal and Man City account for 83.4% of all the title equity in the supercomputer’s predictions.

Liverpool (5.7%) are the model’s third favourites. They are currently unbeaten under new manager Andoni Iraola, but have drawn three of their five games so far. As a result, their title hopes have fallen by 3.5 percentage points, from 9.2% before the season to 5.7% now.

Brighton, the architects of Arsenal’s downfall this weekend, have made a hugely impressive start. They are the division’s top scorers with 16 goals, boast the best goal difference at +11 and handed Arsenal their first defeat since 19 April, 155 days ago. They look like the real deal.
The Seagulls are now fourth in the Opta supercomputer’s title predictions, with a 4.2% chance of winning an improbable Premier League title.
From there, a multitude of teams are clustered around the 1% mark. Brentford have a 1.2% chance, Everton 1.1%, Chelsea 1.0%, and Manchester United are given a 0.9% chance.
Manchester City’s title chances have increased by 20.2 percentage points, more any other team across the first five matchdays.
As mentioned, City began the season as the supercomputer’s second favourites, but they have made a perfect start to life under Enzo Maresca.

Maresca is the sixth manager to win his first five Premier League games in charge of a club, after Carlo Ancelotti at Chelsea (six), Pep Guardiola at Manchester City (six), Craig Shakespeare at Leicester City (five), Maurizio Sarri at Chelsea (five) and Ole Gunnar Solskjær at Manchester United (six).

Arsenal’s title chances have also increased, rising 3.0 percentage points from their pre-season figure. That might seem surprising given their defeat to Brighton, but several of the teams that started the season among the favourites have already faltered.
Chelsea and Manchester United, for example, have both made poor starts, while Liverpool have dropped points in three of their first five games.
Brighton are the only other team to rise significantly. Their chances of winning the Premier League title have more than doubled (2.0% to 4.2%) following their excellent start.
It’s been a disappointing start to the campaign for Manchester United.

B24AF92EFF71C1370ECFF3F52A77B841.title: Preview: England host World Champions Spain at Wembley
B24AF92EFF71C1370ECFF3F52A77B841.subtitle: FotMob
paragraphs: NewsAboutTV schedulesPreview: England host World Champions Spain at WembleyShareEngland return to action for the first time since the World Cup with a Nations League match against opposition that couldn’t be more challenging.

Given the peculiarly timid manner in which they were eliminated from the World Cup against Argentina in July, there’s a case for saying that England’s first match of the 2026/27 season is more important than it might otherwise have been. The heat has turned up slightly under Thomas Tuchel as a result of the nature of that defeat, and he needs a decent performance in this match, if the pressure under him isn’t to build further.

Spain are their first opponents in Group A3 of the Nations League, and in theory the challenge couldn’t be much greater. Their head coach Luis de la Fuente certainly faces none of the pressures that could be set to build up behind the scenes for England. The visitors haven’t lost to anybody in two and a half years, while their last match saw them lift the World Cup trophy.

Given how strong Spain have been over much of the last two decades, England’s record against them isn’t completely terrible, though it’s been 15 years since they last beat them at Wembley and they’ve only won one of their last five meetings with them.

These two teams met in the first iteration of the Nations League in 2018, and away wins were the order of the day that time around, with Spain winning 2-1 at Wembley in September of that year and England winning 3-2 in Sevilla six weeks later.

Their last meeting came in the final of Euro 2024 in Berlin, when goals from Nico Williams and Mikel Oyarzabal handed Spain a 2-1 and the Henri Delaunay Trophy. In losing this match, England became the first team in the history of the European Championships to lose two consecutive finals.

One of the players who should know his opponents better than anyone else is midfielder Jude Bellingham, who is now up to almost 150 appearances for Real Madrid since his big money move to the Bernabéu from Borussia Dortmund in 2023. Bellingham saw his popularity soar during the World Cup, and he’ll be expected to take a leading role, if England are to find a way through Spain in this match.

One Spain player worth watching who may be back in their team for this match is Barcelona’s Fermín López. He missed the World Cup after fracturing his foot shortly before the start of the tournament, but he’s recovered and has worked his way back into a Barcelona team that is flying at the start of their domestic season. López has recently been subject to speculation that Manchester United could be preparing a £129 million move for him. The international break gives him a valuable opportunity to clear that background noise from his head for a couple of weeks.

There’s something almost traditional about a rash of withdrawals at the very start of an international break, and the Premier League hasn’t let us down this time. Declan Rice, Cole Palmer, Marcus Rashford, Kobbie Mainoo, and Tino Livramento have all been withdrawn from the England squad, while Morgan Gibbs-White and James Garner have both received late call-ups.

Spain have made changes from their World Cup squad for their opening Nations League matches, with Inter goalkeeper Josep Martínez, Real Madrid defender Dean Huijsen, and Espanyol striker Roberto Fernández joining the squad along with Fermín López. Fernández is of particular interest, having started his season with six goals in seven matches in LaLiga. Joan García (knee), Marcos Llorente (retired from international football), Gavi (precautionary), Pedro Porro (hamstring) and Borja Iglesias (fitness) have all been omitted from the squad.

The mood surrounding the England team following the World Cup finals has been a peculiar one. On the one hand, there’s nothing ‘disgraceful’ about losing a World Cup semi-final. But on the other, the team’s performances throughout the tournament were patchy at times, and losing to Argentina in such a supine manner calls into question whether they’ll be able to go further, take that final step, and actually win a major tournament. Co-hosting the next Euros means that expectations will be sky-high again in two years’ time, but the evidence that they have the capability to do this remains patchy.

Kicking off their 2026/27 matches against Spain is a huge challenge, but there’s a case for saying that these are the best circumstances to do so. La Roja proved what they needed to prove in the summer, and with this match being at the exact half-way point between being a friendly and a competitive match, their opponents are unlikely to be as fired up for this match as they might have been had they been meeting under just about any other circumstances.

Home advantage helps, though Spain are unbeaten on their last two trips to Wembley, and a desire to stay fit throughout the club season may lead to the players from both teams deciding that going full throttle in this match isn’t the wisest of ideas, especially considering that, with the other two teams in the group being Croatia and Czechia, there are no ‘easy’ games in this Nations League group. A 1-1 draw with no serious injuries on either team would leave everybody feeling that they’ve got through it relatively unscathed.

          Chelsea vs Arsenal Prediction: WSL Preview
        
      
                          
                      Sep 25, 2026
          
                      Chloe Horswill / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
While they are both unbeaten, Chelsea and Arsenal have not been at their best in 2026-27. Can either side apply pressure on Manchester City? We preview a heavyweight showdown at Stamford Bridge that could have major ramifications for the early WSL title race.
Heading into Matchday 4, only one team in the Women's Super League have a perfect record, with champions Manchester City setting the pace in 2026-27.

Chelsea were the pre-season favourites for the title, winning 40.8% of the Opta supercomputer's simulations, with Arsenal also expected to be challengers. But neither have matched their rivals' fast start.
There is still a very long way to go in the title race and both teams are unbeaten, but Sunday's clash at Stamford Bridge already feels pivotal for Chelsea and Arsenal.

Chelsea come into this match after a narrow 1-0 win over Austria Wien in the Women's Champions League on Wednesday, while Arsenal prevailed by the same scoreline against Køge on Tuesday, needing a 93rd-minute Mariona Caldentey penalty to secure the three points.
So, can either of them kick into gear in the WSL this weekend?
After a disappointing 1-1 draw with Aston Villa, Chelsea have strung together two wins, hammering Manchester United 5-0 before beating Birmingham City 2-0.
While they looked comfortable against Eva Olid's struggling United, there was plenty to be desired against Birmingham, namely their finishing.
They accumulated 3.9 expected goals (xG) from 22 shots, with eight of those on target and one hitting the woodwork. They also recorded five Opta-defined ‘big chances' but could only score twice.
Melvine Malard came off the bench to net on her WSL debut for the club in the second half, settling the nerves after they failed to get the goals their early dominance deserved.
But while there may be question marks over their chance conversion, they have started the season well defensively, conceding just one goal and keeping two clean sheets.
No team have faced fewer shots (14), while the Blues have also limited their opponents to just 1.3 expected goals against (xGA).

With a record like that, if they score the first goal, Arsenal could be in trouble; Chelsea are unbeaten in their last 45 WSL matches when leading at any stage (W38 D7), the longest run in the competition's history.
Arsenal, meanwhile, were expected to pick up where they left off at the end of last season, but it has been a stuttering start to their title charge.
They edged a 1-0 win over Brighton on the opening weekend, before drawing with Crystal Palace and Man Utd.

At this point, they are hoping to avoid matching an unwanted record: the Gunners could win as few as five points from their first four matches for the second time in the last three seasons after 2024-25, when the fourth game was a defeat to Chelsea (W1 D2).
In the WSL, they have netted just two goals – only promoted duo Palace and Charlton Athletic have scored fewer (both one) – and have massively underperformed their 5.9 xG.
The Gunners' shot conversion rate of 3.3% this term is also the worst seen in the WSL since bottom-of-the-league Yeovil Town in 2017-18 (2.2%).
They rank fourth for shots (60), with 10 of those classed as ‘big' chances, and have had 22 attempts on target.
It was a familiar story against Koge as they racked up 19 attempts worth 1.9 xG – a figure inflated by their late penalty – but only two of those shots were on target.

B8593B52ED98D7F173134AB0C95DE0AF.title: How will Zinedine Zidane change France’s playing style after years of Deschamps-ball?
B8593B52ED98D7F173134AB0C95DE0AF.subtitle: FotMob
paragraphs: NewsAboutTV schedulesHow will Zinedine Zidane change France’s playing style after years of Deschamps-ball? ShareZinedine Zidane will take charge of his first matches as France’s new manager in the extended September and October international break.

Zinedine Zidane just had to bide his time. The three-times Champions League-winning manager could have taken any other job after leaving Real Madrid (for a second time) in 2021. He surely had offers. Zidane, however, remained patient as France’s next national team manager in waiting.

That patience paid off when the 54-year-old was officially named Les Bleus boss after the World Cup, confirming the worst kept secret in international football. Zidane was long seen as the natural heir to Didier Deschamps and now the former midfielder will get his chance to reshape the French national team in his own image.

What that image is, though, is unclear. While Zidane enjoyed incredible success as a manager over two spells at Real Madrid, winning three Champions League titles and two LaLiga titles, as well as two European Super Cups and two Club World Cups for good measure, he never had much of an identifiable playing style.

Zidane was the ultimate man-manager during his two managerial stints at the Santiago Bernabéu. The former Ballon d’Or winner instantly commanded the respect of Real Madrid’s superstars in a way some of his successors in the job were never able to do. Zidane managed by aura, and it worked.

At no point, however, did Zidane have an overarching tactical philosophy. Under his stewardship, Real Madrid played in quick transition. They were never able to control games through possession. Most of the time, they didn’t need to, but Zidane’s Real Madrid certainly weren’t revered for their tactical structure.

In many ways, Zidane’s Real Madrid played a similar brand of football to the style professed by Deschamps over 14 years as France boss. This should make the handover of managerial power a smooth one. There is a lot of stylistic overlap between Zidane’s game and Deschamps-ball.

The problem for Zidane, though, is that after nearly a decade-and-a-half of stodgy, conservative football under Deschamps, many French fans are ready for something different. They broadly want a more modern style of play and Zidane, for all his glittering success as a player and manager, might not be the man to deliver this.

Zidane has picked five new faces in his first France squad for the UEFA Nations League matches against Türkiye, Belgium and Italy. Liverpool centre back Jérémy Jacquet is expected to feature while Rennes striker Esteban Lepaul, Como midfielder Lucas Da Cunha, Inter Milan’s Andy Diouf and Toulouse goalkeeper Guillaume Restes have all been included.

France’s squad is one of the most talented in the international arena right now. Their forward line is terrifying with Les Bleus capable of out-scoring any opponent. Zidane’s lack of tactical principles might not matter due to the level of attacking talent of his new team just as it didn’t matter much for Deschamps.

In Kylian Mbappé, Zidane has inherited one of the best players in the world. The Real Madrid forward hasn’t always been the easiest to coach as an individual and doesn’t offer much on the defensive side of the ball, but France has always seen the best version of Mbappé. He is at his most influential in the blue of his national team.

“For French people, he means a great deal – he’s a legend, he’s the nation’s ‘Zizou', he represents elegance, greatness,” said Mbappé when asked for his opinion on Zidane’s appointment. “⁠He ​made his mark on the history of the national team as a ​player and he had some truly iconic moments. He’s perhaps the player who most embodies the France team. He’s one of those players who ​transcended generations. He left an indelible mark on the history of French football.”

As the most iconic member of the France team that won the World Cup on home soil in 1998, Zidane’s legacy as a national hero is already secure. In a sense, he has nothing to lose by taking over as Les Bleus boss. Zidane has more credit in the bank than any new France manager in history.

Zidane is an anomaly in the modern game. At a time when every manager at the elite level seemingly has a philosophy and consistent values that underpin their view of the game, the Frenchman’s approach is vibes-based. That could work for him as an international manager even better than it did for him in the club game.

France under Deschamps were successful, but not always entertaining. Some fans believed Deschamps restricted Les Bleus as an attacking outfit when Mbappé and co should have been unleashed. Zidane might decide to do that. He might not. Nobody really knows what to expect from the great enigma of modern management now that he’s finally taken on a new challenge.

          The Florian Wirtz Debate: Were Jamie Carragher’s Criticisms Harsh or Fair?
        
      
                          
                      Sep 22, 2026
          
                      David Segar / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
Florian Wirtz has not had the impact many expected at Liverpool, and the criticism is getting louder. Has the Germany international really been that bad, though?
When Florian Wirtz signed for Liverpool in the summer of 2025, there was only one logical assumption.

The Premier League champions at the time had recruited one of the hottest young talents in world football, one who played a pivotal role in winning a historic double with Bayer Leverkusen in 2023-24, and was already a star of the German national team at just 22 years old.
An exciting and productive attacking midfielder being added to the best team in England? How could this not work?
Football has a habit of flipping the script, though, making the impossible possible, and ensuring that something that seems so obviously right is somehow wrong.

The 2025-26 season was difficult for several reasons at Anfield, and Wirtz, along with other new arrivals, struggled to make as much of an impact as expected for the fee agreed (£100 million + £16m in add-ons).

There were conversations among fans this summer as to how long he and fellow nine-figure signing Alexander Isak should be given before difficult questions needed be asked. The broad consensus was ‘until Christmas’.
As it turned out, the real answer was ‘after the opening game of the season’ as Wirtz and Isak laboured in Liverpool's 2-2 draw at Newcastle United and loud doubts began to surface.
Jamie Carragher spoke on the first Monday Night Football of the season about Wirtz’s signing in 2025 potentially being part of the “worst transfer window in Premier League history”.

The former Liverpool defender was criticising a few players that time – and Isak has since gone on to score four times in his last four Premier League appearances to somewhat silence his doubters – but Carragher did focus his ire solely on Wirtz on Sunday in the first episode of his new podcast for Sky Sports.

🗣️ "I don't think Florian Wirtz is in poor form, what we're seeing is what he is"Jamie Carragher says he is worried for Florian Wirtz and doesn't see how he will hurt teams ⤵️ pic.twitter.com/umgZ0ZgfzK

“The reason I worry is, I don’t think Wirtz is in poor form since he came to Liverpool. I actually think what we’re seeing is what he is,” he said. “The worry for Wirtz now is that his performances so far, or what he’s given Liverpool, is so low. Where we were expecting him was to take Liverpool to another league title, to take Liverpool to a Champions League.

“The gap he’s got to [close] to justify what people were expecting, I almost think is too big. You can’t get there. Even if he improves a bit and gets there, it’s still not what Liverpool thought they were getting.
“I think [Andoni] Iraola’s got a decision to make here. Wirtz would not be in my Liverpool team.”

Carragher particularly derided Wirtz – who has just one assist in six games this season – for his performance in Sunday’s 1-0 win at Bournemouth, labelling it “one of the poorest I've ever seen him in a Liverpool shirt.”
Reds boss Andoni Iraola was a little more generous in his review of Wirtz’s outing, though did accept when speaking to reporters that the German had struggled in the first half.
“He started the game slowly, I agree,” Iraola said. “After that first phase, I think we improved. Florian has helped us also to improve.
“Second half he was playing much better, he was finding better spots to receive and turn… I’m much more happy with his second half.”

On paper, Wirtz’s numbers from the game weren’t that bad. He created three chances, the joint-most of any Liverpool player along with Cody Gakpo, won six of his eight duels, and won possession four times: only Alexis Mac Allister (7), Ronald Araujo (6), and Jérémy Jacquet (6) did so more often for the visitors.
Perhaps we shouldn’t be saying this, being Opta and all, but data doesn’t always tell the whole story.

          Man Utd 4th, Spurs 12th, Newcastle 20th? Premier League Expected Points Table After Matchday 5
        
      
                          
                      Sep 22, 2026
          
                      Oliver Hopkins / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
We’re five games into the 2026-27 Premier League season. That gives us some data to work with, but it’s still a small enough sample for luck and variance to have played a significant role in the results. So, which teams have been fortunate, and which might feel hard done by?
Is the early-season Premier League table lying to us?

With five wins from five, Manchester City sit top as the only team with a 100% winning record. Opta’s pre-season favourites, Arsenal, are second, three points behind. Brighton and Brentford, who have both made hugely impressive starts, round out the top four.
Tottenham prop up the table, sitting bottom of the league with just two points. Fulham and Coventry City join them in the relegation zone.

In many ways, absolutely. The table is a perfect reflection of how matches have gone so far this season. The aim of the game is to win football matches, and there is no more hard-hitting proof of success than the league table.
In other ways, though, it might be slightly skewed. Some teams might feel they have performed better than their results suggest. For others, the opposite might be true.
This is where Opta’s expected points model can add a little more nuance.

The expected points model simulates the number of goals scored by each side in each match based on the expected goals (xG) value of every shot taken. It then uses those simulated goal totals to determine the outcome of the match, whether that is a win, draw or defeat. Each match is simulated 10,000 times.
The expected points for each team can then be calculated based on the proportion of simulations they win, draw or lose.

We’re aware this is not an exact science. Expected goals data doesn’t account for every factor at play during a football match, including game state and dangerous periods of possession that don’t result in shots. We’re also very much aware that real points matter infinitely more than expected ones.
Nevertheless, the expected points table can give us some interesting additional context on what we have seen across the opening five matchdays.
The first major talking point is that Arsenal sit top of the expected points table.

They remain favourites to win the title according to the Opta supercomputer, and their underlying numbers are still strong. They have the highest expected goals difference (+4.44) of any side in the Premier League.

Man City are second according to the expected points model. They have made a hugely impressive start under new manager Enzo Maresca, but the model suggests they have collected 5.8 more points than the underlying data from the chances they have created and conceded would normally warrant.

Sunderland generated 3.57 expected goals against them on MD5, the third-highest figure ever recorded (since 2013-14) by a losing team in a Premier League game, while the chances in City’s game against Manchester United (won 1-0) were essentially even.

There is important context to add here, though. City have spent a greater proportion of their game time leading (52.5%) than any other Premier League side this season. That means they have had less need to chase matches and push numbers forward, which could naturally reduce their overall xG output.

That’s something we need to bear in mind when analysing the expected points table, and one of the model’s limitations. A team protecting a lead doesn’t necessarily need to generate chances at the same rate as one searching for a goal.
So, which teams might feel they should be higher up the league?

Michael Carrick has come in for plenty of criticism following Manchester United’s poor start to the season. United have taken just five points from their opening five league games, their joint-fewest at this stage of a Premier League campaign alongside 2014-15.

Their underlying numbers, however, are far more encouraging. United lead the Premier League for total shots (113) and touches in the opposition box (182). Their total xG of 9.89 is the fourth-highest in the division.

          How Long Has Your Premier League Team Been Leading, Level or Losing in 2026-27?
        
      
                          
                      Sep 22, 2026
          
                      Matt Furniss / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
Which teams have held a winning position the longest in the Premier League this season, and which have spent the most time trailing? We look at every team’s time in each game state after five matchdays of 2026-27.
Manchester City have started the 2026-27 campaign with five wins from five and are the only team with a 100% record in the competition.

Therefore, it’s hardly a shock to see Enzo Maresca’s side lead the rankings for proportion of game time spent in a winning position.City are the only side to have been winning for over half (52%) of match minutes this season, but their opening game of the campaign at home to Bournemouth was a different story.
Trailing after a 27th-minute goal from Marcus Tavernier, City worked their way back into the game with an 84th-minute Marc Guéhi strike, before Josko Gvardiol won the game in added time.

That match saw them hold the lead for only four minutes and 52 seconds. The 60 minutes and 52 seconds that they were behind is the longest by any team that’s gone on and won a match in the Premier League this season.

City led the Premier League ranking for proportion of game time spent in a winning position across last season too (48.6%), but that was irrelevant in the end. Arsenal, who spent 44.5% of match time winning, ended up with the league title, finishing seven points clear of their rivals.

Bournemouth are yet to win a match in the Premier League this season but they have only been in a losing position for 9.3% of game time – the third lowest proportion. They have, however, lost a league-high nine points from winning positions, which might explain their winless run under new boss Marco Rose.

In three games so far, the Cherries have held a lead for more than 50 minutes before eventually failing to pick up all three points: Man City on MD1 (60:52), Everton on MD2 (52:29) and Newcastle on MD3 (82:11).
Arguably the most eye-catching number after five matchdays of this season is Brentford’s time spent in a losing position.
Keith Andrews’ side have been losing for just three minutes and 10 seconds of match action this season – that coming in the 2-2 away draw with Bournemouth on 12 September.
That means that they have been losing for just 0.6% of Premier League game time this season (rounded up to 1% in the viz above), which is substantially lower than the next lowest: Leeds on 8.6%.
At the other end of the spectrum, it’s been a miserable start to the season for Tottenham, who sit bottom of the Premier League table as we reach the extended international break.

Roberto De Zerbi’s team failed to score in their first four league games of 2026-27, and when they did finally find the net in the MD5 defeat to Aston Villa through Conor Gallagher in the 86th minute, they were already 3-0 down. That means that they haven’t led for a single second of Premier League action this season – the only team yet to do so.

Sunderland have only been in a winning position for 3.9% of their match time this season. That all came in the final 19 minutes and 24 seconds of their game against Fulham on MD2 after Wilson Isidor’s strike decided a tight game at the Stadium of Light.

          Spain Built the Youth Development Pathway England Still Crave
        
      
                          
                      Sep 25, 2026
          
                      Ryan Benson / Author, Jakob Abrahamson / Design, Peter McKeever / Data Viz
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
Spain have won successive major international men's tournaments. The pathways from academy football to senior teams at La Liga clubs has undoubtedly helped.
Drastic, nationwide reviews of football development in specific countries are ordinarily associated with prolonged fallow periods or short spells of extreme underperformance.
Two relatively recent high-profile examples would be Germany and England.

For Germany, a disappointing quarter-final exit to Croatia at the 1998 World Cup proved a pivotal moment for a re-think and increased investment behind the scenes in youth football. So, when there was outrage and calls for root-and-branch investigations in the wake of the national team failing to get out of their group at Euro 2000, strides had actually already been made. Germany went on to finish as runners-up at the 2002 World Cup, third at both the 2006 and 2010 World Cups, before winning it in 2014.

England, meanwhile, failed to even qualify for Euro 2008, and that was followed by an exit to Germany in the last 16 of a thoroughly underwhelming 2010 World Cup campaign. About six months after the latter, the FA unveiled its Youth Development Review, which provided 25 recommendations intended to improve the standard of football at every level, but especially in the grassroots game.

This review is broadly accepted as being a major catalyst for England's significantly improved results at major men's international tournaments in recent times, with the Three Lions reaching as many semi-finals (4) across the World Cup and European Championship since 2018 as they had in their entire history before Russia 2018.
How does any of this relate to Spain, then?
Well, if you're looking for similarities with respect to underperformance, it doesn't really relate at all, and that's the point.

Over several years, Spain did their own review of youth development and is currently in the second phase of a 10-to-12-year La Liga-led National Plan for the Optimisation and Improvement of Youth Academies, essentially a strategy to professionalise them. But as Juan Florit, La Liga's head of football projects, explains, academy reform in Spain was different to the prior examples because it was not triggered by a crisis.

“Traditionally, when a country, an organisation such as La Liga or a football association begins such a project, you start it from a position of weakness, from a problem or from a negative situation,” he says when asked by Opta Analyst about the initiative's grounding. “But if we think that with this it will be enough for the first decade, sooner or later we will be behind other countries [again].”
In 2016, clubs from the top two divisions began hosting annual Youth Academy Meetings with the intention of sharing knowledge, methodology and tools, hoping to improve competitiveness.

Granted, at this point Spain had recently underwhelmed at Euro 2016, having also failed to impress at the 2014 World Cup. But still, this was only four years on from winning Euro 2012, their third successive triumph at a major international tournament. Spanish football was hardly in crisis.
The Youth Academy Meetings ultimately led to the 2022 creation of the aforementioned ‘National Plan', which set out to take “grassroots football to a new level”.

It comprised five key principles: infrastructure, resources and technology; comprehensive player care; development and transition to professional football; training model and transition to competition; and structure and professional development.

This wasn't a reaction to any extreme underperformance either. The senior side had got to the semis of the delayed Euro 2020 a year earlier and the final of the 2021 Nations League. And at youth level, their Under-19s and Under-17s had each reached at least the last four of their most recent respective Euros in 2019 (youth tournaments in 2020 and 2021 were cancelled due to the COVID-19 pandemic).

While the phrase “if it isn't broken, don't fix it” does spring to mind, Spanish clubs and authorities spotted an opportunity to help themselves. If all academies were more professionally run, every club could potentially stand to benefit. At the very least, the steady stream of domestic players coming through and supplying the national team would be maintained.
“We thought that we needed to do something,” says Florit. “Other countries like Germany, Austria and Sweden were starting good projects with a solid base and a long-term vision.
“[Before] there was no real collective plan, collective vision, or collective strategy to work within the academy system and to strengthen the development of young talents [across Spain].”

And while that may have been the case, the domestic contingent in La Liga was already very strong and remains as such, perhaps to a degree most won't be fully aware of. This is their position of strength.

For the 10 seasons prior to 2026-27, the average number of Spanish players to play more than 450 minutes (so, the equivalent of five full matches) in a campaign is 236.6, a figure that dwarfs the rest of the big five leagues. The next closest is Italians in Serie A (152.2), followed by French players in Ligue 1 (149.9), Germans in the Bundesliga (142.6) and then English players in the Premier League (117.7).

          WSL Matchday 3: The Opta Numbers That Defined the Weekend
        
      
                          
                      Sep 21, 2026
          
                      Louise Bawden / Author, Gareth Boyes / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
Manchester City maintained their perfect start to the season, while Arsenal dropped points at home for the second successive match. We use Opta data to uncover the standout performances, emerging trends and biggest numbers from Matchday 3 of the 2026-27 WSL season.
There was no shortage of entertainment across the third matchday of the Women’s Super League, with goals flying in around the league, though Arsenal’s struggles continued in front of goal.

Manchester City maintained their perfect start in a six-goal thriller against Liverpool, Tottenham ran riot with seven against Crystal Palace, while London City Lionesses bounced back from defeat, firing in four goals at Charlton.

Elsewhere, Chelsea made it back-to-back wins, Everton edged past West Ham, and Brighton and Aston Villa shared the points. At the Emirates, Arsenal were frustrated at home once again as Manchester United responded from their difficult start to the season to earn a 1-1 draw.
But, as ever, the scorelines only tell part of the story.
We’ve dug into the Opta data to uncover the standout individual performances and numbers that defined Matchday 3.
We’re three games into the new WSL season and Man City are the only side still with a perfect record. But Liverpool made them work for it.
City took the lead before falling 2-1 behind, only to turn the game around and eventually claim a 4-2 victory.
It was just the second time in their WSL history that City have scored first, subsequently trailed and still gone on to win, after their 3-2 victory over Reading in the 2017 Spring Series.
Khadija Shaw continued her flying start to the campaign, becoming the first player to score in each of Manchester City’s opening three matches of a WSL season.
And Liverpool remain one of her favourite opponents.

Alongside Shaw, Lauren Hemp continues to underline her status as one of the WSL’s most devastating attacking talents – and the 26-year-old reached another significant landmark after hitting 100 goal involvements last weekend.
Only Bethany England (69), Vivianne Miedema (67), Beth Mead (60), Nikita Parris (58), Shaw (55) and Fran Kirby (54) have scored in more, while Hemp is now level with Sam Kerr.
And home continues to be a particularly happy place.
Liverpool may have left Manchester empty-handed, but there was another hugely encouraging performance from summer signing Vivien Endemann.

The Germany international is making quite the impression in her first season in England. Three appearances into her WSL career and Gareth Taylor looks like he may have uncovered a real gem for this reshaped Liverpool side.

The Reds pushed City harder than anyone has so far this season, but the league leaders still found a way to win. They have won three from three, scoring 12 goals in the process. Their perfect start rolls on.
Arsenal may have extended their unbeaten run to record-breaking territory against Manchester United, but for the second successive home game, it took late drama just to rescue a point.
After being held to a goalless draw by Crystal Palace on Matchday 2, the Gunners looked set for a first league defeat of the season before finding an equaliser deep into stoppage time.
Nonetheless, that late intervention preserved an impressive record.

The previous record holder, Köln legend Dieter Müller, took 129 Bundesliga games to score 100 goals – hitting that milestone in 1977. Harry Kane has managed the feat in just 98 appearances; he could have gone until April without registering a league goal and he’d still have broken the record.
It’s been a history-making September for the England captain, whose winner against Elversberg took him to 150 goals in all competitions for Bayern – in only 153 appearances.

The 33-year-old has picked up where he left off last season, when he enjoyed a career-best 61-goal campaign, finishing as Bundesliga top scorer for the third time in as many years since joining Bayern from Tottenham.

We already knew Kane was one of the best strikers in the world, if not the best – but what we’re seeing now is that he might actually still be getting better, an astonishing possibility for a player who, based on your typical centre-forwards, should be some years past his peak (of course, Kane isn’t your typical centre-forward).

Speaking after his latest landmark achievement, Kane – who amassed 213 goals in 317 Premier League outings for Spurs, placing him behind only Alan Shearer in the competition’s all-time scoring charts – said: “I’m very proud, to be honest, to reach 100 goals in the Bundesliga. Obviously, I’ve done it in the Premier League, so now to have it in a different league is something I’m really proud of. All I can say is a big thanks to the team.”
Kane’s 101 Bundesliga goals have come at a truly prolific average of 1.03 per game. He’s already averaging 0.75 goals per game in the league this season and 0.85 in all competitions.

And none of this should come as any kind of surprise: his overall goals-per-game average for Bayern is 0.98. Were he to score a hat-trick in his side’s first match after the international break, away to local rivals Augsburg, he would pull himself to exactly a goal a game.

It’s little wonder Kane, who has found the net 44 times for club and country this calendar year, is considered one of the frontrunners to win the Ballon d’Or – an individual accolade he’s yet to claim in a career full of them. Oh, and he’s done it at exactly a goal a game.
More goalscoring milestones feel like an inevitability for Kane, who has reportedly been in talks over extending his stay at Bayern, where his current deal expires next summer.

He’s one of 56 players with 100 or more Bundesliga goals to their name – but one of only eight non-Germans. Barring a lengthy injury lay-off or unfathomable loss of form, he’ll almost certainly pass 106-goal Ailton (Brazil) and Stéphane Chapuisat (Switzerland) this term in the ranking of leading foreign Bundesliga scorers – and probably 127-goal Vedad Ibišević (Bosnia and Herzegovina) as well.

Kane can also keep working his way up Bayern’s list of top Bundesliga goalscorers – on which he currently ranks sixth. Next in his sights is Dieter Hoeneß (102 goals), followed by fellow 1980s star Roland Wohlfarth (119).

Another couple of par scoring seasons by his standards and Kane will catch two more Bayern icons: Thomas Müller (150 goals) and two-time Ballon d’Or winner Karl-Heinz Rummenigge (162). Only the top two goalscorers in Bundesliga history are – unless he keeps playing for Bayern and producing these levels into his 40s – out of his reach: Robert Lewandowski (312) and perhaps the greatest No. 9 of all time, Gerd Müller (365).

It’s also not out of the question that Kane will become Bayern’s second-highest Champions League scorer ever. He currently sits second with 34 goals, nine ahead of Arjen Robben and 23 behind Thomas Müller – and with his goals-per-game average for the club in that competition an expectedly high 0.87 as things stand, he could well surpass Müller by the end of next season if Bayern go even reasonably deep into the knockout stage.
And if contract talks progress as both parties will hope, Kane is bound to keep tearing up the division for a number of years yet.

The previous record holder, Köln legend Dieter Müller, took 129 Bundesliga games to score 100 goals – hitting that milestone in 1977. Harry Kane has managed the feat in just 98 appearances; he could have gone until April without registering a league goal and he’d still have broken the record.
It’s been a history-making September for the England captain, whose winner against Elversberg took him to 150 goals in all competitions for Bayern – in only 153 appearances.

          England vs Spain Prediction: UEFA Nations League Preview
        
      
                          
                      Sep 24, 2026
          
                      Harry Carr / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
Saturday's UEFA Nations League action is headlined by a huge clash at Wembley. We look ahead to the game with our England vs Spain prediction and preview.
Before a stirring semi-final fightback from Argentina, arguably aided by some suspect substitutions from Thomas Tuchel, England were on course to meet Spain in the 2026 FIFA World Cup final.

Instead, following late goals from Enzo Fernández and Lautaro Martínez, the Three Lions had to contest the third-place play-off with France, edging a frantic encounter 6-4, before watching Spain's 1-0 victory over Argentina in the showpiece match from afar.

Having received stern criticism in the wake of that semi-final collapse, Tuchel needs to rebuild some trust with England's fans, and he has a blockbuster fixture to prepare for as Spain visit Wembley Stadium in the UEFA Nations League on Saturday.

England are back in the top tier of the competition after suffering a humiliating relegation to League B in 2022-23, having to fight their way out of the second level in 2024-25. They did so with five wins from six games under interim boss Lee Carsley (L1), with their current three-match winning streak being their longest ever in the competition.

It is important to remember that Tuchel has the best win rate of any England manager to ever lead the team for at least 10 matches, at 77% (P22 W17 D2 L3), while the Three Lions have only averaged more goals per game under Walter Winterbottom (2.8) than Tuchel (2.3).
England have also won 10 of their last 11 competitive home matches (L1), including each of their most recent five without conceding.

Only once in their history have England's men previously won six consecutive competitive home games to nil, under Roy Hodgson and Gareth Southgate between March 2015 and March 2017. That run also spanned Sam Allardyce's short-lived tenure, but he, of course, never got to lead the team out on home soil.

Tuchel has had to contend with a series of withdrawals ahead of this extended, four-game international break, with Tino Livramento, Kobbie Mainoo, Cole Palmer, Marcus Rashford and Declan Rice all pulling out of England's squad.
Everton's James Garner and Nottingham Forest's Morgan Gibbs-White, neither of whom made the World Cup squad, have been called up as replacements.

Tuchel was criticised for leaving several creative players at home this summer, so Gibbs-White – whose 13 Premier League goals this calendar year are the joint-most alongside Erling Haaland – will hope to seize his opportunity.

But heavy rotation looks unlikely for Saturday's game, at least, which should provide a useful yardstick for the World Cup bronze medallists. Jude Bellingham has scored seven goals in 10 appearances for England in 2026, with David Platt being the last midfielder to net more for them in a calendar year back in 1993 (eight).

He will reprise his partnership with Harry Kane, who is widely seen as a front-runner for the Ballon d'Or. And with one of Kane's main rivals for the award – Barcelona superstar Lamine Yamal – lining up on the other side, that is another storyline to keep an eye on.
Aided by Yamal's brilliance, Spain also reached the final of the 2024-25 Nations League, eventually going down to Portugal on penalties following a 2-2 draw in the final.
Spain's last five Nations League matches have seen them both score 2+ goals and concede 2+ goals, which is the longest run by any nation – in any tier – since the tournament's inception in 2018.

La Roja have reached three of the last four Nations League finals, also losing to France in 2020-21 and beating Croatia on penalties in 2022-23. Excluding spot-kicks, they have lost just one of their last 18 matches in the competition (W10 D7).

And during the last edition of the Nations League, only Cristiano Ronaldo (eight goals) outscored Mikel Oyarzabal (four). The Real Sociedad forward has 26 goal involvements across his last 25 international appearances (19 goals, 7 assists), a run that started with him scoring the winner against England in the Euro 2024 final.

Spain enter the game defending a 38-match unbeaten run in all competitions, winning 29 games and drawing nine in that time. It is the longest ever streak by a European nation, dating back to a 1-0 defeat to Colombia in March 2024, which did take place on English soil, at West Ham United's London Stadium.

Spain's last competitive defeat, which came all the way back in March 2023, also occurred in Britain, as they lost 2-0 to Scotland in a qualifier for Euro 2024. Might that be a positive omen for England?
Spain have won six of their last nine meetings with England across all competitions (D1 L2), most recently winning 2-1 in the Euro 2024 final in Berlin.

          WSL Match Predictions
        
      
                          
                      Sep 24, 2026
          
                      Chloe Horswill / Author, Jordan Collins / Design
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
With the help of the Opta supercomputer, we provide our WSL match predictions for Matchday 4 of the 2026-27 season.

With three matchdays down in the Women's Super League season, defending champions Manchester City remain the only team with a 100% record, following their frantic 4-2 victory over Liverpool last time out.

After drawing 2-2 with Bayern Munich in their Champions League opener on Tuesday, City visit Charlton Athletic – who are the only team yet to pick up a point – to kickstart the week’s action on Saturday, before focus turns to their potential title rivals.
Neither Chelsea nor Arsenal have suffered a defeat yet this campaign, but with both already off City's pace, their head-to-head clash at Stamford Bridge on Sunday looks vital.
There is also a Merseyside derby between Liverpool and Everton, while Manchester United will look to finally earn their first league victory under Eva Olid at home to West Ham.
Who will come out on top in the WSL this weekend? We have a look at the Opta supercomputer’s  Matchday 4 predictions.

With Man City boasting a perfect record and Charlton recording three straight defeats since their promotion, it should come as little surprise that our predictive model makes Andree Jeglertz's champions the clearest MD4 favourites, with a 75.6% win probability to Charlton's 10.6%.
Only once in the last eight campaigns have City enjoyed a longer winning start than this one, winning each of their first four matches in 2019-20.
But they will be supremely confident of matching that feat at The Valley, in what will be their first competitive meeting with Charlton in the WSL era.
Promoted sides have won just one of their last 28 meetings with the reigning champions in the competition (D3 L24), with Liverpool recording a 2-1 home win over Chelsea in September 2022.

Last time out, Khadija Shaw became the first player to score in each of City's first three games of a WSL campaign, and she could become the fifth player to do so in the first four matches of a season for any club.
London City Lionesses were 4-1 winners at Charlton last Saturday and currently sit fourth in the table with six points on the board ahead facing a winless Brighton.
Alexia Putellas and company are assigned a 52.9% win probability on Saturday, with Brighton only winning 23.0% of the supercomputer's pre-match simulations.

London City's three wins in their last four WSL matches (L1) are more than they managed across their previous 12 in the competition (W2 D3 L7), and their nine ‘big’ chances against Charlton last week were the most by any team in a WSL game since October 2020 (when Man Utd had 10 versus Brighton).

The Seagulls could fail to win their opening four matches of a WSL campaign for the third time after 2018-19 (first six) and 2019-20 (first five), and they have lost seven of their last nine league games in London.

Olid got her first win on the board with Manchester United in the Women’s League Cup on Wednesday, with a 10-1 thrashing of Sheffield United, and they will now look to translate that into a WSL victory.
The Red Devils are given a 68.0% chance of beating West Ham – whose own chances sit at 14.3% – having gone unbeaten in their last 12 league games against the Hammers (W8 D4).

Man Utd are winless in their first three WSL matches (D1 L2) for the first time and lost two of their last three home games in the competitions (D1), as many defeats as across their previous 20 (W12 D6).
West Ham struggle on their travels against the Red Devils, having lost each of their six WSL away games by an aggregate score of 1-19.
They have only won one of their three games this term (L2), but given United have attempted just 10 shots in the WSL in 2026-27, they will feel this is a good chance to get one over on them.

F7DCC6E843721A39D4F3296F94E92022.title: The MLS Wrap: Son can’t stop LAFC slump while Revs overtake Messi’s Miami
F7DCC6E843721A39D4F3296F94E92022.subtitle: FotMob
paragraphs: NewsAboutTV schedulesThe MLS Wrap: Son can’t stop LAFC slump while Revs overtake Messi’s MiamiShareThe latest round of MLS matches came amid a moment of celebration for several first-time call-ups to Mauricio Pochettino’s United States team, including one for the league’s standout young star, Cavan Sullivan.

A few of those young players put in notable performances in the latest round of MLS matches, but it was Sullivan and his Philadelphia Union team who once again stole the limelight with a sensational comeback win in Kansas.
Was a wondergoal from Son Heung-min enough to give LAFC a much-needed win? And which team has come up on the rails to overtake Lionel Messi’s Inter Miami?
The latest MLS Wrap answers these questions and has the latest headlines, as well as unearthing some of the more under-the-radar stories in the North American league.
There have been points throughout the last three years when you simply can’t do a weekly roundup of MLS without mentioning Inter Miami and Messi.
The individual performances, coinciding with a team regularly winning games and challenging at the top of the table, meant they could not be ignored.
Even if you try to mix it up to give all the teams some coverage at some point, Messi and Miami demand inclusion most weeks.
Few other players have put in consecutive performances that necessitate such constant attention for their team, but one who is doing so currently is Cavan Sullivan at Philadelphia Union.

The Union’s run since Ryan Richter took over as interim coach is outstanding. They are yet to lose an MLS game during his tenure, and this weekend took that unbeaten run to 11 games in the league, featuring nine wins.

Their run of consecutive wins currently stands at five games thanks to a remarkable 4-3 win against Sporting Kansas City this weekend, coming back to take all three points despite having gone 3-0 down.
What's more, all four of their goals were scored in the space of ten second-half minutes.
A Sporting KC collapse or an unbelievable Philadelphia Union comeback?
Either way, Sullivan, who scored one of those goals to take him to six in his last six games, and the Union are in the headlines once again.

They haven’t stormed up the table like Philadelphia Union, and aren’t one of those teams having a season of two halves that can be separated neatly into pre and post-World Cup narratives, but New England Revolution have gone about the business of winning more games than they lose or draw in 2026, and have sneaked above Inter Miami in the table as a result.
They also boast a teenage American star of their own in 18-year-old Peyton Miller.
The winger scored twice in this weekend’s 4-2 win against Orlando City, building on the one he scored last week against Chicago Fire, and on the three assists in three games he managed in August.
Precise finishes on the break showed his composure even when running at speed with plenty of time to think. Not bad for a player who started out as a left-back.
On the back of such performances, he received a deserved first call-up to the USMNT for the upcoming international window.

The Revolution also have Carles Gil, who has consistently been one of the best players in MLS for eight seasons now, regardless of the kind of form in which the New England team as a whole have been in those years.

Gil contributed a brace of his own to go with Miller’s, and if they can continue with this combination of individual talent and teamwork and results, they may well remain above Inter Miami for the rest of the season and be a threat in the playoffs.

a6b5quefmea11nqh9jbab1pao.title: Run of clean sheets should give Liverpool confidence, says Alisson
a6b5quefmea11nqh9jbab1pao.subtitle: Liverpool have gone three Premier League games without conceding ahead of the extended international break, with Alisson buoyed by that run.
paragraphs: Alisson says Liverpool's run of three straight clean sheets in the Premier League should give them confidence for the rest of the season, having ironed out their early defensive woes.
Liverpool started the Andoni Iraola era with back-to-back 2-2 draws against Newcastle United and Nottingham Forest, never leading either game at any point and looking shaky at the back.

It has been a different story since they beat Ipswich Town 2-0 with an Alexander Isak brace on September 4, though, having drawn 0-0 with Fulham before overcoming Iraola's former club Bournemouth 1-0 on Sunday.

Only Arsenal (4.04) and Forest (4.8) have given up a lower expected goals against (xGA) figure than Liverpool's 6.12 in the Premier League this season, with Leeds United and Everton (three apiece) the only sides to concede fewer goals than their four.
Alisson, meanwhile, has registered the fifth highest save percentage in the league (77.8%), also preventing 0.8 goals according to Opta's expected goals on target (xGoT) model.

The Brazil international made one superb save at the Vitality Stadium, getting down to his right to tip Evanilson's improvised attempt around the post, and he can feel the Reds' backline growing more assured with every shutout.
"I think every Premier League match away from home is tough to play. You have to fight a lot, and this wasn't any different for us," he told Liverpool's website.

"It wasn't the cleanest performance I think we've had, but those games, if you don’t play so well and then you still win it – and keep the clean sheet – I think this brings confidence for the rest of the season as well."
Another key factor in Liverpool's defensive improvement has been the form of new centre-back Jeremy Jacquet, who was named Player of the Match following Sunday's win.
Only Alexis Mac Allister (seven times) won possession more often for Liverpool than the 21-year-old (six, level with Ronald Araujo), while he also won three of his four duels.
But as Alisson noted, playing alongside a defender of Virgil van Dijk's calibre has made the youngster's adaptation smoother.
"I think Jeremy played really well. Virgil, the back four, Ronald, Milos [Kerkez], the midfielders as well, they helped us a lot defensively. Everybody fights a lot," Alisson continued.
"Jeremy has so much quality, of course, but I don't think it's the hardest job in the world to play alongside Virgil van Dijk! Virgil helped him a lot as well.
"I tried to help Ronald as well, someone who came to make us more solid defensively, and he's delivering as well. So, we are really happy to have them in our side."

Iraola is the first manager to remain unbeaten in his first five league games in charge of Liverpool (W2 D3) since Joe Fagan in September 1983, and he will look to keep his positive start going against Manchester City on October 11.

anil5wqtoq5a1jltql8l28jie.title: Fabian eager to follow up World Cup triumph with Nations League success
anil5wqtoq5a1jltql8l28jie.subtitle: Fabian Ruiz won the World Cup with Spain in the summer, and is now determined to progress in the Nations League.
paragraphs: Fabian Ruiz has welcomed the challenge of "winning again" as Spain prepare for their Nations League opener against England on Saturday.
Spain's clash with Thomas Tuchel's side at Wembley Stadium will be their first since defeating Argentina in the World Cup final back in July.
It marked La Roja's second triumph in the competition, while they now simultaneously hold the World Cup and the Euros, as they did from 2008 to 2012.
Spain are unbeaten in each of their last 38 matches in all competitions (W29 D9), the longest-ever streak by a European nation.
Despite their recent success, Fabian acknowledged how difficult it will be to continue winning trophies on the international stage.
"The manager has already told us that the past is forgotten; it's history, and that's wonderful, but now it's time to focus on the present," Fabian told AS.
"The hardest thing in football is winning again. Winning once is great, but doing it again is the difficult part.

"That's the challenge we have now: to want to win again, to keep winning. It's very difficult, but this team has what it takes to do it, and we're going for this title with a lot of enthusiasm; we also consider it very important.
"We hope to be in the final four [of the Nations League]."

Spain have reached the final in three of the last four Nations League tournaments, losing on penalties in the most recent in 2024-25; excluding penalties, La Roja have lost just one of their last 18 matches in the competition (W10 D7).
Luis de la Fuente's side have also won six of their last nine meetings with England across all competitions (D1 L2), most recently winning 2-1 in the final of the 2024 European Championship.
Their last away game against the Three Lions also ended 2-1, at Wembley in the Nations League in September 2018.

bfklrj0mtfyz1eaw5sr080xon.title: Yamal feels World Cup triumph should aid Ballon d'Or bid
bfklrj0mtfyz1eaw5sr080xon.subtitle: Lamine Yamal has continued to make his case for winning the Ballon d'Or, and he feels Spain's World Cup success should be a consideration.
paragraphs: Lamine Yamal believes lifting the World Cup with Spain should aid his hopes of winning the Ballon d'Or, with Harry Kane and Kylian Mbappe viewed as his main rivals.

Yamal helped La Roja win their second world title in North America this year, although his individual impact at the tournament was limited after his 2025-26 season was ended prematurely by a hamstring injury.

He registered 24 goals and 17 assists in 45 outings across all competitions last season, helping Barcelona retain their LaLiga title, with his 41 combined goal involvements being the sixth-most of any player from Europe's top five leagues.
Yamal also attempted (429) and completed (225) the most dribbles of any player, while his 59 chances created following carries were also the most.
On Tuesday, Spain coach Luis de la Fuente declared one of his players should win the prize, just as Rodri did when they triumphed at Euro 2024.
And Yamal, who has not been shy about making his case as the October 26 ceremony inches closer, concurs with that view.

"It's the award for the best player of the year, a player who is different, who is a pleasure to watch play, the one who has that magic, who makes you smile, who makes you want to watch a game just for him," Yamal said in an interview with L'Equipe.
"I think my way of playing is my strongest argument and what makes me different.
"It's very important, in addition to being a good player, that you make your team win.
"The advantage I have is that I have been able to win the World Cup this year and, obviously, that is a plus for me.
"But if a person says, 'Lionel Messi deserves it' or 'Rodri deserves it', that's totally respectable."
Having come through the ranks at Barca, Yamal has faced plenty of comparisons to Messi, who he outshone in the World Cup final as Spain edged out Argentina in extra time.
But the 19-year-old wants to be remembered on his own terms, saying: "I play to make history, so that in 30 years' time, young people will say, 'he was really very good too'.
"But I don't want to compare myself to anyone. I want to be Lamine Yamal, I want to be remembered as Lamine Yamal, and I hope to be among the greats."

Yamal will be in action for Spain on Saturday, as they go to Wembley to face England in their opening Nations League fixture, defending a 38-game unbeaten run (W29 D9), which is the longest ever streak by a European nation.
