k7w5zq6s68fm1xh6odhr5uuv9.title: Mbappe reveals his mother wanted him to join Liverpool in 2017
k7w5zq6s68fm1xh6odhr5uuv9.subtitle: Real Madrid and France superstar Kylian Mbappe could have joined Liverpool nine years ago, if his mother had her way.
paragraphs: Kylian Mbappe has revealed he was "close" to joining Liverpool in 2017, after his mother and agent, Fayza Lamari, "fell in love" with the club during negotiations with Jurgen Klopp.

Nine years ago, Mbappe was one of the hottest properties in world football after bursting onto the scene with Monaco, having registered 40 goal involvements in just 60 appearances for the club (27 goals, 13 assists).
Mbappe ultimately joined PSG in a loan deal that became permanent the following year, plundering 256 goals in 308 outings for the Parisiens and winning 15 trophies, including six Ligue 1 titles.
He then, of course, moved to Real Madrid in 2024, and though he has scored 94 goals in just 111 games for the Spanish giants, he is yet to win the Champions League, LaLiga, or the Copa del Rey.

While working as a German television pundit at this year's World Cup, at which Mbappe became the tournament's all-time leading scorer with 22 goals, Klopp reflected on Liverpool's pursuit of the then-teenage sensation.
Klopp disclosed he accompanied several Liverpool officials on a private plane from Blackpool to Nice, where they met with Mbappe and his mother to discuss a potential transfer.
And on Tuesday, in an interview with The Athletic, Mbappe revealed just how close he came to moving to Anfield.
"It was while I was playing in Monaco. I had to take a decision," Mbappe said. "And yes, I was close to Liverpool.
"My mum was a big fan of Jurgen Klopp and the favourite destination for my mum was Liverpool. She wanted me to go there.
"I didn't listen because I wanted to play in my city, in Paris. I didn't want to leave my country before I was someone.
"But yes, my mum was always saying, 'Liverpool, you're going to be there, playing at Anfield, it's going to be insane for you.' I was like, 'Okay!'

"She went there for the first step of negotiations. She went to the city, she went to the stadium, she met the people. She was like, 'It's a wonderful club, everybody's so kind, it's a family club, a big club.'
"She went to Anfield and fell in love with it. She watched a few games alone, to feel the atmosphere, because she wanted to imagine me in this stadium.

"All the time, we were talking. She'd say, 'For me, you have to go to Liverpool'. I said, 'Okay, okay, okay', because Jurgen Klopp was an amazing manager. I met him and had a wonderful relationship with him. I had big respect for him."

Reflecting on Klopp's attempts to explain Liverpool's project, Mbappe added: "I said, 'You don't need to convince me. You're Jurgen Klopp, it's Liverpool, a great club, so if I'm here, I have some interest. But I have other things, other projects, that are also good.'
"I said to him, 'Whatever decision I take is going to be a good decision, because we are talking about some of the biggest clubs in the world.'
"It's a funny story. But in the end, I took the decision to go to PSG because for me, born and raised in Paris, there was no better feeling than to show I could be a star in my hometown."
Mbappe will be in action for France during the international break, with Les Bleus' first game under Zinedine Zidane pitting them against Turkiye on Friday, in the Nations League.

While working as a German television pundit at this year's World Cup, at which Mbappe became the tournament's all-time leading scorer with 22 goals, Klopp reflected on Liverpool's pursuit of the then-teenage sensation.

Klopp disclosed he accompanied several Liverpool officials on a private plane from Blackpool to Nice, where they met with Mbappe and his mother to discuss a potential transfer.

And on Tuesday, in an interview with The Athletic, Mbappe revealed just how close he came to moving to Anfield. 

"It was while I was playing in Monaco. I had to take a decision," Mbappe said. "And yes, I was close to Liverpool. 

"My mum was a big fan of Jurgen Klopp and the favourite destination for my mum was Liverpool. She wanted me to go there.

"I didn't listen because I wanted to play in my city, in Paris. I didn't want to leave my country before I was someone. 

"But yes, my mum was always saying, 'Liverpool, you're going to be there, playing at Anfield, it's going to be insane for you.' I was like, 'Okay!'

"She went there for the first step of negotiations. She went to the city, she went to the stadium, she met the people. She was like, 'It's a wonderful club, everybody's so kind, it's a family club, a big club.'

"She went to Anfield and fell in love with it. She watched a few games alone, to feel the atmosphere, because she wanted to imagine me in this stadium.

"All the time, we were talking. She'd say, 'For me, you have to go to Liverpool'. I said, 'Okay, okay, okay', because Jurgen Klopp was an amazing manager. I met him and had a wonderful relationship with him. I had big respect for him."

Reflecting on Klopp's attempts to explain Liverpool's project, Mbappe added: "I said, 'You don't need to convince me. You're Jurgen Klopp, it's Liverpool, a great club, so if I'm here, I have some interest. But I have other things, other projects, that are also good.'

"I said to him, 'Whatever decision I take is going to be a good decision, because we are talking about some of the biggest clubs in the world.'

"It's a funny story. But in the end, I took the decision to go to PSG because for me, born and raised in Paris, there was no better feeling than to show I could be a star in my hometown."

Mbappe will be in action for France during the international break, with Les Bleus' first game under Zinedine Zidane pitting them against Turkiye on Friday, in the Nations League.

ktrfhh9h465d1pb339g4qt7bh.title: Noonan wants to build on Cincinnati's 'deciding moment' against Houston
ktrfhh9h465d1pb339g4qt7bh.subtitle: FC Cincinnati are right in the mix for a playoff spot in the Eastern Conference, and they face a struggling CF Montreal side next.
paragraphs: Pat Noonan believes FC Cincinnati's last-gasp draw against the Houston Dynamo could be a "deciding moment" in their quest to reach the playoffs this season.
Cincinnati found themselves 2-0 down after 51 minutes at Shell Energy Stadium thanks to goals from Guilherme and Mateusz Bogusz, the latter scoring from the penalty spot.
Bryan Ramirez halved the deficit in the 73rd minute before Kevin Denkey scored a spot-kick in the seventh minute of second-half stoppage time to seal a share of the spoils.
It was a result that kept Cincinnati ninth in the Eastern Conference, but the likes of New York City FC, D.C. United and Toronto FC are all chasing Noonan's side.
Cincinnati make the trip to Stade Saputo this weekend to face struggling CF Montreal, and Noonan believes his team's latest stalemate could be a solid foundation to build on.
"I think it could be a deciding moment in this stretch run," Noonan said. "We have nine games left in the season, and every game is going to be so important to pick up points.
"And that's because of the position that we're in, where we're fighting for a playoff spot. This isn't about everything being pretty now, or style.
"We were able to get an important point, and so, for the psyche of the group and how to be on the road, like I said, against a strong opponent and push the game like that.
"How do we get more of that urgency, but not recklessness?"
Montreal, meanwhile, will just want the 2026 season to come to an end after they were beaten 2-0 by the Columbus Crew in their last league match.
Only Sporting Kansas City (17) have lost more MLS matches this season than Montreal (15), who find themselves rooted to the bottom of the East on 21 points from 26 games.
It's also been a disappointing start to Alexis Sanchez's Montreal career, as he has failed to register a single goal contribution in his seven matches for the club.
During their defeat to Columbus, Sanchez's frustrations were evident as his team struggled to create any opportunities whenever they got the chance to go forward.
Interim boss Philippe Eullaffroy understood the Chilean's concerns about the team, but he said Sanchez remained committed to the cause and was just showing his passion.
"Alexis would like the team to play faster forward and use more space behind the defenders. I agree, and I ask for it, but it is not happening," Eullaffroy conceded.
"After the game, he was upset and tense about the development of the second half, as were several of his team-mates."
Montreal – Prince Owusu
In a season of frustration for Montreal, Owusu has been the only shining light, scoring 13 goals in 24 league appearances so far this season.
Owusu also has a good record against Montreal. He has scored three goals in six MLS outings against them, only managing to find the back of the net more against D.C. (four).
Cincinnati – Kevin Denkey
With Denkey unavailable after being selected to represent Togo during the international break, Evander will be the man Cincinnati will turn to in the final third.
Only Inter Miami's Lionel Messi (33) has more goal involvements in the MLS this season than Evander's 25 (13 goals, 12 assists).
MATCH PREDICTION: DRAW

Cincinnati earned a draw when trailing by two goals for the eighth time in the club's MLS era (since 2019) against Houston last time out. Three of those occurrences have happened this season and in all three of those occurrences in 2026, they had trailed by two goals in the second half.
But they will be hoping for a better result here. They have a good record against Montreal, winning their last four MLS meetings against them.
And Noonan's side will be desperate for a win. They are without a victory in their last five league matches (D3 L2) since a 2-1 triumph over NYCFC on August 19.

Montreal, meanwhile, will be out to end their poor run at Stade Saputo. Only Minnesota United (two) have fewer home wins in the MLS this season than Montreal (three), who last won in front of their home crowd on May 9 against Orlando City.

mr1iggwb17y81ahlcehafr1g3.title: Van Dijk only needed '10 seconds' to decide Netherlands future in Xavi meeting
mr1iggwb17y81ahlcehafr1g3.subtitle: After considering international retirement, Virgil van Dijk plans to continue until Euro 2028, despite the fact he will turn 37 that year.
paragraphs: Virgil van Dijk said it took him 10 seconds to decide to continue playing for the Netherlands when he held a meeting with new head coach Xavi.
Some had questioned whether the 2026 World Cup might be Van Dijk's last major international tournament, after the Netherlands impressively won their group before crashing out in the round of 32.
They were beaten on penalties by Morocco following a 1-1 draw, failing to reach the round of 16 when appearing at the World Cup for the very first time (failed to qualify on eight occasions).
Van Dijk has won 96 caps for his country and, after deciding to play on, he could bring up a century during the current international break.
The Netherlands open their Nations League campaign at home to Germany on Thursday, before back-to-back away games versus Serbia and Greece, and a home clash with Serbia on October 4.
And when former World Cup-winning midfielder Xavi visited Van Dijk in Liverpool to discuss his international future, the centre-back was given an easy decision.
"I needed a well-deserved holiday with my family and then an important meeting with the national coach," he said at a press conference, as quoted by De Telegraaf.
"After 10 seconds, I already knew I could continue. That was just a very good meeting. It's about trust and appreciation, and he said I could be important to the team.
"Physically, there is no doubt [I can continue], but I also want to keep having fun and feel the appreciation, and that is certainly there."
Van Dijk expects to play in a back four under Xavi, whose predecessor Ronald Koeman was repeatedly criticised by the Dutch media for reverting to a five-man backline during his two spells in charge.
"The way I experience it now, I don't think we're going to play with five at the back," Van Dijk said.
"Spain became world champions with four at the back. Most players are used to playing with four defenders."
Thursday's matchup in Amsterdam will pit Van Dijk against one of the most influential figures in his career, with former Liverpool boss Jurgen Klopp taking charge of Germany for the first time.
Van Dijk played 270 games under Klopp after being signed from Southampton by the German in January 2018, comfortably the most he has played under a single manager (Arne Slot is second, with 104).

And though Van Dijk wishes Klopp well in his new role, he is determined to inflict a debut defeat on his old boss, saying: "It's very nice to meet him again. He has been a very important person in my career, like Ronald Koeman.

"I was able to speak to him during the World Cup, after a training session in Dallas. It will be nice to see him again tomorrow, but hopefully we can make sure that he loses his first game as the coach of Germany."

msgz9o7jbdtj1tyq3mhlzvhcm.title: Mbappe has a 'good feeling' about Ballon d'Or
msgz9o7jbdtj1tyq3mhlzvhcm.subtitle: Kylian Mbappe has previously insisted he should win the Ballon d'Or this year, and the Frenchman has a "good feeling" about the award.
paragraphs: Kylian Mbappe has a "good feeling" about winning the Ballon d'Or this year.
Mbappe has been highly vocal recently over his ambitions to win the award for the first time.
The Frenchman is likely to be going up against Bayern Munich's Harry Kane and Barcelona superstar Lamine Yamal, who has also insisted he should be considered as the favourite for the award.
While Yamal played a role in Spain winning the World Cup, Mbappe has scored 50 goals in 52 games for Real Madrid since the start of last season.
Of players in Europe's top five leagues, only Kane (67) has netted more club goals than Mbappe in that time.

Mbappe, who is also on 499 goal involvements in his club career, also finished as the top scorer at the World Cup, with 10 strikes to his name. He is now the record goalscorer in the history of the competition (22 goals).
And the 27-year-old feels this is his time to win the Ballon d'Or.
He told RFI: "I've had a good year. I've had a great year on an individual level, and I know that's the most important criterion for the Ballon d'Or.
"I was the top scorer in all the major competitions, and I think this could be a good year for me. I've got a good feeling about it.
"At the Ballon d’Or, they won’t be announcing a team in the envelope, but a player. So it's an individual trophy, and I think that's what has to take precedence over everything else.

"Of course, we must not overlook everything else, but the ability to perform well individually and to leave a lasting impression is what makes an impact on people when it comes to a trophy like that."
When it was put to him if he would be disappointed not to win the Ballon d'Or, Mbappe said: "Of course.
"A competitor is always disappointed when he doesn’t win. At that point, I think it'll be my competitive spirit that takes a knock. But we'll have to wait and see how it all pans out."

n4htqqxe4hwi12rxzeicpwdr2.title: Jesus confirms Ronaldo will start on Portugal bow against Wales
n4htqqxe4hwi12rxzeicpwdr2.subtitle: Jorge Jesus is preparing for his first match in charge of Portugal against Wales, and he confirmed Cristiano Ronaldo would start.
paragraphs: Jorge Jesus has confirmed that Cristiano Ronaldo will start his first game in charge of Portugal, against Wales in the opening match of their Nations League campaign.
Portugal welcome Wales to the Estadio Jose Alvalade on Thursday in what will be their first match since exiting the World Cup against eventual champions Spain in the last 16.
Roberto Martinez's three-year reign was brought to an end, with Jesus appointed as his successor on a four-year contract, taking him through to the World Cup in 2030.
The 72-year-old is a player Ronaldo knows well, with the pair linking up at Al-Nassr, where they became Saudi Pro League champions for the first time since Ronaldo arrived.
Ronaldo scored 29 goals in 33 appearances under Jesus for Al Nassr in the 2025-26 campaign, averaging a goal every 99 minutes.

Throughout his career, the only managers under whom Ronaldo has a better goals-per-game average in league play are Carlo Ancelotti (1.22) and Jose Mourinho (1.13) at Real Madrid, and Luis Castro and Rudi Garcia at Al-Nassr (both 1.1).
Following his unveiling, Jesus insisted Ronaldo "would never be a problem" for Portugal, and he revealed he intends to start the five-time Ballon d'Or winner against Wales.
"We have been in many situations of major competitions, such as the Champions League and the World Cup," Jesus said.
"I have never seen an audience with so many people. It's also good, football needs more and more agents to be shared with the national team and players.
"Today will be my first training on the field, because yesterday was a recovery session. And if nothing special happens, Cris will play tomorrow from the start."
This will be the first meeting between Portugal and Wales since the semi-finals of the 2016 European Championship, with the Selecao winning 2-0 en route to the trophy. .

Portugal are also the reigning Nations League holders, beating Spain on penalties in 2024-25. They have won 11 of 14 home matches in the competition (D1 L2), losing only to France (in November 2020) and Spain (in September 2022).

After their defeat to Spain at the World Cup, Portugal will be looking to avoid back-to-back losses for the first time since September and October 2014, when they were beaten by Albania and then France.

They will fancy their chances against a Wales side that remain winless in their last four matches (D3 L1), their worst run under manager Craig Bellamy. Not since 2012 have they had a longer winless start to a calendar year (L5).
Jesus was asked about the relative importance of the Nations League, or whether his full attention was on the 2028 European Championships and the 2030 World Cup.
"I'm in a team that has the best players in the world. All goals are to win," Jesus added.
"And therefore, the first competition is the Nations League, and we are the holders of the title and, of course, we have to defend it."

ns1rmjamy8tk1d0jmm3ez0n16.title: Mbappe: 'Disrespectful' to advise Olise to join Real Madrid this summer
ns1rmjamy8tk1d0jmm3ez0n16.subtitle: Michael Olise was linked with a stunning move to Real Madrid this summer, something Kylian Mbappe did not want to be involved with.
paragraphs: Kylian Mbappe said it would have been "disrespectful" to advise France team-mate Michael Olise to join him at Real Madrid this summer.
Olise was the subject of speculation after a stunning second season with Bayern Munich, which saw him help the club win the Bundesliga and DFB-Pokal.
He ended the Bundesliga season with 34 goal involvements (15 goals, 19 assists), a new record for a winger since Opta data collection began in the German top flight in 2004-05.
Only Harry Kane (41) directly contributed to more Bundesliga goals than Olise, who also scored five goals and provided seven assists in 13 Champions League games.
Florentino Perez pledged to spend big on a 'Galactico' player prior to winning Madrid's presidential election, only for the club to deny making a move for the in-demand Olise.
Olise carried on his form into the World Cup, becoming the first player on record (since 1966) to register seven assists in a single edition of FIFA's flagship competition.

Across Europe's top five leagues in all competitions this season, only Barcelona duo Raphinha (17) and Lamine Yamal (14) have managed more goal contributions than Olise's 11 (eight goals, three assists).
"I was aware of the speculation," Mbappe said. "But I know the situation well myself. Back when I was a PSG player, there were countless rumours.
"And I feel it would be disrespectful to advise a player to make a move. That would be unfair to Bayern, especially since Bayern is a great club where Michael can achieve a lot.
"One thing is clear, though: every club in the world would love to have Michael Olise. He is an outstanding player."
Olise's stunning performances in 2025-26 saw him crowned the Bundesliga Player of the Season.
Mbappe has faced criticism after failing to win a major trophy since joining Madrid in 2024, with Jose Mourinho returning this summer in a bid to change the team's fortunes.
The 27-year-old has managed eight goals and two assists in eight appearances in all competitions, and he believes Mourinho is the right man to lead Madrid back to glory.
"Jose Mourinho is extremely intelligent," Mbappe added. "That's why he's been able to achieve such great success in his career.
"He's very close to us players, and takes a real interest in us. He's a leader, he knows exactly how to get the best out of us."

Mbappe is preparing to play for France for the first time since their third-place defeat at the World Cup to England, with Turkiye their opponents in the first match of their Nations League campaign this Friday.

With two goals and an assist against England in their 6-4 defeat, Mbappe now holds the record for the most goal involvements on record (since 1966) at a single World Cup (14 – 10 goals, four assists), while no player has scored more World Cup goals than his 22.
He was asked whether he would follow in Cristiano Ronaldo's footsteps in turning out for his nation at 41-years-old, something Mbappe could not see himself doing.
"We have to be completely honest, considering the country I play for: France would never let me play until I'm 41," Mbappe said.
"Cristiano proves that if you're physically and mentally fit, you can play at a high level for a long time. In my case, though, I don't see it happening."

"Jose Mourinho is extremely intelligent," Mbappe added. "That's why he's been able to achieve such great success in his career.

"He's very close to us players, and takes a real interest in us. He's a leader, he knows exactly how to get the best out of us."

Mbappe is preparing to play for France for the first time since their third-place defeat at the World Cup to England, with Turkiye their opponents in the first match of their Nations League campaign this Friday. 

With two goals and an assist against England in their 6-4 defeat, Mbappe now holds the record for the most goal involvements on record (since 1966) at a single World Cup (14 – 10 goals, four assists), while no player has scored more World Cup goals than his 22. 

He was asked whether he would follow in Cristiano Ronaldo's footsteps in turning out for his nation at 41-years-old, something Mbappe could not see himself doing. 

"We have to be completely honest, considering the country I play for: France would never let me play until I'm 41," Mbappe said.

"Cristiano proves that if you're physically and mentally fit, you can play at a high level for a long time. In my case, though, I don't see it happening."

o0w0ojavvskfzvw31lgmcrhf.title: Robertson urges struggling Spurs to forget about last two seasons
o0w0ojavvskfzvw31lgmcrhf.subtitle: Tottenham are bottom of the Premier League after five games, having only escaped relegation by two points on the final day of last season.
paragraphs: Andy Robertson says Tottenham's players must forget about their struggles over the last couple of seasons if they are to climb the Premier League table.

Spurs will spend the international break bottom of the Premier League with just two points on the board, with this the first time they have propped up the table at least five games into a season since 2008-09.

Roberto De Zerbi's side did at least end their goalless start to the campaign against Aston Villa on Saturday, but after going down 3-2, they have lost 50 of their 141 Premier League games at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.
In just seven years at the venue, they have suffered as many Premier League defeats as rivals Arsenal have suffered in 382 matches at the Emirates Stadium, which opened 20 years ago.
Spurs finished 17th in both 2024-25 and 2025-26, narrowly avoiding relegation in the latter of those seasons as they finished two points clear of West Ham on the final matchday.

They then spent over £300m on new players in the summer transfer window, but Robertson believes there is still a hangover from their disappointing recent seasons, which he and his fellow new arrivals can help to overcome.
"They're starting this journey. They've had a couple of really tough seasons in terms of finishes in the league," Robertson said in an appearance on The Overlaps' Stick to Football podcast.
"They've had to go into the market, they've spent a bit of money, but I do believe Tottenham are now starting a journey.

"Now, I don't know how far that journey can go, nobody does, but the determination in that group... you can see last season hurt them a lot. And maybe we're still guilty of carrying that weight of last season on our shoulders.

"That's the message of the manager, first and foremost. And also, that falls on me, and the other new players, if we need to forget. We need to now try and get Tottenham back to where we believe they belong. The fans are still carrying it as well and you don't blame them. They've been through such a tough time."
Robertson joined Tottenham on a free transfer after nine years with Liverpool, who he helped to win two Premier League titles, one FA Cup and two EFL Cups.
And when Robertson became aware his contract at Anfield would not be renewed, he immediately viewed Spurs as the most attractive destination available to him.
"I spoke directly to the manager. We had a couple of video calls over the summer. He's super ambitious, you can tell that as a manager," Robertson said of his initial conversations with De Zerbi.
"He wants to be able to win trophies. But he also knows that we need to start showing it sooner rather than later.
"It was always going to be Tottenham, even from January, as long as they stayed up. I ended up getting invested in Tottenham games.
"I was watching Tottenham thinking, 'come on', especially when De Zerbi came in. I was fully confident; I was really happy with how much Spurs wanted me."

Spurs' next Premier League game is against Manchester United at Old Trafford on October 10, with the Red Devils making their joint-worst start to a Premier League season after five matches (five points, level with 2014-15).

o7k6ie5pw9vm19jmzjjysrlqa.title: 'When he calls, you can't say no' – Ebnoutalib credits Klopp for choice to represent Germany
o7k6ie5pw9vm19jmzjjysrlqa.subtitle: Younes Ebnoutalib was eligible to represent either Germany or Morocco, and he says talks with Jurgen Klopp made his mind up.
paragraphs: Eintracht Frankfurt forward Younes Ebnoutalib has highlighted the role Jurgen Klopp played in his choice to represent Germany over Morocco, saying: "When he calls, you can't say no."

Klopp has named a larger, 44-man squad for his first international break in charge of Germany, who face the Netherlands in their Nations League opener on Thursday, before taking on Greece twice, either side of a home clash with Serbia.
Sixteen of them are uncapped as Klopp looks to familiarise himself with as many players as possible, with 23-year-old attacker Ebnoutalib among them.
Having joined Eintracht from Elversberg in a €10m deal in January, Ebnoutalib has made a superb start to this season, scoring four goals in as many Bundesliga games.

Only Patrik Schick, Phillip Tietz, Michael Olise and Yuito Suzuki can match that tally, with Ebnoutalib finding the net with all but one of his shots on target (five, from 11 total attempts) and overperforming his figure of 2.85 expected goals (xG).
Ebnoutalib represented Morocco at youth level, but talks with Jurgen Klopp left him in no doubt as to where his international future lay.
"I am very, very proud. There were also talks with Morocco, but they weren't as intense as with Jurgen," Ebnoutalib said.
"I'm just proud. You have to say, he is one of the best coaches in the world. And when he calls, you can't say no.
"The impression is very positive. He is, of course, someone who brings a great deal of experience and already has a certain presence because of what he has achieved over the years.
"So, naturally, you have a great deal of respect for him. But he was very nice and very likeable in the conversations.
"He is already very well known for the way he wants to play football, with high pressing, with a lot of energy and power. He has already fired us up.
"I think that's what he is known for, that he is very good at reaching people and getting them on board. He has certainly got us in the right mindset."

Klopp has overseen 1,080 matches across his managerial career, winning 588 of those (D256 L236). His 431 games in charge of Liverpool are the third-most by a manager in the club's history, behind Bill Shankly's 799 and Bob Paisley's 523.

Klopp's 334 Premier League games with the Reds, who won the title under him in 2019-20, are also the fifth-most with a single club in the history of the competition, after Arsene Wenger with Arsenal (828), Alex Ferguson with Manchester United (810), David Moyes with Everton (488) and Pep Guardiola with Manchester City (380).

Defender Philipp Treu is another player hoping to make his senior Germany debut in the coming days, with three of his Freiburg team-mates also called up following their run to the Europa League final last season.
"It's definitely something where you say, 'Hey, it's cool that I can now train under Jurgen Klopp'," Treu said of working with Klopp.
"And that's why I'm just looking forward to being on the pitch with him later, soaking it all in, and just giving it my all."

oa2hmo4uvcgy14ixcazdis5xb.title: Belgium and Italy in same situation, says Van Bommel ahead of debut
oa2hmo4uvcgy14ixcazdis5xb.subtitle: Mark van Bommel is preparing for his first game in charge of Belgium against Italy, and he believes the two teams are closely matched.
paragraphs: Mark van Bommel likened the situation surrounding Belgium to the one at Italy as he prepares for his debut in charge of the Red Devils in the Nations League.
Belgium make the trip to the Stadio Olimpico on Friday to begin their Nations League campaign, with this their first match since exiting the World Cup in the quarter-finals.
The 49-year-old is Belgium's third managerial change in as many years, and becomes the first Dutchman to take charge of the Red Devils since Dick Advocaat back in 2009.
Rudi Garcia was dismissed following the World Cup, with Belgium impressing in the group stage before losing late on to eventual tournament winners Spain in the last eight.

Excluding the third-place play-off match, Belgium have now been eliminated from each of their last four World Cup knockout stage ties against fellow UEFA nations, since beating Spain on penalties at the quarter-final stage of the 1986 tournament.
That brought an end to Garcia's reign. He took charge of 20 games, recording 12 wins (D6 L2), to finish with a 60% win rate, with Van Bommel the next man in the hot seat.
It is Van Bommel's fourth managerial role, and his first since spending two years in the Belgian Pro League with Royal Antwerp between 2022 and 2024.
He won 57 of his 107 matches in charge across all competitions (D21 L29), averaging 1.79 points per game along with a 51.4% win rate, while also winning three major titles.

But he comes up against another manager making his debut in Roberto Mancini, though it is his second stint with the Azzurri after he replaced Gennaro Gattuso following their failure to qualify for a third consecutive World Cup.
"It's not easy to prepare the team in four days. We had some meetings with the players to explain what we wanted to do," Van Bommel said.
"We want the ball, and if we lose it, to win it back as soon as possible. We want to dominate the game, but it’s not easy when starting a new era.
"We're in the Nations League against Italy, France and Turkiye, so there's no time to experiment, but Italy are in the same situation as us."
Van Bommel has named a strong 25-man squad for their clashes with Italy, France (home and away) and Turkiye, though some big names are also missing.
Thibaut Courtois is unavailable after requesting to be excused from the matches, while Jeremy Doku, Amadou Onana, Alexis Saelemaekers and Thomas Meunier also miss out.
He chose to name four uncapped players, which include goalkeepers Jari De Busser, Mike Penders and Maarten Vandevoordt, along with young full-back Kyriani Sabbe.
Kevin De Bruyne is also in despite struggling for fitness with Napoli, with reports saying Van Bommel flew to Italy to convince him to remain a part of the international set-up.
"Kevin, Lukaku, Tielemans, De Ketelaere, we have several players with a lot of experience, others who are in Serie A, so it's good that we can adapt to Italian football," he added.
"We've got players who can bring that experience to the team and help the younger members."

Van Bommel revealed he would adopt a 4-3-3 formation against Italy, but said his preparations had been hindered given the uncertainty around Mancini and whether he would change his tactics from his previous stint with Italy.
"It's difficult to prepare, because you don't know what he is going to do. Gattuso was the coach last season. I know Rino and his style of football," Van Bommel said.
"It won't be easy for Italy either. I watched many of Roberto's games. I'm not sure if he will do the same things, they might have a 4-3-3, we'll see."

qhsho3pm0as61xs0e18vg4pe7.title: Van Dijk: Utter nonsense I influenced Netherlands World Cup tactics
qhsho3pm0as61xs0e18vg4pe7.subtitle: Virgil van Dijk is not impressed by claims he influenced a tactical change at the World Cup, hitting back during a press conference.
paragraphs: Virgil van Dijk slammed the suggestion that he had forced Ronald Koeman into changing his Netherlands tactics at the World Cup as "utter nonsense".
The Netherlands were knocked out of the World Cup in the round of 32 on penalties by Morocco – after a 1-1 draw – having gone unbeaten throughout their group stage.
Van Dijk served as Koeman's captain throughout the tournament, with the 63-year-old leaving his position following their early exit.
In a press conference ahead of the Netherlands' Nations League clash with Germany, Van Dijk clashed with reporters after it was insinuated that he was involved in tactical shifts.
Koeman had played a back four throughout the group stage, where they won two of their games and drew the other, before switching to a back five for their clash with Morocco.
"One of your colleagues also said, of course, that it was my idea to switch to playing with a back five. That is utter nonsense," Van Dijk told one reporter.
"The fact is we simply failed at the World Cup. Those are the hard facts.
"We didn't play a good World Cup. It's not about me. You perform together; you're a team. Your claim that I destroyed Dutch football after the World Cup – that sort of thing is completely baseless.
"The plan is devised by the staff. Nonsense is being spread so that I look even worse. That happens far too often.
"I was told that it was my fault we played with five, that Ronald Koeman and I have destroyed Dutch football.
"The plan worked for 89 minutes, even though it was a bad match. We almost broke through. The idea that I destroyed Dutch football makes absolutely no sense. I didn't decide that."
Van Dijk will continue to captain the Netherlands under new head coach Xavi and could win his 100th cap in this extended international break if he plays in all four of their Nations League matches.
The first of which comes at home against Germany on Thursday.

qoth7vtxk05i1dxyoa71q6hza.title: Kolo Muani not facing spell out after hand surgery
qoth7vtxk05i1dxyoa71q6hza.subtitle: Randal Kolo Muani has undergone surgery on a fractured finger on his right hand, but he will not miss any time for Juventus.
paragraphs: Juventus have confirmed Randal Kolo Muani will remain available for selection after undergoing surgery on a fractured finger.
Kolo Muani played 89 minutes on Saturday as the Bianconeri returned to winning ways in Serie A, beating Atalanta 2-0 at the Allianz Stadium.
He played on despite sustaining an injury to his right hand, and though the issue required surgery, reports in Italy said he would return to training with Juve within a couple of days.
A statement released on Juve's website said: "During the first half of Sunday's match against Atalanta, Randal Kolo Muani sustained an injury to the fifth finger of his right hand.
"Tests carried out after the match revealed a fracture of the proximal phalanx, making osteosynthesis surgery necessary.
"The operation, performed this afternoon by Dr Loris Pegoli, was completely successful and the player will remain available for selection."
Kolo Muani has appeared in all six of the Bianconeri's matches in all competitions this season, starting five of those and recording one goal and two assists in 468 minutes.

He was not selected in Zinedine Zidane's first France squad ahead of their Nations League fixtures against Turkiye, Belgium and Italy, so will continue training with his club ahead of Juve facing Cagliari on October 11.

rrsw0lbtj8yh1b4ivbpwvxruq.title: Mancini: Winning start to Nations League the only medicine to cure Italy
rrsw0lbtj8yh1b4ivbpwvxruq.subtitle: Roberto Mancini begins his second stint in charge of Italy against Belgium in the Nations League, and he wants to get fans back onside.
paragraphs: Roberto Mancini believes a winning start to Italy's Nations League campaign will be the perfect medicine after the Azzurri missed out on the World Cup this summer.
Italy welcome Belgium to the Stadio Olimpico on Friday, for what will be Mancini's first match back in charge after replacing Gennaro Gattuso.
Mancini previously led the Azzurri from 2018 to 2023, guiding them to the European Championship title five years ago by beating England on penalties.
During his first spell, Mancini led Italy on a 37-match unbeaten streak, a European record that has since been surpassed by Spain following their victory over Argentina in the World Cup final.

The 61-year-old won 38 of his 58 games during his first stint (D12 L8) before resigning in August 2023 after a failed qualification bid for the 2022 World Cup in Qatar, before having a short-lived spell in charge of Saudi Arabia.
Italy have been placed in Group A1 alongside Belgium, France and Turkiye, and they will play all three nations during this extended international break.

The Azzurri have finished third in the Nations League twice, doing so in 2020-21 and 2022-23, and Mancini believes a good start will go some way to repairing the damaged relationship between the supporters and their team.
"To play well from the start, which won't be easy considering we've had just two days to prepare for this game," Mancini told reporters about his aims for the Nations League.
"This is what international football is like. We have to get things done quickly and get results. That is the only medicine for what ails us.
"We hope to reach the final four of the Nations League. It's a strong group and so it won't be easy, but we'll try. I can't wait to hear the national anthem playing.
"Many of these players are experienced, and naturally there is pressure, but it's positive pressure because playing football is their passion, and they need to enjoy it."

Mancini's last game in charge of Italy saw the Azzurri beat the Netherlands 3-2 to seal third place in the Nations League three years ago, but the end of his tenure was overshadowed by his failure to secure a spot at the Qatar World Cup.
After Luciano Spalletti's tenure, Gattuso also failed to lead Italy to the tournament, with Italy losing 4-1 on penalties to Bosnia-Herzegovina as they missed out on a third consecutive edition.
"Unfortunately, this is football, you can lose games sometimes in absurd fashion," Mancini added.
"But the good thing about the sport is that it gives you an opportunity to make up for it immediately. We must keep it in mind, but then focus on the future."
Gianluigi Donnarumma was in between the sticks for Italy during those near misses, and he too echoed the disappointment of Mancini.
Donnarumma has played for Italy since he was 17 years old, and following his nation's latest setback, he may not play at his first World Cup until he is 31.
"It's been very tough," Donnarumma told Sky Sport Italia. "I struggle to even explain it. This has been a very long and difficult summer, but we must start again.
"It's a new era, tomorrow we have a big game and the fans like us are disappointed, so it's up to us to fire them up and get them to fall back in love with the Azzurri jersey."

Roberto Mancini believes a winning start to Italy's Nations League campaign will be the perfect medicine after the Azzurri missed out on the World Cup this summer. 

Italy welcome Belgium to the Stadio Olimpico on Friday, for what will be Mancini's first match back in charge after replacing Gennaro Gattuso.

Mancini previously led the Azzurri from 2018 to 2023, guiding them to the European Championship title five years ago by beating England on penalties. 

During his first spell, Mancini led Italy on a 37-match unbeaten streak, a European record that has since been surpassed by Spain following their victory over Argentina in the World Cup final. 

The 61-year-old won 38 of his 58 games during his first stint (D12 L8) before resigning in August 2023 after a failed qualification bid for the 2022 World Cup in Qatar, before having a short-lived spell in charge of Saudi Arabia.

Italy have been placed in Group A1 alongside Belgium, France and Turkiye, and they will play all three nations during this extended international break. 

The Azzurri have finished third in the Nations League twice, doing so in 2020-21 and 2022-23, and Mancini believes a good start will go some way to repairing the damaged relationship between the supporters and their team.

"To play well from the start, which won't be easy considering we've had just two days to prepare for this game," Mancini told reporters about his aims for the Nations League.

"This is what international football is like. We have to get things done quickly and get results. That is the only medicine for what ails us.

"We hope to reach the final four of the Nations League. It's a strong group and so it won't be easy, but we'll try. I can't wait to hear the national anthem playing.

"Many of these players are experienced, and naturally there is pressure, but it's positive pressure because playing football is their passion, and they need to enjoy it."

Mancini's last game in charge of Italy saw the Azzurri beat the Netherlands 3-2 to seal third place in the Nations League three years ago, but the end of his tenure was overshadowed by his failure to secure a spot at the Qatar World Cup. 

After Luciano Spalletti's tenure, Gattuso also failed to lead Italy to the tournament, with Italy losing 4-1 on penalties to Bosnia-Herzegovina as they missed out on a third consecutive edition. 

"Unfortunately, this is football, you can lose games sometimes in absurd fashion," Mancini added.

"But the good thing about the sport is that it gives you an opportunity to make up for it immediately. We must keep it in mind, but then focus on the future."

Gianluigi Donnarumma was in between the sticks for Italy during those near misses, and he too echoed the disappointment of Mancini. 

Donnarumma has played for Italy since he was 17 years old, and following his nation's latest setback, he may not play at his first World Cup until he is 31. 

"It's been very tough," Donnarumma told Sky Sport Italia. "I struggle to even explain it. This has been a very long and difficult summer, but we must start again.

"It's a new era, tomorrow we have a big game and the fans like us are disappointed, so it's up to us to fire them up and get them to fall back in love with the Azzurri jersey."

rtpfqwg2ox3h1se8jv58r9u3n.title: Netherlands boss Xavi relishing 'great challenge' against Klopp's Germany
rtpfqwg2ox3h1se8jv58r9u3n.subtitle: Xavi begins his tenure with the Netherlands against Germany in the Nations League, and he is looking forward to the challenge ahead.
paragraphs: Xavi described his first game in charge of the Netherlands as a "great challenge" as they prepare to welcome Germany and Jurgen Klopp to the Johan Cruijff Arena on Thursday.
It is a meeting of two coaches making their debuts for the respective nations, with Xavi having replaced Ronald Koeman after another early exit at this summer's World Cup.
The Netherlands were eliminated from the World Cup in the round of 32 on penalties by Morocco, the first time they had failed to reach the last 16 at the tournament.
Xavi had been out of management since leaving Barcelona in 2024, having won LaLiga in 2022-23 and the Supercopa de Espana in the same season.
He compiled 90 wins, 23 draws and 29 defeats in 142 games in charge of the Blaugrana across all competitions, giving him a win percentage of 62.7%.
Xavi is the first foreign coach of the Netherlands since Ernst Happel in 1977-1978, and he is looking forward to going head-to-head with former Liverpool boss Klopp.
"We have to play our best football tomorrow because Germany are a great team," Xavi told reporters.
"I can feel this rivalry. Everyone in our team is really looking forward to the game, and it is a great way for us to start this journey.
"He [Klopp] has been one of the best coaches in the world in recent years. It will be a great challenge for the whole team and for me personally.
"It is always the goal to win, but it is even more important to leave a good impression with the execution. I want the team to show passion, ambition, desire and our philosophy."
When he was unveiled, Xavi described himself as a "winner" and he was confident that his success as a player could be translated to the Netherlands' dugout.
Xavi also believes the quality within the Netherlands' ranks can deliver what he intends to achieve.
"They have the capacity to carry out what we ask of them. I have clearly seen that in the training sessions," Xavi added.
"They are hard workers and are open to listening. I am very happy with that. And I was impressed by the physical aspect, among other things."
The Netherlands also face back-to-back away games versus Serbia and Greece, and a home clash with Serbia on October 4 after they take on Germany.
Memphis Depay, Wout Weghorst, Marten de Roon, Guus Til and injured midfielder Mats Wieffer are missing from Xavi's first Netherlands squad.

Ruben van Bommel and Gjivai Zechiel have been handed senior call-ups, while Jurrien Timber is also expected to feature throughout their four matches having struggled with a groin injury at the start of the campaign.
"We are now focused on tomorrow, not on the rest of the matches. We are ready," Xavi said.
"We have to be a bit careful with Jurrien Timber, who was injured for a long time. But he is available, that goes for everyone."

spg5pl0s04xv14ffyt4svtu51.title: Bellamy concedes Wales had to 'suffer a lot' against Portugal
spg5pl0s04xv14ffyt4svtu51.subtitle: Wales were narrowly beaten by Portugal to start their Nations League campaign, with Craig Bellamy's side put under pressure in Lisbon.
paragraphs: Craig Bellamy admitted Wales had to "suffer a lot" against Portugal but hailed his injury-hit side's resilience in their Nations League opener.
Wales began their Nations League campaign with a narrow 1-0 defeat to Portugal, with Joao Felix's deflected first-half strike proving the difference.
Cristiano Ronaldo also had a goal ruled out for offside after the break, while Wales finished the contest on top, hitting the woodwork late on through Brennan Johnson.

Despite that, Wales are without a win in their last five matches in all competitions (D3 L2), while they have lost five of their last 10 matches (W2 D3), one more than in their previous 25 outings (W11 D10 L4).
The 23 shots Wales faced against Portugal is their most in a single game since a Nations League match against Turkiye in November 2024 (25).
But Bellamy was impressed with how his team played despite being under pressure for long spells in the game.
"It was a difficult game for us. We had to suffer a lot," said Bellamy.
"I think that's the longest we've been in a game without the ball.
"We could have done more with the ball, but I'm beyond proud as well.
"We have a lot of players who weren't here. That's OK; we can handle it.

"A lot of players who don't play week in, week out. So, for them to use the energy they were able to, we've got to have a big heart to be able to do that. They've always shown that, and they showed that again."
The loss leaves Wales bottom of Group A4 after the first matchday, with Norway and Denmark also drawn alongside them.
Wales are missing the likes of Harry Wilson, Karl Darlow, Joe Rodon, Dylan Lawlor and Nathan Broadhead through injury, and face a quick turnaround before facing Denmark away on Sunday.
Bellamy is determined to see an improved performance when they step out in Copenhagen.
"There's more for us, so that's something we always look at as a positive," he added.
"How can we improve? How can we get better?"

vd9tsfex0wo71gk61iwv60a7d.title: Inter Miami 2-2 San Diego FC: Dreyer strikes late to deny Messi and co.
vd9tsfex0wo71gk61iwv60a7d.subtitle: Inter Miami's recent struggles continued as they played out yet another draw in MLS, losing more ground on the Eastern Conference leaders.
paragraphs: Anders Dreyer netted a late equaliser to earn San Diego FC a 2-2 draw with Inter Miami, who were held to a fourth straight stalemate despite Lionel Messi's free-kick.

Dreyer opened the scoring early on, but Miami turned the game on its head, with Messi and Luis Suarez both hitting the back of the net, only for San Diego's striker to complete his brace with eight minutes remaining at Nu Stadium.

San Diego's 12th-minute opener came out of nowhere as Jeppe Tverskov slotted a perfectly weighted throughball in behind for Dreyer, who charged in behind Miami's defense from the halfway line before dinking a lovely shot over Dayne St. Clair.
Twelve minutes later, Miami were back on level terms. Messi's free-kick looked to be more of a cross as it floated towards the far post, but it missed everyone in the middle and snuck in.

German Berterame's curler was cleared in front of the line by the retreating Ian Murphy, but San Diego could not clear their lines as Yannick Bright picked out Messi, whose first-time shot was kept out by CJ dos Santos.
Marcus Ingvartsen had a goal disallowed shortly after at the other end for an offside in the build-up, while Dos Santos punched away an awkward strike from Suarez.
But the Uruguayan soon got his goal in the 74th minute, lifting over Dos Santos from a tight angle to find the far corner.
Miami's lead only lasted eight minutes, though, with Dreyer again timing his run to perfection to meet a Tverskov pass, and a rooted St. Clair could not get a hand to it.

Messi had the chance to win it in stoppage time, bending a low shot through the crowded box, but Dos Santos got down to keep it out despite seeing it late, meaning Miami sit 11 points behind Eastern Conference leaders Nashville SC.
Messi makes more history despite Miami's frustrations
While Miami are unbeaten in their last five matches, they have drawn each of the last four, having held the lead in three of those.

But Messi has played his part in trying to get Miami back to winning ways, and netted his 101st goal for the Herons in total, while extending his lead in the Golden Boot race, as it was his 20th in MLS this season.
That means he is now just the second player in the league's history to score 20+ goals in three straight seasons, after Los Angeles FC's Denis Bouanga (2023-2025).
Messi finished the match with 10 shots – Miami had 19 overall – with five of those on target, while he also led the metrics for touches in the opposition box (14) and chances created (three).
But Dreyer ensured Messi would not end up on the winning side on Sunday, as he netted his 11th goal in MLS this term, more than any other San Diego player.
It was a vital point for San Diego, who halted a three-game losing streak and responded well to their 5-0 thumping at the hands of the Philadelphia Union.

vszo0dk89vzq15fvjgsznv68v.title: Wirtz 'the poorest I've ever seen him in a Liverpool shirt' against Bournemouth, claims Carragher
vszo0dk89vzq15fvjgsznv68v.subtitle: Florian Wirtz struggled to make an impact against Bournemouth, and Jamie Carragher has questioned his starting place going forward.
paragraphs: Jamie Carragher believes Florian Wirtz must be dropped for Liverpool's clash with Manchester City after the international break, claiming his performance against Bournemouth was the "poorest I've ever seen him in a Liverpool shirt".
Liverpool edged to a 1-0 victory over Bournemouth, giving Andoni Iraola a winning return to Vitality Stadium thanks to Alexander Isak's second-half goal.
Iraola is the first manager to remain unbeaten in his first five league games in charge of Liverpool (W2 D3) since Joe Fagan in September 1983.
However, Wirtz came under fire for his performance on the south coast as he struggled to make an impact.
He finished the match with a team-low 70.3% passing accuracy (completing 26 of 37 passes), had 53 touches, and just two off-target shots, though he did create a joint-game-high three chances.
Only Ronald Araujo (24) lost possession more often than the German (16).
And Carragher was far from impressed by Wirtz's showing, claiming that Iraola needs to think about leaving him out of the side if they want to improve their results.
"That was one of the poorest I've ever seen him in a Liverpool shirt," said Carragher on the bonus Jamie Carragher Podcast.

"I've been critical of the fact that he hasn't got the numbers. But normally when you watch Wirtz, he's neat and tidy; he keeps possession. There's things that you like. He gets out of a tight situation where you're normally expecting your player to lose the ball.
"But the reason I worry is: I don't think Wirtz is in poor form since he came to Liverpool. I actually think what we're seeing is what he is.
"And I was worried for Wirtz probably 12 months ago. And maybe that was a little bit early to say that, but I didn't say it. It was just in the back of my head.

"I commentated on Liverpool away at Burnley, and Liverpool won with a late penalty from Mo Salah. And when I was watching that game, it was what I've seen for the last 12 months: I don't see how he's going to hurt you.
"It's just neat and tidy. And in some way, the price tag for that type of player should be half of what Liverpool have paid.

"The worry for Wirtz now is that his performances so far, or what he's given Liverpool, is so low. Where we were expecting him was to take Liverpool to another league title, to take Liverpool to a Champions League.

"The gap he's got to get to almost justify what people were expecting, I almost think is too big. You can't get there. Even if he improves a bit and gets there, it's still not what Liverpool thought they were getting.

"And it's not just Wirtz, it's the knock-on effect. So when he plays at No. 10, it means Dominik Szoboszlai has to play central midfield. I don't think Szoboszlai is a central-midfield player; I don't.
"I think going forward, Iraola's got a decision to make here. Wirtz would not be in my Liverpool team.
"Wirtz wouldn't be in my Liverpool team. Manchester City at home; for me, he can't be in the team."
Wirtz has been called up in Jurgen Klopp's Germany squad for the upcoming Nations League.
Klopp – the former Liverpool manager – has named two squads, with Wirtz getting a rest before being in contention for their final two games of the international break against Serbia and Greece.
"The one hope for Liverpool supporters now is Jurgen Klopp is the Germany manager," Carragher added.

"Wirtz goes away with the Germany team for three weeks, and he's obviously one of the best players in Germany; that's how they see him. Can Jurgen Klopp sprinkle a bit of stardust on him in that position?

"Jurgen is one of the greatest managers in the world; we know that. And what he gets out of players is probably more than most managers because of the nature of his personality, and fingers crossed something can happen for him.

"There's a scenario there that Jurgen Klopp and Germany have a great international window, he gets loads of goals, assists and comes back on a high. Manchester City's the next game; he impacts that, all is forgotten, all is forgiven. There's a potential turnaround there.
"I would love that to happen. I'd love him to be the match-winner against Manchester City."
Liverpool, who sit sixth in the Premier League table on nine points after an unbeaten start, return to action on October 11 against leaders Manchester City.

wr6gl8v1zsss1qwbwzekpnd0a.title: Zirkzee replaces injured Brobbey in Netherlands' Nations League squad
wr6gl8v1zsss1qwbwzekpnd0a.subtitle: Brian Brobbey's injury against Germany has seen him withdraw from the Netherlands squad, with Joshua Zirkzee called up to replace him.
paragraphs: The Netherlands have confirmed Joshua Zirkzee will link up with Xavi's squad for their upcoming Nations League fixtures following an injury to Brian Brobbey.
Brobbey was replaced in the 35th minute by Mexx Meerdink during Thursday's 1-1 draw with Germany, an incident which led to Felix Nmecha opening the scoring.
Cody Gakpo was able to salvage a point with a stoppage-time leveller at Johan Cruijff Arena, but Xavi has been forced into making an early change to his squad.
The in-form Sunderland striker looked in visible discomfort as he left the pitch, clutching his hamstring, though the Netherlands did not disclose the severity of the injury.
It offers the chance for Zirkzee to impress new Netherlands boss Xavi, with the Manchester United forward set to make his first appearance for his nation since November 2024.
Zirkzee has accumulated six caps for the Netherlands since making his debut against Turkiye in July two years ago.
The Netherlands sit third in Group A2 following the first round of fixtures, with Greece at the top of the table following their 2-1 victory against Serbia away from home.
Serbia are the Netherlands' next opponents this Sunday, before the Oranje travel to Greece and welcome Serbia to Philips Stadion on October 4.

xk9d48m2npsc17n7ynf5ybhvf.title: 'Someone has got to make a play', says Mastroeni amid Real Salt Lake woes
xk9d48m2npsc17n7ynf5ybhvf.subtitle: Real Salt Lake still have not won in MLS since the World Cup, ahead of Sunday's clash with the high-flying New England Revolution.
paragraphs: Pablo Mastroeni feels Real Salt Lake's shortcomings have been in both boxes, saying "someone's got to make a play" if they are to end their 13-game winless streak.
RSL have not won since beating the Colorado Rapids on May 16, drawing four matches and losing nine in that stretch, with each of their last four being losses.
It is the longest single-season winless run in their MLS history, with their only longer sequence spanning being an 18-match skid between August 2005 and May 2006.
They travelled to Lumen Field to face the Seattle Sounders – who were themselves on a 13-game winless run – on Wednesday, only to lose 2-0 to goals from Danny Musovski and Albert Rusnak.

Now sitting three points adrift of the playoff picture, they host the New England Revolution on Saturday, when Mastroeni believes it will come down to the big moments, rather than his team's tactical approach.

ycibu60ctvzf1bvfu5mmnmg5r.title: The Numbers Game: Spain take record unbeaten run to Wembley as Tuchel looks to rebuild trust
ycibu60ctvzf1bvfu5mmnmg5r.subtitle: England are still dealing with the scars of their World Cup semi-final loss to Argentina, ahead of their Nations League clash with Spain.
paragraphs: Just over two months on from their heartbreaking defeat to Argentina in the World Cup semi-finals, England are back in action at Wembley Stadium on Sunday.

And their opening game in the 2026-27 Nations League pits them against the team they would have faced in the World Cup final, had Thomas Tuchel's side not retreated into their own penalty area after Anthony Gordon's goal and conceded two late goals to Argentina.

Spain travel to London off the back of their second World Cup win, having held Lionel Messi and company to zero shots through 90 minutes of the final – the first time that has ever occurred – before claiming the trophy through Ferran Torres' extra-time goal.
The top two teams in Group A3 will progress to the quarter-finals next March, but with Croatia and Czechia also lurking, the Three Lions and La Roja will have to be switched on.
Who will get off to a positive start? Here, we preview the game using Opta insights.
What's expected?
Saturday's match looks almost too close to call on paper, and the Opta supercomputer is also struggling.
Across 10,000 pre-match simulations conducted by the predictive model, England were victorious in 33.6% of scenarios.
Spain have the slight edge, with a win probability of 40.2%, with the remaining 26.2% of simulations being drawn.
Spain have won six of their last nine meetings with England across all competitions (D1 L2), most recently triumphing 2-1 in the Euro 2024 final in Berlin.
Their last away game against the Three Lions also ended in a 2-1 victory, at Wembley in the first edition of the Nations League, in September 2018.
Gareth Southgate's England did manage a memorable victory in the reverse fixture of that group, however, with a Raheem Sterling brace and a Marcus Rashford goal sealing a 3-2 triumph in Seville.
But England have only won two of their last 13 games against the reigning World Cup holders, losing nine of those matches (D2).
One of those victories was a 1-0 triumph at home to Spain in November 2011, though, with the other being a 3-2 success in Germany in March 2016.
Tuchel aims to rebuild trust after semi-final collapse
It is now 60 years of hurt for England at major tournaments, with their next shot at silverware coming on home soil at Euro 2028.
And after this year's World Cup, perhaps more than any other edition in recent history, there was a real feeling of what could have been.
England were in a commanding position when Gordon applied the finishing touch to Morgan Rogers' cross 55 minutes into their tense semi-final clash with the Albiceleste in Atlanta.
They then immediately retreated into their shells, not helped by Tuchel introducing defenders Ezri Konsa, Dan Burn and Nico O'Reilly with his first three substitutions.

Between opening the scoring and conceding an 85th-minute equaliser to Enzo Fernandez, the Three Lions had just 11.9% possession, the lowest share ever recorded by a leading team in a World Cup match over a period of at least 10 minutes (since 1966) by a team who were leading. Their leading passer in that period was centre-back Marc Guehi, with six.
Defeat felt inevitable from the moment Argentina levelled, and now Tuchel – who faced stern criticism from supporters and the media – has bridges to build.

A win over the World champions would be a fine place to start, and it should be noted that Tuchel has the best win rate of any England manager to ever lead the team for at least 10 matches, at 77% (P22 W17 D2 L3), while the Three Lions have only averaged more goals per game under Walter Winterbottom (2.8) than Tuchel (2.3).

England have also won 10 of their last 11 competitive home matches (L1), including each of their most recent five without conceding. Only once in their history have they previously won six in a row to nil, doing so between March 2015 and March 2017.
But after the meek surrender that ended their World Cup dream, fans will want to see intensity and creativity.

The withdrawals of Declan Rice and Cole Palmer – who scored against Spain in the Euro 2024 final before being overlooked by Tuchel for the World Cup – do not help matters, though Morgan Gibbs-White could now have a chance to impress. His 13 goals in the Premier League this calendar year are the joint-most of any player, alongside Erling Haaland.
Spain out to extend record-breaking run
The mood in Spain's camp could hardly be more positive coming into this fixture, having followed up their World Cup triumph by handing head coach Luis de la Fuente a six-year contract extension.
They are also defending a 38-match unbeaten run in all competitions, winning 29 games and drawing nine in that time.
It is the longest-ever streak by a European or South American nation, dating back to a 1-0 defeat to Colombia in March 2024, which took place on English soil, at West Ham's London Stadium.

La Roja's last competitive defeat, which came all the way back in March 2023, also occurred in Britain, as they lost 2-0 to Scotland in a qualifier for Euro 2024. England will hope that is a positive omen.

But this is a truly special Roja side, led by Ballon d'Or contender Lamine Yamal but also boasting plenty of other talent across the board – including World Cup Golden Ball winner Rodri and Young Player of the Tournament Pau Cubarsi.
Aided by Yamal's brilliance, Spain also reached the final of the 2024-25 Nations League, eventually going down to Portugal on penalties following a 2-2 draw in the final.

Spain's last five Nations League matches have seen them both score multiple goals and concede multiple goals, which is the longest run by any nation – in any tier – since the tournament's inception in 2018.

La Roja have reached three of the last four Nations League finals, also losing to France in 2020-21 and beating Croatia on penalties in 2022-23. Excluding spot-kicks, they have lost just one of their last 18 matches in the competition (W10 D7).
And during the last edition of the Nations League, only Cristiano Ronaldo (eight goals) outscored Mikel Oyarzabal (four).

The Real Sociedad forward has 26 goals involvements across his last 25 international appearances (19 goals, seven assists), a run that started with him scoring the winner against England in the Euro 2024 final.
England – Jude Bellingham
While England's attack is spearheaded by one of Yamal's Ballon d'Or rivals in Harry Kane, Bellingham has been the Three Lions talisman this year, netting seven goals in 10 appearances for England.
David Platt was the last midfielder to find the net more often for them in a single calendar year, back in 1993 (eight).
Barcelona have scored 31 goals in their first seven games in LaLiga this season, with only Sevilla in 1940-41 (40) ever bettering their tally at this stage.

And Yamal has been a key part of their sensational attacking start, with only team-mate Raphinha (12) bettering his seven goals in the competition and only Kylian Mbappe (41) having more shots than his 38.

yyc48whrkuhm14mv9ti4qg6wu.title: Smith says focus remains on Charlotte after recording 50th victory
yyc48whrkuhm14mv9ti4qg6wu.subtitle: Dean Smith enjoyed his 50th win in charge of Charlotte FC last weekend, and he will be hoping to add another against the Chicago Fire.
paragraphs: Dean Smith intends to continue winning at Charlotte FC after claiming his 50th victory in charge of the Crown in all competitions, last time out against D.C. United.
Smith replaced Christian Lattanzio at Charlotte in December 2023 and has gone on to manage 112 matches for the club, with their results improving year-on-year under him.
Charlotte have finished fifth and then fourth in the Eastern Conference with Smith at the helm, while they find themselves fourth in the division so far this season.
However, they have failed to go beyond the first round of the playoffs while Smith has been at the club, something they will be hoping to rectify by the end of the 2026 campaign.
Ashley Westwood and Allan Saint-Maximin were on target in Smith's 50th win with Charlotte, with their goals sealing a 2-1 victory over D.C. at Bank of America Stadium.
Charlotte meet the Chicago Fire this weekend, and while Smith was thrilled with his personal achievement, he said that his main focus remains on the team's aspirations.
"[I'm] just pleased," Smith said. "I mean, it's 50 wins in 112 games. It's a good record, but we just want to keep winning them.
"It's not about my records, it's about the club. Every win, you probably don't enjoy them as much as you should because you're always thinking about the next game.
"So, hopefully we can get to the end of the season, and I'm enjoying the win for a special reason. I think we're getting there. The building blocks have been there.
"The ideology, everybody knows what is expected of them, so I think that's the easy part. The hardest part is always recruiting good people and good players."
Chicago are just four points behind Charlotte heading into this weekend's meeting, and they will be seeking a return to winning ways following a 3-0 defeat to Nashville SC.
Sam Surridge's 33rd-minute opener was followed up by second-half strikes from Cristian Espinoza and Hany Mukhtar to seal a comfortable triumph for the Eastern leaders.

The Fire were only able to register an expected goals (xG) total of 0.91 from their nine shots, only one of which was on target, with Gregg Berhalter conceding after the match that his team were simply beaten by stronger opposition.
"I don't look at it as if the result was unfortunate for us. We just lost to a better team. It's really simple," Berhalter said.
"I think the most important lesson from this evening is that Nashville are a benchmark for us. This is a team that we want to reach and with which we want to be able to compete.
"At the beginning, we were a little too conservative. We held on, then we lost a goal. We got back into the game, but then we lost another one.
"For us, the conclusion is that as a team, we have to improve."

The Fire's task against Charlotte will be made even more difficult, with Noah Allen, Chris Brady, Anzor Mekvabishvili, Puso Dithejane, Robert Lewandowski and Robin Lod all joining up with their respective national teams for the extended international break.
Charlotte FC – Allan Saint-Maximin
Since making his debut for Charlotte, only Cavan Sullivan (30), Kristoffer Velde (25) and Guilherme (23) have completed more dribbles in the MLS than Saint-Maximin's 22.
The former Newcastle United star also has five assists and one goal for Charlotte in that time, and he will be hoping to make his mark once again for Smith's side.
Chicago Fire – Maren Haile-Selassie
Haile-Selassie has scored eight goals this season for Chicago, the most among players currently on the Fire's roster.
Five of those goals have come in road matches this season, including four goals in his last four road matches.
MATCH PREDICTION: CHARLOTTE FC WIN

Chicago earned a 2-1 win over Charlotte in the first meeting between the two teams this season back in August. It was the third straight win in the series for the Fire, after they had lost five straight in the fixture entering last season.
The Fire were shut out for just the second time this regular season in their road loss to Nashville, tied for the fewest games being held scoreless this season with Inter Miami.
That ended a 21-game run with a goal in league play, as it was the first time Chicago had failed to score since March 7, against the Columbus Crew.
Charlotte, meanwhile, have recorded their two longest regular-season unbeaten runs in club history from July onward, with a 10-game streak in 2025 and a current eight-match run.
Over the past two seasons, the Crown have averaged 2.24 points per match from July to October, compared to 1.31 in March through June.

yyjyzcfg4gz1v1lygu5o6dxf.title: Klopp not promising silverware ahead of Germany debut
yyjyzcfg4gz1v1lygu5o6dxf.subtitle: Jurgen Klopp is preparing to take charge of Germany for the first time on Thursday, though he was quick to temper expectations of his team.
paragraphs: Jurgen Klopp refused to make any promises of delivering silverware for Germany ahead of his debut against the Netherlands in the Nations League.
Klopp is preparing for his first game in charge at the Johan Cruijff Arena on Thursday after replacing Julian Nagelsmann following Germany's disappointing World Cup campaign.
Germany were knocked out in the round of 32 at the World Cup after losing on penalties to Paraguay, a defeat which led to Nagelsmann's departure after three years in charge.
The former Liverpool boss has signed a four-year deal, which will see him guide the team at the European Championship in 2028 and the World Cup two years later.
Nagelsmann had said following Germany's Euro 2024 quarter-final defeat that he was sad he ​would have to wait two years to lift the World Cup, something that did not come true.
Klopp was also asked about his remark at the ​start of his Liverpool tenure that he would probably have won a title if ​he was still in the job four years later.
"I ​don't want to promise anything," Klopp told a press conference. "What I can say ​is we will try and that's what it is about now. That's where we are at ‌the ⁠moment.
"We have had a little debate, rightly or wrongly, I think, about the impression that we have a lower quality than in other countries.
"This has become the main issue. We need to train better, train differently. But I firmly believe that it is always possible to improve training.
"This not only applies to football, but also to many other areas."
Germany have failed to go beyond the round of 32 in each of the last three editions of the World Cup, going out in the group stage in 2018 and 2022 before this summer's exit.
They last lifted silverware on the international stage in 2014, when they won the World Cup in Brazil.
